records.name: Mathoverflow1973.mathoverflow_1973
records.entry_name: A complex structure on the six-sphere
records.doc: Formalizes Levent Alpöge's construction of a complex-analytic atlas on the standard six-sphere. The development builds a compact complex threefold from torus fibrations with cusp and elliptic fibres, computes its homology and fundamental group, proves that its underlying topological space is homeomorphic to the six-sphere, and transports the complex atlas across that homeomorphism. It adapts Lean developments by Yury G. Kudryashov and Sebastian Kumar, together with the statement from the Formal Conjectures Authors.
records.informal: The formalized statement of MathOverflow question 1973: the standard six-sphere carries a complex three-dimensional manifold atlas.

records.name: PalomarHS.main_result
records.entry_name: Hard-sphere Mayer NBC identity and fork-packing volume bound
records.doc: A kernel-checked Lean formalization of the exact no-broken-circuit volume identity for hard-sphere Mayer cluster integrals and the stronger dimension-three fork-packing upper bound for each tree-owned NBC region. The development proves finite broken-circuit cancellation, the measurable finite-region decomposition, the anchored Euclidean product-measure theorem, and its explicit flat-coordinate transport.  Its geometric result is the attachment-aware estimate Vol(NBC_T) <= (17/32)^hardSphereNu T * hardSphereKappa^(k-1), where hardSphereNu T is the maximum cardinality of a packing of pairwise vertex-disjoint, order-compatible forks in T.  A formal fork is an ordered triple (a,b,c) with a < b < c, center a, leaves b,c, and tree edges {a,b} and {a,c}.  The central contribution is the complete pointwise-to-integral bridge together with the orientation-aware measure-preserving factorization that realizes the per-fork volume suppression.
records.informal: The absolute hard-sphere Mayer coefficient, multiplied by the factorial, equals the sum of nonnegative no-broken-circuit region volumes over spanning trees.

records.name: TriangleInflation.Graph.classification_NW
records.entry_name: Inflation termination for classical pair-source networks
records.doc: For finite binary pair-source networks without isolated vertices, classifies when the inflation hierarchy characterizes compatibility with finite latent alphabets: precisely forests of double stars, where order two suffices. records.name: genus_eq_zero_iff_homeo
records.entry_name: The Jacobian of a Compact Riemann Surface
records.doc: Constructs the Jacobian of a compact Riemann surface as the period-lattice quotient of the dual of holomorphic 1-forms, and proves the surrounding theory it needs: the genus as the dimension of the space of holomorphic 1-forms, discreteness and full rank 2g of the period lattice, the Abel-Jacobi map and its injectivity in positive genus, functoriality (pushforward, pullback, degree, and the projection formula), Riemann-Roch, Serre duality via Laurent tails, the residue theorem, the Dolbeault-Cech comparison, and finite dimensionality of the first cohomology by a Schwartz/Montel argument. The headline no-hack guard is that the genus vanishes exactly when the surface is homeomorphic to the sphere.
records.informal: A compact connected Riemann surface has genus zero if and only if it is homeomorphic to the 2-sphere.

records.name: JL.johnson_lindenstrauss
records.entry_name: The Johnson–Lindenstrauss Lemma and Quantized JL
records.doc: Formalizes the Johnson–Lindenstrauss lemma end to end — a Gaussian random projection preserves pairwise distances of a finite point set up to a (1 ± ε) factor, so a distortion-ε embedding of any m-point set exists once k is logarithmic in m — together with the quantized JL (QJL) one-bit sign sketch: unbiasedness of the asymmetric 1-bit estimator and its sub-Gaussian distortion bound.
records.informal: The abstract probabilistic-method union bound — if the summed per-pair distortion-failure probability is below one, a distortion-preserving map exists.

records.name: KahnKalai.covering_theorem
records.entry_name: Kahn–Kalai expectation-threshold theorem
records.doc: Formalizes Tran and Vu's short proof of the Park–Pham theorem resolving the Kahn–Kalai expectation-threshold conjecture. For an ℓ-bounded family of subsets of a finite ground set, it proves the strengthened covering theorem with the explicit constant L = 1000 and derives the threshold bound p_c(F) ≤ K q(F) log₂ ℓ with the explicit witness K = 100000. The supporting library develops finite-set cover cost, level-density, double-counting, binomial-tail, and numeric estimates.
records.informal: If ℓ ≤ N, p lies in [0, 1], and an ℓ-bounded family H has cover cost at least 1/2 - 2^(-(ℓ+2)), then its upset has at least (2/3 + 2^(-(ℓ+2))) choose(N, m) members of cardinality m, where m = floor(1000 p N log₂(ℓ+1)). For m ≤ N this is the corresponding level-density bound; for N < m both cardinalities are zero.

records.name: KasamiCyclicAdditive.carlet_kasami_cyclic_additive_literature
records.entry_name: Carlet's Kasami cyclic-additive conjecture
records.doc: Proves Carlet's cyclic-additive conjecture for the Kasami power function: over every finite field of characteristic two with cardinality 2^n and every k coprime to n, the normalized derivative image has the exact coefficient triple count 2^(2n-3) for all distinct nonzero slopes. The development combines the Müller--Cohen--Matthews permutation theorem, multiplicative character sums, Fourier inversion, and a Fermat-cubic Frobenius-kernel argument.
records.informal: For every finite field K of characteristic two with |K| = 2^n, every k coprime to n, and all distinct nonzero v₁ and v₂ in K, the coefficient triple count of the normalized Kasami derivative image is exactly 2^(2n-3).

records.name: Koethe.KotherConjecture.variants.general_matrix.disproof
records.entry_name: Disproof of the Köthe conjecture (Krempa's matrix form)
records.doc: Refutes Köthe's 1930 conjecture in Krempa's matrix form: there is a ring R (the unitization of a nil algebra of three weighted backward shifts over the algebraic closure of F_2) with a nil two-sided ideal I such that the matrix ideal M_2(I) contains a non-nilpotent matrix. The compared theorem is exactly the negation of the research-open statement `Koethe.KotherConjecture.variants.general_matrix` from Google DeepMind's Formal Conjectures, in every universe. The supporting library proves a multiprojective common-zero theorem via the Segre cone, the Nullstellensatz and Krull's height theorem, a mask-mortality theorem for one-row matrix pencils, a diagonal construction of universal mortal sequences, and a linearization theorem reducing nilness of a three-generator algebra to nilness of its root-row pencils.
records.informal: It is not the case that for every ring R, every nil two-sided ideal I of R and every finite index type n, the matrix ideal M_n(I) of M_n(R) is nil. This is the negation of Krempa's matrix form of Köthe's conjecture, stated verbatim as in Formal Conjectures.

records.name: Komlos.discrepancy_le_of_forall_sum_sq_le_one
records.entry_name: The Komlós and Beck–Fiala bounds with constant 36
records.doc: Proves that finitely many real vectors of Euclidean norm at most one admit signs whose sum has every coordinate bounded by 36, and deduces the Beck–Fiala discrepancy bound 36 times the square root of the maximum vertex degree for finite hypergraphs. The Karingula–Lovett splitting argument is supported by reusable finite-distribution, total-variation, transport, convex-hull, and matrix-discrepancy infrastructure. The near-invariant distribution uses discrete squared tent weights, and real vectors are handled by coordinatewise truncation toward zero.
records.informal: For a real matrix with arbitrary finite row and column index types, if each column has sum of squared entries at most one, its minimum signed-column discrepancy is at most 36.

records.doc: Proves that finitely many real vectors of Euclidean norm at most one admit signs whose sum has every coordinate bounded by 36, and deduces the Beck–Fiala discrepancy bound 36 times the square root of the maximum vertex degree for finite hypergraphs. The Karingula–Lovett splitting argument is supported by reusable finite-distribution, total-variation, transport, convex-hull, and matrix-discrepancy infrastructure. The near-invariant distribution uses discrete squared tent weights, and real vectors are handled by coordinatewise truncation toward zero.
records.informal: For a finitely supported probability distribution on any real module and n vectors, if translation by six times each vector has total variation distance at most one third, some signed sum added to the mean belongs to the convex hull of the distribution's support.

records.name: KrafftSieve.mu_min_lt_one_implies_tpc
records.entry_name: A Conditional Sieve Criterion for Twin Primes via Krafft Geometry
records.doc: Introduces an original conditional sieve criterion for the Twin Prime Conjecture. Using a centered modular alignment (termed the Krafft alignment), proves that if the Rayleigh-Ritz quotient over the orthogonal unit sphere satisfies muMin < 1, then a twin prime pair must exist in the corresponding interval.
records.informal: If there are infinitely many intervals where the optimal multidimensional weight achieves a ratio strictly less than 1, then there are infinitely many twin primes. This is a conditional reduction; the hypothesis muMin n < 1 is not established here for any n.

records.name: LeanPool.KrohnRhodes.krohn_rhodes_prime_decomposition
records.entry_name: Aperiodic and simple-group wreath-division towers
records.doc: Constructs a finite recursive wreath-division tower for every finite monoid in universe zero, with finite aperiodic or finite simple-group factors and every simple-group factor a monoid divisor of the original monoid. Implements a variant of the Diekert–Kufleitner–Steinberg local-divisor argument, with reusable monoid and semigroup division, local divisors, action coverings, wreath reassociation, and the Krasner–Kaloujnine group embedding. The endpoint permits arbitrary aperiodic factors and recursive intermediate bases; it does not assert the three-element flip-flop reduction, a single transformation-monoid strong division, or quantitative decomposition bounds.
records.informal: Every finite monoid M in universe zero admits a finite list of finite monoid factors, each witnessed to be aperiodic or a simple group, with DivTowerWreath M factors and every simple-group factor a monoid divisor of M. An empty tower means M divides the trivial monoid. At a nonempty step, M divides F wreath B for a finite action of a finite monoid B that itself has the tail tower.

records.entry_name: Finite-N Kuramoto Synchronization
records.doc: Formalizes the finite-N Kuramoto model of coupled phase oscillators: the order parameter and its unit bound, the potential/force gradient identities, smoothness and local Lipschitz continuity of the vector field with ODE existence and uniqueness, Lyapunov descent along trajectories, pairwise and semicircle contraction estimates, Hebbian phase/weight dynamics, and full convergence to synchrony under all-to-all coupling from initial phases in an open semicircle.

records.name: GraphCoveringTheory.KuroshStatement.kurosh_decomposition_with_inclusions
records.entry_name: Kurosh and Schreier subgroup theorems via covering graphs
records.doc: Proves the Kurosh subgroup theorem for arbitrary subgroups of indexed free products, with factors given by actual intersections with conjugates of the original factors and with the decomposition maps induced by their inclusions. The development constructs Bass–Serre trees, quotient graphs, graph-of-groups covers, path lifting, and normal forms. It also gives an explicit finite Schreier basis and classifies automorphisms of a finite regular Schreier action by its quotient group. The finite-graph basis infrastructure is reused from LeanPool.FiniteGraphFundamentalGroup.
records.informal: Every subgroup H of an arbitrary indexed free product admits a free product decomposition into a free group and subgroups of H that are intersections with conjugates of the original factors. The isomorphism to H is induced by the actual subgroup inclusions and a homomorphism from the free factor.

records.name: GenLimit.FiniteWitness.Simplified.ordinary_iff_finiteWitnesses
records.entry_name: Finite witnesses and the width hierarchy for language generation
records.doc: Characterizes generation in the limit for arbitrary families of infinite languages over any countably infinite universe by finite positive witnesses. Ordered-history generators admit a single set-driven normalization, chosen before the target language. The separation-width invariant takes every value 0, 1, 2, ..., omega, omega+1; generation is equivalent to width at most omega. Reusable infrastructure includes locking witnesses, positive separation, bounded diagonal capture over arbitrary universes, transport under equivalences, and finite-query normalization on natural numbers. The formalized scope is the semantic characterization and hierarchy, not the paper's additional density-one or Turing-computability results in Appendices D and E.
records.informal: For any family H of infinite languages over a countably infinite universe, there exists one ordered-history generator that eventually outputs an unseen target element on every exact presentation of every target in H if and only if H admits a finite positive witness assignment whose nonempty active subfamilies always have infinite common intersection.

records.informal: For a holomorphic scalar function on a convex open domain D, its Gamma-regularized Dirichlet average extends jointly holomorphically to all complex Dirichlet parameters and all node vectors in D. records.name: PalomarClarkOcone.generated_clark_ocone
records.entry_name: Malliavin calculus and the Clark–Ocone representation
records.doc: Constructs the Malliavin derivative, Gaussian integration by parts, closability, Wiener chaos, Brownian Itô integration and martingale representation. The Clark–Ocone endpoint uses a generating pre-Brownian process with continuous linear coordinates on a separable real Gaussian Banach space, its natural filtration, and pairs in the closed Malliavin graph; the conditional-expectation sections agree almost everywhere at positive times.
records.informal: For a generating pre-Brownian process on a separable real Gaussian Banach space whose coordinates are pointwise represented by continuous linear functionals, constructs a time realization of the Malliavin derivative and an Itô isometry for the natural filtration, with martingale representation for every terminal L² variable. For pairs in the closed Malliavin graph, the Clark–Ocone formula identifies the derivative's predictable projection with its conditional-expectation sections for almost every positive time.

records.name: PalomarSpectralStone.spectral_theorem_intrinsic
records.entry_name: lean-spectral-theory
records.doc: The spectral theorem for possibly unbounded self-adjoint operators on complex Hilbert spaces, formalized through the Cayley transform and real projection-valued measures. The selected spectral theorem constructs a PVM whose scalar measures give the exact finite-second-moment domain and first-moment quadratic form, with measurable-set uniqueness, and is proved equivalent to equality with the unbounded coordinate spectral integral. The selected Stone theorem proves both that strongly continuous one-parameter unitary groups have self-adjoint generators and that every self-adjoint operator generates such a group.
records.informal: Every self-adjoint partial linear operator on a complex Hilbert space has a real projection-valued measure representing its domain and scalar moments, unique on Borel sets.

records.name: LehmerE10.main_theorem
records.entry_name: Lehmer's Polynomial and the E10 Coxeter Element
records.doc: Proves that Lehmer's degree-10 polynomial — the integer polynomial of smallest known Mahler measure above 1 — is irreducible over the integers, and that it is the characteristic polynomial of a Coxeter element of the E10 Weyl group (the rank-10 instance of McMullen). Against Mathlib's Mahler-measure API it computes M(L) exactly as the Salem root with the unconditional bounds 1 < M(L) < 7/5, states Lehmer's conjecture as a defined Prop (never assumed) with the strong form implying the gap form, and contrasts the E8 Coxeter element (order exactly 30) with the E10 element (infinite order in GL(10,Z)): the E-series crosses from torsion to a Salem matrix at rank 10, and the crossing value is Lehmer's number.
records.informal: Lehmer's polynomial L(x) = x^10 + x^9 - x^7 - x^6 - x^5 - x^4 - x^3 + x + 1 is irreducible over the integers, and the characteristic polynomial of a Coxeter element of the E10 Weyl group equals L.

records.name: li_criterion
records.entry_name: Li's criterion for the Riemann Hypothesis
records.doc: Li's criterion for the Riemann zeta function, formalized in Lean 4 over Mathlib: Mathlib's `RiemannHypothesis` holds if and only if every Li-Keiper coefficient of the completed xi function has nonnegative real part. The zero-indexed analytic coefficient at n is Li's classical lambda_(n+1), the n-th Taylor coefficient at 0 of the logarithmic derivative of s |-> xi(1/(1-s)). A second compared theorem identifies this analytic coefficient with Li's arithmetic coefficient, the symmetrized sum over the nontrivial zeros counted with multiplicity, and proves that symmetrized family summable so the sum is the genuine one. Both results are unconditional: the biconditional, the coefficient identification, the genus-1 Hadamard factorization of xi (with multiplicity), genus-1 summability of 1/|rho|^2, and the growth bound order(xi) <= 1 are all proved. This is a formalization of a classically known equivalence (X.-J. Li, 1997); it is not a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis, nor of the positivity of the coefficients.
records.informal: The Riemann hypothesis is equivalent to nonnegativity of every Li–Keiper coefficient.

records.name: SimpleGraph.lineGraphColoringEquivMatchingDecomposition
records.entry_name: Line-graph colourings and matching decompositions
records.doc: Connects Mathlib line-graph colourings to palette-indexed partitions of actual graph edges into Mathlib matching subgraphs. Both conversions are inverse, preserve each matching exactly, and allow empty colours without a default colour or a finiteness assumption. An edge equivalence yields exact edge accounting: natural-number counts require only finite edges and a finite palette, while indexed cardinal counts allow arbitrary vertices, edges, and palettes. This is classical representation interoperability, not a new colouring bound or a claim of priority.
records.informal: Proper colourings of the line graph on any palette are equivalent to partitions of the original edges into matching subgraphs indexed by that palette, with empty classes permitted.

records.name: LeanPool.ListEdgeColoringComplete.exists_listEdgeColoring_complete
records.entry_name: Häggkvist–Janssen list edge colouring of complete graphs
records.doc: Proves that arbitrary lists of at least n colours on the edges of a complete graph with n vertices admit a proper list edge colouring. The proof constructs and proves uniqueness of the local rank certificate, identifies a nonzero extended-star polynomial coefficient, and applies Mathlib's combinatorial Nullstellensatz. This is an alternative proof presentation, not a literal translation of the article's argument. The conclusion uses Mathlib's actual edge type and line-graph colouring, with no certificate hypothesis and no restriction on the colour universe. This formalizes a classical theorem, not a new bound or a solution of the general list-edge conjecture.
records.informal: For every finite vertex type V, arbitrary colour type and finite list on each edge of the complete graph, if every list has cardinality at least the number of vertices, there is a proper colouring of the line graph choosing a colour from each list. This includes orders zero and one.

records.name: LongGapsBetweenPrimes.long_prime_gaps
records.entry_name: Improved long gaps between consecutive primes
records.doc: Formalizes the unconditional lower bound showing that, for all sufficiently large X, the largest gap between consecutive primes below X is at least a positive constant times log X (log log X)^2 log log log log X / (log log log X)^2. The development includes the short-translates sieve proposition, divisor coefficient estimates, truncated product weights, moment bounds, and the Erdos--Rankin covering argument used to derive the headline result.
records.informal: There are a positive constant c and a real threshold X0 such that for every X at least X0, some pair of consecutive indexed primes below X has gap greater than c times log X (log log X)^2 log log log log X / (log log log X)^2.

records.name: LongGapsBetweenPrimes.long_gap_theorem
records.entry_name: Improved long gaps between consecutive primes
records.doc: Formalizes the unconditional lower bound showing that, for all sufficiently large X, the largest gap between consecutive primes below X is at least a positive constant times log X (log log X)^2 log log log log X / (log log log X)^2. The development includes the short-translates sieve proposition, divisor coefficient estimates, truncated product weights, moment bounds, and the Erdos--Rankin covering argument used to derive the headline result.
records.informal: For all sufficiently large X, there are consecutive primes p < q with q at most X and q - p at least a fixed positive multiple of the improved long-gap scale.

records.informal: For all sufficiently large x, every sufficiently sparse subset S of an interval of length between x and x(log x)^2 has a translate b + Q(x)t + S consisting entirely of composite numbers, with 1 <= t <= exp x.

records.name: Lean4LPD.PauliString.pauliNorm_layerStep_error_le_model_of_source_regime
records.entry_name: Low-weight Pauli dynamics and truncation error
records.doc: Derives a normalized Pauli 2-norm truncation-error bound for concrete circuits of disjoint-support Hermitian Pauli rotations, with explicit locality, angle, step-count, and cutoff hypotheses. Develops a faithful matrix representation, Pauli coefficient reconstruction, finite Schur bounds, and reusable scalar multi-jump ladder estimates. Also proves a combinatorial light-cone bound and exact counterexamples showing why repeated product-formula layers must count toward the layer exponent. This is the norm-level analysis, not a formalization of expectation-value accuracy, Hamiltonian approximation, or the paper's full algorithm.
records.informal: For an observable supported on Pauli weights at most ko, a block of Γ positive-many disjoint-support layers of Hermitian rotations of weight at most kh, kh ≥ 2, and |sin θ| ≤ a ≤ αt/r with α > 0 and t ≥ 0, truncation to weight ko + m(kh - 1) after each of r blocks has Pauli 2-norm error at most (2Γ(kh - 1)αt)^(m+1) (e(m+1))^(ko/(kh-1)) times the input norm. The conditions include m ≥ 1, r ≥ 5, m ≤ r, rΓ ≥ 8(m+1)^2, and r ≥ 8e^2(ko+kh-1)αt. Γ counts every layer of the actual block, including repeated product-formula layers.

records.name: MainTheoremOfPolytopes
records.entry_name: The main theorem of polytopes

records.name: MarkovProcess.existsUnique_continuousProcess
records.entry_name: MarkovProcess
records.doc: A Lean formalization of continuous-path Markov processes associated with conservative Feller transition semigroups on nonempty locally compact Polish spaces. A uniform Kolmogorov displacement-moment bound yields a unique measurable kernel from each starting point to continuous-path space, with the prescribed finite-dimensional distributions. The library also develops strong Markov properties, generators and resolvents, stopping and killing, and Brownian motion as an example.
records.informal: A conservative Feller transition semigroup on a nonempty locally compact Polish space satisfying the Kolmogorov moment criterion determines a unique continuous-path Markov kernel with its prescribed finite-dimensional distributions.

records.name: MarshallHall.marshallHall
records.entry_name: Marshall Hall's theorem through finite cores
records.doc: Formalizes Marshall Hall's finite-index free-factor theorem for finitely generated subgroups of finite-rank free groups. The proof extracts the finitely many suffix states of a subgroup generating set, completes the resulting partial generator actions to permutations of a finite state set, identifies the connected orbit with a finite core, and extends a geodesic spanning tree to obtain an inclusion-compatible free-product decomposition. It also exposes an explicit finite permutation separator for every finitely generated subgroup and element outside it, yielding the LERF consequence. The repository also proves binary and finite-indexed free-group instances of Grushko--Neumann rank additivity, and the arbitrary-factor binary theorem. The arbitrary-factor proof is carried by a finite labelled-graph fold, source-unfold, and monochromatic-vertex contraction reduction.
records.informal: Every finitely generated subgroup of a finite-rank free group is an inclusion-compatible free factor of a finite-index subgroup.

records.name: MatchingLogic.global_completeness_entryIII
records.entry_name: Global completeness of one-sorted definedness-free matching logic
records.doc: Formalizes the one-sorted case of Chen and Roșu's global-completeness argument and independently discharges its local-completeness oracle by mechanizing the canonical-model construction from their 2019 Matching μ-Logic technical report (Theorem 73, Lemmas 80–81, and strong local completeness Theorem 83). The resulting theorem supplies both local completeness and soundness for countably infinite variable types.
records.informal: For a one-sorted finitary signature, closed premises and conclusion, and a countably infinite element-variable type, global semantic consequence is equivalent to derivability, with both soundness and local completeness discharged.

records.name: MetricCodes.Johnson.main_binary_theorem
records.entry_name: Improved asymptotic bounds for binary and spherical codes
records.doc: Formalizes asymptotic coding bounds obtained from multilevel harmonic analysis, branching rules, and spectral decompositions. The development proves a binary-code exponent strictly below the MRRW rate, constructs a strict hierarchy of spherical-code bounds, and derives the published 0.39661 asymptotic kissing-number exponent. This import incorporates substantial proof and performance optimizations by Dean Cureton.
records.informal: For every relative distance strictly between zero and one half, the combined variational upper bound on the asymptotic binary-code rate is valid and is strictly smaller than the MRRW rate.

records.name: MinModulus.nmin_eq
records.entry_name: Minimum modulus for the unique multiset-sum problem
records.doc: Formalizes the exact minimum modulus `N_min(n) = 2^n - 2^{floor(log_2 n)}` for the unique multiset-sum problem on the super-increasing residue set `{2^i - 1 : 0 <= i < n}`, and proves the sharp elementary-abelian-2-group lower bound `k >= n - 1` for unique multiset sums in `(Z/2Z)^k`.
records.informal: Proves that among moduli `N >= 2` the least one making the super-increasing residue set `{2^i - 1 : 0 <= i < n}` valid for the unique multiset-sum problem is `2^n - 2^{floor(log_2 n)}`, for every `n >= 2` (stated as `IsLeast`).

records.doc: Formalizes the exact minimum modulus `N_min(n) = 2^n - 2^{floor(log_2 n)}` for the unique multiset-sum problem on the super-increasing residue set `{2^i - 1 : 0 <= i < n}`, and proves the sharp elementary-abelian-2-group lower bound `k >= n - 1` for unique multiset sums in `(Z/2Z)^k`.
records.informal: Proves that if `g_0, ..., g_{n-1}` in `(Z/2Z)^k` have unique multiset sums, then `k >= n - 1`: an elementary abelian 2-group admitting such a family has order at least `2^(n - 1)`.

records.name: BKLOK2.lemma107K2_holds
records.entry_name: BKLO simultaneous perfect matchings and spread matchings
records.doc: Formalizes the r = 2 specialization of the simultaneous factor-selection step in BKLO Lemma 10.7: under quantitative parity, minimum-degree, codegree, and incidence hypotheses, a linearly sized, overlapping family of neighbourhood graphs admits perfect matchings whose edge sets are pairwise disjoint. The proof replaces the published randomized greedy process by a deterministic pessimistic-estimator sweep. Supporting results develop perfect, near-perfect, edge-disjoint, and quantitatively weighted spread matchings from sharp minimum-degree hypotheses.
records.informal: Specializes BKLO Lemma 10.7 to r = 2 in its apex-neighbourhood configuration: for every sufficiently large admissible configuration, all indexed neighbourhood graphs admit perfect matchings whose edge sets are pairwise disjoint. The proof is deterministic.

records.name: LeanPool.Monsky.monsky_theorem
records.entry_name: Monsky's Theorem
records.doc: Formalizes Monsky's theorem that a square can be dissected into n triangles of equal area if and only if n is nonzero and even, via a 2-adic valuation, a three-coloring of the unit square, and a rainbow-triangle argument.
records.informal: Proves that the unit square admits a dissection into n equal-area triangles if and only if n is nonzero and even.

records.name: LeanPool.MoserLatticeColorings.MoserRing.both_colorings_are_geometric
records.entry_name: Geometric Four-Colorings of the Moser Lattice and Ring
records.doc: Formalizes the two explicit parity colorings from Dúcz's 2026 note on the Moser lattice. The development derives the exact quadratic norm formula, proves that the integer-coordinate embedding is faithful, proves both colorings proper and geometric on the entire lattice, and descends them through localization by powers of three to the Moser ring. As a structural corollary, every unit-distance graph realized entirely in the Moser ring is four-colorable. The uniqueness classification of geometric four-colorings and the chromatic number of the full Euclidean plane are not claimed.
records.informal: The two parity maps defined by Dúcz descend to proper four-colorings of the full Moser ring, and equality of colors for each map depends only on Euclidean distance.

records.doc: Formalizes Baek's solution of the moving sofa problem: Gerver's sofa attains the supremum of the areas of closed connected shapes that can move continuously around a right-angled corner in a unit-width hallway. records.name: ErdosProblems.MulticolourTriangleRamsey.erdos_problem_183_explicit
records.entry_name: Superexponential lower bounds for multicolor triangle Ramsey numbers
records.doc: Resolves Erdős problem 183 by proving that the k-color triangle Ramsey number has a k-th root tending to infinity. The development constructs saturated palette families and recursive edge colorings, derives an explicit superexponential lower bound, and proves matching order-of-growth bounds for the logarithm of the Ramsey number.
records.informal: For every k at least two, the k-color triangle Ramsey number is at least ((k^(1/3))/(6 exp(38) log k))^k, and its k-th root tends to infinity.

records.name: Front.IsFront.nash_williams
records.entry_name: Nash-Williams fronts and 2-better-quasi-orders
records.doc: Formalizes Nash-Williams fronts through their well-founded prefix trees and ordinal ranks, proves the finite-color Nash-Williams theorem, and derives the infinite Ramsey theorem for arbitrary finite arity. The order-theoretic development proves that 2-better-quasi-orders are well-quasi-orders and establishes closure under finite products, lexicographic sums, domination of subsets, and pointwise embedding of sequences. Throughout, TwoBQO r is the good-triple property of an arbitrary binary relation r (every pair-sequence has m < n < l with f(m,n) related to f(n,l)); it assumes no reflexivity or transitivity of r.
records.informal: Every two-coloring of a Nash-Williams front on an infinite set has an infinite restriction whose front is monochromatic.

records.name: NashEmbeddingTheorem.nash_isometric_embedding
records.entry_name: Nash's smooth isometric embedding theorem
records.doc: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of Nash's C^∞ isometric embedding theorem for closed manifolds: every compact smooth manifold without boundary, equipped with a smooth Riemannian metric, admits a smooth injective map into some Euclidean space ℝ^q whose differential pulls the Euclidean inner product back to the given metric. The proof formalized is Günther's (1989), which replaces the Nash-Moser iteration by an elliptic fixed-point argument, following the presentation in A. J. Wassermann's Cambridge Part III lecture notes as the primary source. The development has two layers. The first proves the theorem for the flat torus: a self-contained Sobolev toolkit on 𝕋ⁿ (weighted ℓ² Sobolev spaces on ℤⁿ, Rellich compactness, the Sobolev sup bound, three multiplication theorems, mollifiers, periodization, Fourier inversion and Parseval), the approximation of smooth metrics by realizable ones, Günther's perturbation theorem proved by a contraction in Hˢ, and their assembly into the statement that every smooth 2π-periodic positive-definite matrix field on ℝⁿ is the pullback metric of a smooth periodic immersion that is injective modulo 2πℤⁿ. The second layer reduces the closed-manifold case to the torus: a Whitney embedding from Mathlib is extended to the ambient space, the metric is extended by a pseudo-inverse construction, cut off, symmetrized and periodized, and the torus theorem is applied. No bound on the embedding dimension is claimed. Concrete instances (round spheres of every dimension, products of spheres, the flat torus 𝕊¹ × 𝕊¹) are derived, and the flat-torus instance is shown to reproduce the torus theorem's conclusion, tying the two layers together. Nothing here is claimed to be new.
records.informal: Every compact smooth boundaryless manifold with a smooth Riemannian metric admits a smooth isometric embedding in some finite-dimensional Euclidean space.

records.entry_name: Finite-time breakdown for Navier–Stokes and Euler
records.doc: Formalizes forced three-dimensional Navier–Stokes breakdown on Euclidean space and the periodic torus for every positive viscosity, and finite-time singularity formation for unforced Euler from smooth, compactly supported, divergence-free initial data. records.name: NemytskiiLebesgue.IsCaratheodory.memLp_nemytskii_volume_iff_growth
records.entry_name: Nemytskii operators on Lebesgue spaces
records.doc: Develops superposition operators induced by Caratheodory functions: measurability, Lp-to-Lq growth bounds and sequential continuity, Lipschitz estimates, monotonicity and coercivity, and Frechet remainder estimates. For Lebesgue measure on the real line and finite-dimensional real fibers, characterizes when every Lp input has an Lq output by the standard integrable-envelope growth condition, for 1 <= p,q < infinity. First-order remainder estimates on arbitrary measure spaces assume a Caratheodory derivative with the stated Holder-compatible growth. The integral-functional result bounds the integrated remainder and proves integrability of the linearized integrand; it does not assert integrability of the original integrand without its separate growth hypotheses. Caratheodory here requires strongly measurable sections and almost-everywhere continuity in the fiber variable.
records.informal: For f from R times R^m to R^k with strongly measurable sections and almost-everywhere continuous fibers, and 1 <= p,q < infinity, every Lp input gives an Lq output if and only if there exist an Lq real envelope a and a nonnegative constant C such that almost everywhere, simultaneously for every fiber vector xi, norm(f(x,xi)) <= abs(a(x)) + C * norm(xi)^(p/q).

records.name: NFChoice.Foundation.NFStandard.NF_proves_not_WPP
records.entry_name: New Foundations refutes the Weak Partition Principle
records.doc: Constructs a formal first-order derivation of the negation of the Weak Partition Principle from New Foundations, with extensionality and the full integer-stratified comprehension schema. Proves full deductive equivalence with Metamath's Hailperin-derived finite presentation, including its added singleton axiom. Replays the source proof through nominal syntax, explicit freshness certificates, and a de Bruijn calculus. Includes reusable first-order soundness and completeness, stratification, lowering, and proof-translation infrastructure. This is a derivability theorem; it does not assert the consistency of New Foundations.
records.informal: Standard New Foundations formally derives the negation of WPP. WPP says that, for all sets x and y, if a function maps y onto x and an injective function maps y into x, then an injective function maps x into y.

records.name: Nivat.nivat
records.entry_name: Nivat's conjecture
records.doc: Formalizes the proof of Nivat's conjecture found by GPT-6 Pro. A configuration on the integer lattice over a finite alphabet whose number of distinct patterns on some m-by-n rectangle is at most m times n has a nonzero period. Develops rational alphabet labelings, the Laurent-polynomial shift action and its annihilator ideals, the exact line ideal of a half-plane-supported difference of orbit-closure points, complexity descent to a smaller rectangle, and Szabados's two-factor theorem for finite-range configurations.
records.informal: For every finite alphabet A and configuration c from the integer lattice to A, if for some positive m and n the number of distinct patterns of c on the m-by-n rectangle, counted over all integer translations, is at most m times n, then there is a nonzero lattice vector h with c(z + h) = c(z) for every z.

records.doc: Constructs a finitely presented group that is not sofic, resolving the question whether every group admits arbitrarily accurate finite permutation approximations. records.entry_name: Equal-area and equal-perimeter convex partitions
records.doc: Formalizes the Akopyan–Avvakumov–Karasev theorem that every planar convex body can be partitioned into any prescribed positive number of convex pieces with equal area and equal perimeter. Area is Lebesgue measure and perimeter is Hausdorff measure of the boundary.
records.informal: Every compact convex planar set with nonempty interior admits a convex partition into any positive number of pieces whose areas and perimeters are all equal.

records.name: OddPrimeValuationDistribution.oddPrimeValuationGeneratingSeries_identity
records.entry_name: Exact odd-prime distributions of central-binomial valuations
records.doc: Formalizes the exact distribution of the p-adic valuation of the central binomial coefficient binom(2n,n) over every complete block 0 <= n < p^k for every odd prime p. The development proves Kummer correctness for padded digit words, constructs the two-state doubling carry enumerator, identifies it with the arithmetic valuation polynomial, derives its second-order recurrence, proves the rational bivariate generating function, and obtains closed formulas for valuations zero and one.
records.informal: For every odd prime p = 2h+1, proves the denominator-cleared identity for the bivariate series whose coefficient of T^k X^r counts n < p^k with nu_p(binomial(2n,n)) = r; equivalently the series is (1-XT)/(1-(h+1)(1+X)T+pXT^2).

records.name: NumberField.Odlyzko.odlyzkoBound
records.entry_name: Poitou's Explicit Odlyzko Bound for Root Discriminants
records.doc: Formalizes the unconditional explicit-formula argument for a lower bound on root discriminants of totally complex number fields. Develops the completed Dedekind zeta function and its functional equation, Poitou's explicit formula, the Tartar test function, and a certified numerical estimate proving that degree at least 18 forces root discriminant at least 8.25.
records.informal: Proves that every totally complex number field of degree at least 18 has absolute discriminant at least 8.25 raised to its degree.

records.name: OrderClosures.exists_weaklyFatou_not_equivalent_fatou
records.entry_name: Order closure, order adherence and Fatou norms
records.doc: Formalizes order and unbounded-order adherence in vector lattices, the Gao-Leung characterization of order-continuous norms on sigma-order-complete Banach lattices, and the Solovay/Stone-space construction of order-complete C(K) spaces with arbitrarily large density and norm-closed separable sublattices whose only order-closed vector-sublattice extension is the whole C(K) space. Constructs solid sets with a prescribed infinite number kappa of solid generators whose adherence towers are strict below any ordinal at most kappa's successor cardinal. Constructs a complete weakly Fatou lattice norm with constant 2 that is not equivalent to any Fatou lattice norm. Includes reusable vector-lattice, net-convergence, sublattice, seminorm, Boolean-algebra and transfinite-iteration infrastructure.
records.informal: There is a real vector lattice with a complete lattice norm p satisfying the weak Fatou property with constant 2, such that no lattice norm q with the Fatou property is equivalent to p. Norms, completeness and equivalence are represented explicitly by PaperLatticeNorm, IsCompleteFor and EquivalentNorms.

records.name: SimpleGraph.isChordal_iff_nonempty_subtreeRepresentation
records.entry_name: Clique trees, subtree representations and chordal treewidth
records.doc: Develops rooted clique forests with the running-intersection property, constructs them from perfect elimination orders of finite chordal graphs, characterizes chordality by their existence, and obtains maximal-clique, separator, and counting results. Also characterizes chordality under retained-clique gluing of induced pieces, with exact vertex and edge inclusion-exclusion identities. The original library was extracted as a reusable byproduct of the published Paper IV formalization of the chordal-graph case of Erdős problem #81; this library is not by itself a proof of that paper's partition bound. Gavril's characterization supplies exact finite-tree subtree representations and the converse to chordality. Finite subtree Helly places every finite clique in a bag of any tree decomposition and gives optimal chordal treewidth. The supplied representation includes an empty connector; no minimal-host or runtime bound is claimed.
records.informal: A finite graph on a vertex type in Type is chordal if and only if it has an exact representation by nonempty connected vertex sets of a finite tree.

Also characterizes chordality under retained-clique gluing of induced pieces, with exact vertex and edge inclusion-exclusion identities. The original library was extracted as a reusable byproduct of the published Paper IV formalization of the chordal-graph case of Erdős problem #81; this library is not by itself a proof of that paper's partition bound. Gavril's characterization supplies exact finite-tree subtree representations and the converse to chordality. Finite subtree Helly places every finite clique in a bag of any tree decomposition and gives optimal chordal treewidth. The supplied representation includes an empty connector; no minimal-host or runtime bound is claimed.
records.informal: A finite nonempty chordal graph admits a tree decomposition whose width plus one is its clique number.

records.name: ParallelPostulate.Hilbert.playfair_independent_continuous
records.entry_name: Independence of Playfair's axiom via Euclidean and Klein models
records.doc: Constructs Euclidean and Klein models of a synthetic Hilbert plane, proving that Playfair's axiom is independent of incidence, Pasch order, and congruence axioms, even with Archimedes and Dedekind continuity. Develops reusable coordinate geometry over ordered fields, projective motions, Klein angles and metric, smooth-path length and distance, congruence constructions, and a coordinate curvature calculation. Dedekind continuity replaces Hilbert's maximal completeness axiom; their equivalence is not formalized. Curvature uses Brioschi's formula, and distance uses C1 paths; no identification with Mathlib's Riemannian distance or connection curvature is asserted.
records.informal: There exists a Hilbert plane satisfying Archimedes and Dedekind continuity and Playfair's axiom, and there exists another satisfying the same continuity axioms and the negation of Playfair's axiom. The models use real coordinate planes with bounds zero and minus one.

records.name: V7.main
records.entry_name: Parameter-Free Gradient Minimization in l_p Geometry
records.doc: Exact value-gradient query-complexity results for convex differentiable objectives on finite-dimensional real l_p spaces with attained minima and a positive global primal-to-dual Lipschitz-gradient bound. For finite real p > 1, the development proves strict-local scale-identification impossibility at LR/epsilon = 4 and a deterministic method family with three post-secant-initialization query-rate regimes. For p > 2 it also proves deterministic known-parameter upper and lower query exponents p/(p+2), with explicit horizon and dimension restrictions on the lower bound.
records.informal: For convex differentiable objectives with attained minima and positive global L-Lipschitz gradients from l_p to its dual, one deterministic family works for every finite real p > 1 and positive epsilon after supplied nondegenerate secant initialization with 0 < M0 <= L. It returns a queried point with dual gradient norm at most epsilon. Writing R for distance to the minimizer set, the post-initialization oracle-call bound has polynomial dependence on max(1, LR/epsilon) with exponent 1/2 for 1 < p < 2 and p = 2, and p/(p+2) for p > 2, plus additive log(e + L/M0) calibration cost. Constants depend only on p, with a universal constant at p = 2; discovering the secant pair is outside the count.

records.name: PDL.interpolation
records.entry_name: Craig interpolation and Beth definability for propositional dynamic logic
records.doc: Proves Craig interpolation for full propositional dynamic logic, including tests and Kleene star, by constructing interpolants from uniform cyclic tableaux. Interpolants use only atomic propositions and atomic programs common to the two formulas. The development also proves the local Beth definability property for a propositional letter, and supplies reusable syntax, Kripke semantics, Fischer-Ladner closure, tableau soundness and completeness, finite reachability and game-theoretic infrastructure. The results assert existence; no executable extraction algorithm or complexity bound is claimed. Human contributors and Aristotle jointly developed the formalization. The completeness modules reuse the finite game determinacy theorem already pooled in `LeanPool.Lean4GlCoalgebras` instead of duplicating it.
records.informal: If the implication from PDL formula phi to psi is valid in every Kripke model, there exists a PDL formula theta whose atomic proposition and program vocabulary is contained in the intersection of theirs, such that phi implies theta and theta implies psi in every model.

records.name: PentagonalNumberTheorem.Franklin.euler_pentagonal_number_theorem_packaged
records.entry_name: Euler's pentagonal number theorem, two independent proofs, and the Jacobi triple product
records.doc: Two independent proofs of Euler's pentagonal number theorem that share no lemmas, so each confirms the result on its own. The primary development is combinatorial: Franklin's sign-reversing involution on partitions into distinct parts, giving p_e(n) - p_o(n) = (-1)^|k| when n is the generalized pentagonal number k(3k-1)/2 and 0 otherwise, stated under a single integer index, together with the identification of that signed count with the coefficient of X^n in the truncated product over ℤ⟦X⟧. It builds on Mathlib's Nat.Partition.genFun. The second route develops q-Pochhammer symbols, the Gaussian binomial coefficient, Euler's two identities and the Cauchy identity, proves the Jacobi triple product both as a formal power series identity in (LaurentPolynomial ℂ)⟦X⟧ and analytically over ℂ for ‖q‖ < 1, and reaches the same theorem for the infinite product by specialization. The Lean proofs in both routes were largely generated by Aristotle; the Franklin route additionally has an author-written blueprint that the formalization follows lemma by lemma, and carries substantially more manual intervention and review, whereas the q-series route is machine-generated blueprint and all. The Franklin route and the analytic pentagonal number theorem overlap the pooled `pentagonal-number-theorem` development, which states its analytic form over RCLike fields rather than only over the complex numbers; the q-Pochhammer, Gaussian binomial and Euler identity definitions overlap arXiv:2607.01544. The project's distinct contribution is the complex-analytic layer: an analytic Jacobi triple product over the complex numbers for norm q < 1, its extension to the punctured disc, the analytic Cauchy identity, and the summability and locally-uniform-convergence machinery they require. Neither the pooled entry nor the non-archimedean development of arXiv:2607.01544 covers that setting.
records.informal: The primary result. For every n, either n is a generalized pentagonal number k(3k-1)/2 for some integer k, in which case the number of partitions of n into an even number of distinct parts exceeds the number with an odd number of distinct parts by exactly (-1)^|k|; or n is not of that form, in which case the two counts are equal. Proved by Franklin's sign-reversing involution.

records.name: PermanentFormulaLowerBound.permanent_rational_formula_logarithmic_lower_bound
records.entry_name: Quartic-over-logarithmic lower bound for rational permanent formulas
records.doc: Proves that every valid rational arithmetic formula over the complex numbers computing the n-by-n permanent, for n at least 32, has at least n^4 / (192 log_2 n) variable leaves. The development derives the bound through coefficient-field transcendence degree, Jacobian minors, matching-polynomial identities, and a cyclic block decomposition.
records.informal: For n at least 32, every valid rational formula over the complex numbers that computes the n-by-n permanent has at least n^4 / (192 log_2 n) variable leaves.

records.name: PermanentFormulaLowerBound.permanent_rational_formula_lower_bound
records.entry_name: Quartic-over-logarithmic lower bound for rational permanent formulas
records.doc: Proves that every valid rational arithmetic formula over the complex numbers computing the n-by-n permanent, for n at least 32, has at least n^4 / (192 log_2 n) variable leaves. The development derives the bound through coefficient-field transcendence degree, Jacobian minors, matching-polynomial identities, and a cyclic block decomposition.
records.informal: The same quartic-over-logarithmic lower bound controls variable leaves, total leaves, and vertices, and half that bound controls internal gates.

records.name: LeanPool.PoincareThreeBody.nonintegrability_of_collisionBand
records.entry_name: Poincaré's Nonintegrability Theorem for the Restricted Three-Body Problem
records.doc: Formalizes Poincaré's classical parameter-analytic nonintegrability theorem for the planar circular restricted three-body problem. The development defines the rotating-frame Hamiltonian on its collision-free domain, proves logarithmic blow-up of the resonant disturbing average at an apoapsis collision boundary, and analytically propagates the resulting dense resonant obstruction to exclude an additional analytic first integral. The final statement is the fixed-coordinate, global uniform-domain special case of the planar part of Yagasaki's Theorem 1.1; his local meromorphic resonant-orbit obstruction is Theorem 3.1.
records.informal: No jointly real-analytic family near zero mass can be an additional first integral of the planar circular restricted three-body Hamiltonian with phase differential independent from the Hamiltonian differential anywhere on the uniform collision-free domain.

records.name: LeanPolyLog.Proofs.A016
records.entry_name: Polylogarithms and sixteen log-trigonometric integral identities
records.doc: Formalizes the sixteen A-series identities from rainrzk's PolyLog Integrals tutorial, together with reusable real and complex polylogarithm series, absolute convergence on the closed unit disk, differentiation, duplication, Euler reflection and Landen identities, logarithmic moments, Fubini kernels and radial integration machinery. The formulas involve Catalan's constant, zeta(3), Li_4(1/2) and Im Li_3((1+i)/2). These are classical identities, not new informal results. A004 uses the corrected factor pi^2/24; A014 uses a proved expression entirely inside the unit disk, replacing the tutorial's invalid series expansion. A015 uses radial differentiation instead of a half-disc contour integral. The formalization was materially completed on 2026-10-01 at 00:01:57 UTC. The 2022 informal tutorial is older; the eligibility date is that of the completed Lean proofs.
records.informal: The integral from 0 to 1 of Li_3(x)/(x sqrt(1-x^2)) equals Li_4(1/2)/2 + 41 pi^4/5760 + log^4(2)/48 + pi^2 log^2(2)/6.

records.name: PuiseuxSeries.isAlgClosure
records.entry_name: Puiseux's theorem
records.doc: Constructs Puiseux series as the bounded-denominator subfield of rational-exponent Hahn series. Proves that this field is algebraic over Laurent series over any coefficient field, and is an algebraic closure when the coefficient field is algebraically closed of characteristic zero. The Newton-Puiseux proof includes reusable Hensel splitting and polynomial translation lemmas. Dean Cureton directed the AI formalization and subsequently simplified its proofs.
records.informal: For an algebraically closed field K of characteristic zero, the field of Puiseux series over K is an algebraic closure of the Laurent series field K((t)).

records.name: QECCertificates.hgp_kunneth
records.entry_name: Quantum code certificates and hypergraph-product theory
records.doc: Formalizes general binary row reduction, kernel bases and rank certificates; quantum-code distance bounds from witnesses and exhaustive low-weight enumeration; arbitrary-matrix hypergraph-product dimension and X/Z cleaning bounds; and CSS orthogonality of lifted products over finite groups. records.name: QuadraticIterates.section3_main
records.entry_name: Galois groups of quadratic polynomial iterates
records.doc: Formalizes Stoll's criterion for when the Galois group of the n-th iterate of X² + a over the rationals is the full n-fold iterated wreath product of C₂. It proves the criterion in terms of two-independence of a signed critical-orbit sequence and its pairwise-coprime Möbius factors, and derives the paper's congruence families for which maximality holds at every level. The supporting library develops reusable multiquadratic-extension, iterated wreath-product, Möbius-factor, and valuation results.
records.informal: The Galois group is the full iterated wreath product at every positive level when a is positive and congruent to 1 or 2 modulo 4, or when a is negative and divisible by 4 with -a nonsquare.

records.name: QuadraticIterates.section1_equiv

It proves the criterion in terms of two-independence of a signed critical-orbit sequence and its pairwise-coprime Möbius factors, and derives the paper's congruence families for which maximality holds at every level. The supporting library develops reusable multiquadratic-extension, iterated wreath-product, Möbius-factor, and valuation results.
records.informal: For each n, assuming -a is not a rational square, the Galois group of the n-th iterate of X² + a is the full n-fold iterated wreath product of C₂ exactly when either the first n terms of the signed sequence c₁ = -a, cₖ = fₖ(0) for k ≥ 2, or the first n integer Möbius factors of that sequence are independent modulo rational squares.

records.informal: If -a is not a rational square and none of the absolute Möbius factors from levels 2 through n is a rational square, then the n-th iterate has the full iterated-wreath-product Galois group.

records.name: RS.regts_sevenster_characterisation
records.entry_name: A proof of the Regts–Sevenster conjecture, formalized
records.doc: A Lean 4 proof of the Regts–Sevenster conjecture. A complex-valued graph parameter, normalized at the empty graph and invariant under isomorphism, has exponentially bounded edge-connection rank if and only if it is a mixed partition function. For a natural rank base R, a representing model can be chosen with k even and 2ℓ odd colours satisfying k + 2ℓ ≤ R. The development also proves the even connection-rank growth limit, minimum total colour dimension, minimal parity formulas and prescribed-dimension criterion. Schrijver's factorial argument supplies nilpotent-trace vanishing; semisimplicity and Deligne's fibre-functor theorem give the model; a polynomial commutant estimate gives the sharp colour budget. Deligne's theorem and the required symmetric-group character theory are proved within the development. The appendix's trace-zeta results give rationality and degree bounds, with an independent proof of nilpotent-trace vanishing. The theorems of record use only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound, checked by pinned audits.
records.informal: Normalized isomorphism-invariant complex graph parameters with exponentially bounded edge-connection ranks are precisely mixed partition functions.

records.entry_name: Rellich–Kondrachov compact embedding theorem
records.doc: Formalizes the Rellich–Kondrachov compact embedding theorem: the Sobolev embedding H¹ → L² is a compact operator on compact Riemannian manifolds. The proof builds the Euclidean core (compactness of the H¹ → L² inclusion on a fixed compact support via the Fréchet–Kolmogorov criterion and the H¹ translation estimate ‖τₐu − u‖₂ ≤ ‖a‖ · ‖∇u‖₂), glues chart contributions over a finite atlas, and specializes to the Levi-Civita Riemannian volume measure.
records.informal: On a compact Riemannian manifold there exists finite chart data equipped with explicit Lipschitz neighborhoods and a subordinate partition of unity, the input to the manifold Rellich glue.

records.name: FunctionField.riemann_roch
records.entry_name: Riemann–Roch for algebraic function fields
records.doc: Formalizes the Riemann–Roch theorem for algebraic function fields of one variable through the adelic route. Divisors are indexed by intrinsic places (discrete rank-one valuation subrings containing the constants), with an equivalence to a two-chart coordinate model via Ostrowski's theorem. The development builds Riemann–Roch spaces, the genus, an intrinsic adele space, Weil differentials and the canonical class, and proves Riemann's inequality, the duality theorem, Riemann–Roch, Clifford's inequality, and the standard corollaries. As an application it shows that a Weierstrass elliptic curve has genus one and identifies its degree-one places with the class group of the coordinate ring compatibly with the group law.
records.informal: For a function field K over its full constant field k, a canonical divisor W, and any divisor D indexed by intrinsic places, ℓ(D) = deg D + 1 − g + ℓ(W − D).

records.name: Sabidussi.LoopMultigraph.loop_sabidussi_compatibility_ordinary
records.entry_name: Sabidussi's compatibility conjecture for Eulerian multigraphs
records.doc: Formalizes Sabidussi's compatibility conjecture for finite labelled endpoint multigraphs with loops and parallel edges, where a loop contributes two half-edge incidences to the degree of its vertex. Given an Euler tour and minimum degree at least four, the main theorem constructs a partition of all edges into nonempty, edge-connected, 2-regular ordinary circuits such that consecutive edges of the Euler tour never lie in the same circuit. The proof runs a four-colour (F_2^2) algebra over the cyclic transition word, uses an odd balancing parity lemma to choose compatible local frames, and transports the resulting colouring back to a compatible ordinary circuit decomposition.
records.informal: For any finite endpoint multigraph with an Euler tour and minimum degree at least four, the edges partition into ordinary, nonempty, connected, 2-regular circuits that are compatible with the tour: no circuit contains two consecutive tour edges.

records.name: card_noncrossingPairing_eq_catalan
records.entry_name: Genus-Zero Pairings and Catalan Numbers
records.doc: Formalizes the finite combinatorics behind the genus-zero term of the Wigner semicircle law: a pairing of Fin (2n), viewed as a fixed-point-free involution, has genus zero (total cycle count of the rotation product maximal) exactly when it is noncrossing, and these genus-zero pairings are counted by the Catalan number Cₙ. The Catalan recurrence is obtained from an explicit equivalence decomposing a noncrossing pairing by the partner of vertex 0 into independent inside and outside pairings.
records.informal: The number of noncrossing pairings on 2n points equals the Catalan number catalan n.

records.name: Sendov.sendov
records.entry_name: Sendov's conjecture and the Phelps–Rodriguez conjecture
records.doc: Proves Sendov's conjecture in full generality: if every zero of a complex polynomial of degree at least two lies in the closed unit disk, then every zero has a critical point within distance one. Also proves the Phelps–Rodriguez strengthening, with strict inequality unless the zero lies on the unit circle and the polynomial is a scalar multiple of z^n - a^n, and recovers Rubinstein's boundary theorem. Formalizes Tao's digestion of Lech Mazur's proof: the problem is reduced to a numerical inequality in the degree and one real parameter, settled by exact rational Bernstein certificates for degrees up to one hundred and by an analytic large-degree reduction beyond. Includes the top case of Maclaurin's inequality and multiset AM–GM, a defect inequality on the closed unit disk, a sharp bound on log(sinh h / h), kernel-checked polynomial certificate infrastructure, and a packed-exponentiation bridge for exact moment integrals.
records.informal: For every natural number n at least two and every complex polynomial p of degree n all of whose roots have norm at most one, every root a of p admits a root of the derivative of p within distance at most one of a.

records.name: MassFormula.tsum_one_div_q_pow_c
records.entry_name: Serre's mass formula for totally ramified local-field extensions
records.doc: Proves both of Serre's mass formulas for totally ramified separable extensions of a nonarchimedean local field of any positive degree, together with the discriminant bound, tame-ramification criterion, finiteness dichotomy, convergence, and automorphism-weighted orbit count. The proof develops Eisenstein monogenicity, quantitative Newton-Hensel lifting, local constancy of root counts, and Haar measures of lattices over discrete valuation rings.
records.informal: For every nonarchimedean local field K with residue-field cardinality q and every positive integer n, the sum of q^(-c(L)) over the totally ramified degree-n subextensions L of a separable closure of K is n, where c(L) is the discriminant exponent minus n plus one.

records.name: allpos_has_pos_eigenvec
records.entry_name: Spectral positivity
records.doc: Perron-Frobenius theory, Jentzsch's theorem, and matrix/operator positivity in Lean 4. At the matrix level it proves that nonnegative matrices have nonnegative powers, the Metzler decomposition and positivity of the matrix exponential of a Metzler matrix, M-matrix inverse positivity, and the Perron-Frobenius theorem for irreducible nonnegative matrices (a positive dominant eigenvalue with a strictly positive eigenvector). At the operator level it proves Jentzsch's theorem for compact self-adjoint positivity-improving operators on L2 — a simple, strictly positive ground state with a spectral gap — together with a kernel positivity criterion.
records.informal: A matrix with all strictly positive entries has a positive eigenvalue with a strictly positive eigenvector (Perron-Frobenius for positive matrices, via the Collatz-Wielandt characterization).

records.name: PackingBounds.sharpFullCohnElkiesManuscriptConclusions
records.entry_name: Sharp asymptotic upper bounds for sphere packing
records.doc: Formalizes the sharp high-dimensional asymptotics of the unrestricted Cohn--Elkies linear program and bridges them to sphere-packing density. records.name: Stallings.folded_recognizer_exists
records.entry_name: Verified Stallings folding for finitely generated subgroups of F2
records.doc: Constructs a finite inverse automaton recognizing the subgroup generated by any finite list of signed words in the rank-two free group. Proves exact subgroup preservation and correctness of canonical reduced-word membership testing. Reusable infrastructure includes inverse-automaton walks, reduction-compatible traversal, finite fold congruences, coset potentials, flower graphs, and basis roses. Folding uses exhaustive finite search over Boolean relations; no complexity bound, core pruning, subgroup basis, intersection, or index algorithm is claimed.
records.informal: For every finite list S of signed words on two generators, there exist a finite type of states, a base state, and a partial transition table with inverse-labelled reverse edges, such that traversing the canonical reduced word of any g in FreeGroup (Fin 2) returns to the base exactly when g lies in the subgroup generated by the word values in S. The witness is the computed flower-graph fold.

records.name: LeanStationaryHarmonicMaps.StationaryHarmonicMap.StationaryW12LocMap
records.entry_name: Monotonicity Formula for Stationary Harmonic Maps
records.doc: Formalizes the monotonicity formula for stationary `W^{1,2}_{loc}` maps with Euclidean target. The proof is target independent: it uses only the displayed weak gradient and a vanishing domain first variation, so no target-manifold structure enters the argument. From a bundled stationary Sobolev witness `StationaryW12LocMap u Omega` it proves, for `0 < s <= r < R0`, that the normalized energy `Theta(Du, a, rho) = rho^(2-n) * integral over B(a, rho) of |Du|^2` is monotone: `weakTheta Du a s <= weakTheta Du a r`, together with the exact increment formula `weakTheta Du a r - weakTheta Du a s = weakMonotonicityRhs Du a s r`. The Sobolev layer is project-defined from Mathlib's `MemLp`, weak-derivative identities, Bochner integration, and Euclidean measure theory, following the De Giorgi-Nash-Moser engineering choice; the internal proof routes through a radial vector-field first variation, a coarea/Radon-Nikodym radius representation, smooth radial cutoffs, and an absolute-continuity boundary step.
records.informal: The public input package: a domain-variation stationary `W^{1,2}_{loc}` Sobolev map bundling a chosen weak gradient (`W12LocMapWitness`) with the vanishing domain first-variation identity. This is the object users construct to invoke the monotonicity theorem.

records.name: SimpleGraph.isThreshold_iff_nonempty_creationRepresentation
records.entry_name: Split, cograph and threshold graph structures
records.doc: Connects split partitions, cotrees and threshold creation sequences on Mathlib SimpleGraph. Proves the finite forbidden-induced-subgraph characterizations, split iff chordal and co-chordal, and completeness of cotrees and creation sequences. Supplies certificate-preserving operations, twins and nonempty union/join decompositions for cographs, maximum-clique split partitions, and induced/isomorphic transport of existing chordal elimination orders and clique trees. Classical graph theory is formalized; no new mathematical theorem, canonical certificate or recognition-time bound is claimed.
records.informal: A finite graph is threshold iff it is isomorphic to a graph constructed from the empty graph by successively adding an isolated or universal vertex.

records.name: SumDifferenceExponent.sSup_admissibleExponents
records.entry_name: The optimal exponent relating sumsets and difference sets
records.doc: For a finite integer set A with at least two elements, proves that C(A) = log(|A+A|/|A|) / log(|A-A|/|A|) is strictly below 2, while explicit finite sets have exponents tending to 2. Thus 2 is the supremum and is never attained. Also gives an explicit witness within 10^(-999) of 2. This imports the upstream base-39 row-and-column variant, not the paper's base-12 automaton construction or its quantitative cardinality estimates. Supporting infrastructure includes injective digit expansions and the strict Pluennecke-Petridis equality argument for finite integer sets.
records.informal: The supremum of the growth exponents of all finite integer sets with at least two elements equals 2.

records.name: SteinhausThreeGap.three_gap_card_le_three
records.entry_name: The Three-Gap (Steinhaus) Theorem
records.doc: Formalizes the three-gap (Steinhaus, three-distance) theorem: for every real `a` and every `N`, the `N`-point orbit `{i·a mod 1 : i < N}` partitions `[0,1)` into gaps taking at most three distinct lengths, and when exactly three occur the largest is the sum of the other two. The proof works in `[0,1)` via `Int.fract` (not `AddCircle`) through the two first-return times `η⁺` and `η⁻`, and is uniform in the rotation number, covering rational and irrational `a` with no case split.
records.informal: For every real `a` and natural `N`, the gaps of the orbit `{i·a mod 1 : i < N}` take at most three distinct lengths.

records.informal: When the gaps take exactly three distinct lengths, those lengths are precisely the two first returns `η⁺`, `η⁻`, and their sum `η⁺ + η⁻`; in particular the largest gap is the sum of the other two.

records.name: TutteFormalization.path_theorem
records.entry_name: Tutte’s path theorem for matroids
records.doc: Proves the modular-cut path theorem for finite matroids, with reusable rank-partition, hyperplane-separation, relative-complement, indecomposable-cover, and diamond constructions.
records.informal: In a finite connected matroid, any two hyperplanes containing a proper indecomposable flat and lying outside a modular cut are joined by a finite Tutte path all of whose vertices contain that flat and avoid the cut. Consecutive vertices are distinct hyperplanes with indecomposable corank-two intersection; repeated nonconsecutive vertices are permitted.

records.name: UlmsTheorem.ulm_theorem
records.entry_name: Ulm's theorem for countable reduced abelian p-groups
records.doc: Formalizes Ulm's classification theorem for countable reduced abelian p-groups in arbitrary Lean universes. The development constructs the transfinite Ulm filtration and invariants, proves their invariance under additive equivalence, establishes Kaplansky's one-generator extension lemma, and completes the countable back-and-forth classification. A finite-group regression distinguishes Z/4 x Z/4 from Z/2 x Z/8 at the zeroth Ulm invariant.
records.informal: For any prime p and any two countable reduced abelian p-groups in the same arbitrary Lean universe, the groups are additively isomorphic if and only if all of their classical Ulm invariants, indexed by universe-zero ordinals, agree.

records.name: LeanPool.Vizing.exists_equitable_edge_colouring
records.entry_name: Vizing's theorem and equitable edge colourings
records.doc: Proves the maximum-degree-plus-one edge-colouring bound for finite simple graphs by fans and Kempe exchanges. A separate component-swapping argument equitably rebalances any finite proper edge colouring on its original palette. Together they give equitable proper edge colourings on any palette of at least maximum degree plus one colours, with every class bounded by the ceiling of the average class size. Extracted from the published Paper IV formalization; these are classical colouring results, not a claim to new mathematics or to the paper's clique-partition bound.
records.informal: For every finite simple graph G and natural c at least maximum degree of G plus one, there is an equitable proper edge colouring with c colours; each colour class has at most ceiling(|E(G)|/c) edges.

records.name: WhiteheadTheorem
records.entry_name: Whitehead's theorem for CW-complexes
records.doc: Formalizes Whitehead's theorem — a continuous map between CW-complexes that induces isomorphisms on all homotopy groups is a homotopy equivalence — including the supporting theory of CW-complexes, relative homotopy groups, the homotopy extension property, and compression of maps.

records.name: Zeta5Irrational.irrational_five
records.entry_name: Irrationality of the Riemann zeta function at five
records.doc: Proves that Mathlib's Riemann zeta function at five is an irrational real number, following Aabir Fauzan's September 2026 preprint. Constructs integer polynomials of degree 37n with positive values at zeta(5) that decay exponentially in n squared. Includes a general integer-polynomial irrationality criterion, Hankel determinant and moment-integral identities, logarithmic-energy estimates, prime-adic integrality bounds, and kernel-checked rational certificates. The formalization uses a different normalizer and a positive decay constant in place of the paper's specific constant 139/5. Reuses the prime number theorem infrastructure already in the MooreBound project.
records.informal: There exists an irrational real number x whose complex coercion equals Mathlib's Riemann zeta function evaluated at five.

records.name: ZetaZeros.simple_proportion_d4
records.entry_name: Simple zeros of the Riemann zeta function
records.doc: Formalizes Lamzouri's Hilbert-space proof of lower bounds for simple and distinct zeros of the Riemann zeta function. From explicit Riemann--von Mangoldt and unconditional pair-correlation hypotheses, the development proves that eventually more than 67.25% of nontrivial zeros are simple and on the critical line and more than 83.625% are distinct. It includes the finite-multiset Hilbert-space inequality, zeta-zero multiplicity symmetries, an admissible cutoff construction, and certified trigonometric estimates.
records.informal: Assuming the stated Riemann--von Mangoldt and unconditional pair-correlation formulas, beyond some height more than 67.25% of nontrivial zeta zeros are simple and lie on the critical line.

records.name: ComparatorClaims.schurMod_integerClosedForm
records.entry_name: Modular Schur numbers: S_m(k,ℓ) = n − 1 for k ≥ n − 1, where n = m/gcd(m,ℓ−1)
records.doc: A Lean 4 formalization, with Mathlib, of the main results of the paper "Prime-power structure of the stable regime for modular Schur numbers" (docs/paper/modular-schur.pdf in this repository). The modular Schur number S_m(k,ℓ), introduced by Chappelon, Revuelta Marchena and Sanz Domínguez (2013), is the largest N such that 1, …, N can be coloured with k colours so that no colour class contains a solution of x_1 + ⋯ + x_ℓ ≡ y (mod m). For m ≥ 2 and ℓ ≥ 2, put n = m/gcd(m,ℓ−1). The main theorem is the closed form S_m(k,ℓ) = n − 1 for every k ≥ n − 1. D'orville, Sim, Wong and Ho (Integers 25 (2025) #A62) gave it when gcd(m,ℓ−1) = 1 (their Corollary 5). The general case is a short corollary of the singleton criterion and their Corollary 3; to the author's knowledge it is first stated in the paper. The proof turns on one value: ℓ copies of n sum to n modulo m, so the class {n} alone breaks the rule, while each of 1, …, n − 1 is safe in a class of its own. The formalization also proves the one-colour closed form S_m(1,ℓ) = min(ℓ − 1, ⌊m/ℓ⌋) for 2 ≤ ℓ ≤ m, which answers Problem 1.3 of D'orville et al.; the bound S_m(k,ℓ) ≤ m − 1 of Chappelon et al.; and the reduction from integers to residues modulo m. Twelve theorems with Mathlib-only statements are compared by lake comparator (statement identity, permitted axioms, and replay through the Lean, nanoda and con-ron kernels); their only axioms are propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. The 33 project modules also contain further results, listed in LEAN_STATUS.md, that are proved and axiom-audited but are not compared, among them the bound m/p, with p the least prime factor of m, on the size of a set of residues whose pairwise differences all lie in a proper subgroup of ℤ/m. An earlier computational part of the project, which uses native_decide, is not in this repository and is not part of these results. The informal proofs, the Lean formalization and the paper were produced with AI systems (Claude, Aristotle and GPT-5) under the direction of the author.

records.name: Challenge.generalizedMarkoff_reduction_surjective_of_large_prime
records.entry_name: Generalized Markoff strong approximation
records.doc: A Lean 4 formalization of the generic branch of eventual strong approximation for generalized Markoff surfaces, specialized to a fixed ordered integral coefficient triple. It proves punctured transitivity for both the full Vieta group and the two-Vieta rotation group, supplies an explicit coefficient-dependent cutoff, and derives surjectivity of coordinatewise reduction onto the full finite-field surface.

records.name: Stafford38Challenge.universalStatement
records.entry_name: Stafford 3.8
records.doc: Lean formalization of Stafford's Conjecture 3.8 for every characteristic-zero field and every Weyl-algebra rank, proving that each nonzero d admits F, R, and S with 1 = d*R + F*d*S. The development also proves an exact Bernstein-degree fixed-source strengthening and derived localization, adjoint, and evolutionary results.

records.name: MohP3.Palomar.global_setTheoretic_completeIntersection
records.entry_name: Moh's P3 curve is a set-theoretic complete intersection
records.doc: A Lean 4 formalization proving that the Moh curve parametrized by x=t^6+t^31, y=t^8, z=t^10 is cut out set-theoretically by two explicit equations over every characteristic-zero field. The development computes the polynomial and formal-power-series parametrization kernels, proves the radical equality for the two-generated witness ideal, and proves that the curve ideal has height two and arithmetic rank two, both globally and after completion. It also verifies the exact Hilbert-Burch presentation given by the manuscript's explicit four-by-three matrix.
