records.name: SarkozySubmission.interval_moment_bound
records.entry_name: An interval-moment criterion for square-difference-free integer sets
records.doc: We prove a general interval-moment criterion for square-difference-free integer sets and apply it to obtain an improved unconditional lower bound in Sarkozy's theorem, with exponent 0.7580758318008816. If D(N) is the largest size of a subset of {1, ..., N} containing no two distinct elements whose difference is a square, then for every epsilon > 0 and all sufficiently large N we prove D(N) >= N^(0.7580758318008816 - epsilon). The exact exponent is 473797394875551/625000000000000. The reusable criterion starts from finite digit sets in pairwise coprime square bases, with ordered intervals and width-moment inequalities. A strict surplus in the component exponents yields the asymptotic bound through finite stopping words, rank rounding, the Chinese remainder theorem, and interpolation between geometric scales. Both the general criterion and its numerical application are formalized in Lean. All nine concrete components are proved: six prime chains, a 25-state binary recursion, and two complete composite witnesses, at the primes 5 and 43 (three restricted digits at each) and at 19 and 23 (three at 19, two at 23). Every required ordering, numerical moment, lifting, and asymptotic argument is checked, with no remaining finite-certificate hypotheses. This version replaces the exponent 0.75806746 of version 1 with new finite witnesses and more precise certificates. The repository includes self-contained PDF and LaTeX write-ups of the full result and a simpler companion construction attaining exponent 0.758001 that explains several core ideas, together with exact computational certificate programs. The simpler construction is not separately formalized or a selected submission statement.

records.name: BoundedWanderingDomains.wandering_domain_has_locally_uniform_escaping_subsequence
records.entry_name: Absence of bounded-orbit wandering domains
records.doc:
We formalise the proof of two major recent results on wandering domains of transcendental entire and meromorphic functions: every orbit in a wandering domain accumulates at infinity and at a non-isolated (derived) point of the spherical set of singular values.
Both results are obtained as a special case of a more general theorem, for locally defined functions on possibly disconnected complex one-manifolds. Let f be an open holomorphic function from an open subset O of such a manifold X into X. Different components of O may map to different components of X, even when those source components lie in the same ambient component. Suppose that U is a wandering component of the set of normality of f, and that z is in U. If the orbit of z is contained in a compact subset of X, then it accumulates at a non-isolated point s of the set of singular values. Moreover, this accumulation must occur close to singularities for infinitely many singular values. That is, there exists a sequence (s_n) of distinct singular values converging to s, a sequence of embedded discs D_n containing s and a sequence U_n of components of f^{-1}(D_n), with the following properties. (We say that the orbit of z has "singular encounters"; see HasSingularEncounterSequence in the formalisation.) * the discs D_n shrink to s; that is, every neighbourhood of s contains D_n for sufficiently large n; * each component U_n contains a point of the orbit of z; * s_n is a singular value of the restriction f:U_n\to D_n. In particular, the orbit of z is not contained in any compact subset of O. In the special case of a transcendental entire or meromorphic function, we can take X to be the Riemann sphere, and hence compact, so that the hypotheses are satisfied for any wandering Fatou component.
We also prove a corresponding theorem for measurable wandering subsets of the complement of the domain of normality on which all iterates are defined and injective; here the conclusion is that almost every point of the set (in any chart) behaves as above: ambient escape along a subsequence, or singular encounters.
As corollaries we recover Epstein's absence of wandering domains for finite-type maps on arbitrary open subsets of compact, possibly disconnected complex one-manifolds, and the classical no-wandering results for rational maps, compact-surface self-maps, and class S entire and meromorphic functions.
This is an update from the previous registered submission on Palomar, https://palomar-registry.org/entry.html?id=PALOMAR-2026-09-25-000001&version=3 . The change in this update is to allow functions in the local result to take values in a possibly disconnected complex 1-manifold, rather than a Riemann surface. This aligns the definition with Epstein's original discussion of finite-type analytic maps, which likewise allow (compact) complex 1-manifolds.

records.entry_name: Absence of bounded-orbit wandering domains
records.doc:
We formalise the proof of two major recent results on wandering domains of transcendental entire and meromorphic functions: every orbit in a wandering domain accumulates at infinity and at a non-isolated (derived) point of the spherical set of singular values.
Both results are obtained as a special case of a more general theorem, for locally defined functions on possibly disconnected complex one-manifolds. Let f be an open holomorphic function from an open subset O of such a manifold X into X. Different components of O may map to different components of X, even when those source components lie in the same ambient component. Suppose that U is a wandering component of the set of normality of f, and that z is in U. If the orbit of z is contained in a compact subset of X, then it accumulates at a non-isolated point s of the set of singular values. Moreover, this accumulation must occur close to singularities for infinitely many singular values. That is, there exists a sequence (s_n) of distinct singular values converging to s, a sequence of embedded discs D_n containing s and a sequence U_n of components of f^{-1}(D_n), with the following properties. records.entry_name: The quasi-isometry classes of Galton–Watson trees: Lean formalisation
records.doc: Lean 4 formalisation of the automorphism-matching theorems and the quasi-isometry classification of Galton–Watson trees from the paper "The quasi-isometry classes of Galton–Watson trees" by Jayadev S. Athreya and Sascha Troscheit (arXiv:2609.23882). The audited statements are: the i.i.d. matching theorem on the binary tree (Theorem 5.1), the general Markov matching theorem for typed label processes on the binary tree, in its finite-type and zero-compatible forms (Theorem 6.1), the complete classification, up to quasi-isometry, of Galton–Watson trees with finitely supported offspring law conditioned on infinite diameter (Theorem 1.2), the mutual embeddability theorem (Theorem 1.3), and two-value universality with its quantitative rate (Theorem 1.4). The statements are made in Challenge.lean over Mathlib alone and discharged by Solution.lean from four library targets.

records.name: Zeta2.Pair.zeta2_7_9_not_both_rational_palomar
records.entry_name: At least one of the 2-adic zeta values ζ₂(7), ζ₂(9) is irrational
records.doc: A Lean 4 and Mathlib proof that at least one of the 2-adic zeta values ζ₂(7), ζ₂(9) is irrational. The theorem has no hypotheses, and its proof uses only the axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. The values are defined through the Volkenborn integral: zeta2 s = J(s−1)/((s−1)·2^s), where J(s) is the 2-adic limit of the Riemann sums 2^(−N) Σ_{x<2^N} (x+1/2)^(−s), and the theorem also proves that these limits exist. By Lemma 2.8 of Lai, Sprang and Zudilin (IMRN 2026), zeta2 s is the Kubota–Leopoldt value ζ₂(s) = L₂(s, ω^(1−s)) for s ≥ 2. That identification is cited, not formalised; it only involves a non-zero rational factor, which does not affect irrationality. The result sharpens Theorem 1.1 (case s = 3) of L. Lai (Int. J. Number Theory 2025), which shows that at least one of ζ₂(7), ζ₂(9), ζ₂(11), ζ₂(13) is irrational, and it implies the companion result, formalised in a separate repository, that at least one of ζ₂(7), ζ₂(9), ζ₂(11) is irrational. The proof uses linear forms S_n = ∫ R_n'''(t+1/2) dt in 1, ζ₂(7), ζ₂(9) built from the shifted well-poised rational functions R_n(t) = (2t+n) Π_{m=1}^{6} (t+1/2−h_m)_(n+2h_m) / (t)_(n+1)^6 with h = (n/40)(−17, 1, 2, 3, 5, 6). The 2-adic size of S_n comes from Lai's and Sprang's Δ-calculus. The size of the coefficients comes from a contour-integral representation and a saddle-point bound, whose numerical inequalities are certified in Lean. The odd part of the denominators is bounded by Legendre-type counts at the poles, the vanishing of R_n at half-integers, kernel-checked certificates and the prime number theorem (proved here from a vendored Lean proof of the Wiener–Ikehara theorem). If both values were rational, the valuations of the coefficients at the prime n − 1 (an idea of Lai and Sprang) would make S_n non-zero for infinitely many n, and Lai's irrationality criterion gives the contradiction. The mathematics and the Lean code were produced by AI agents under human direction and have not been refereed.

records.name: MAFComposition.reactionEdit
records.entry_name: MAF composition criteria, exact enumeration of child-selection autocatalytic cores, and degradation regions of linear diluted source networks
records.doc: We establish three sets of results addressing published questions about the composition, enumeration and degradation of autocatalytic reaction networks. In response to the composition questions of Gagrani, Wang, De Decker and Lacoste (arXiv:2603.02627, Discussion and outlook), we give exact criteria for strict increases in the maximum amplification factor (MAF) under reaction addition, nonnegative species aggregation and shared-species coupling, assuming nonnegative inputs and attained MAFs. A block direct sum attains the larger component MAF, while an explicit example shows that component MAFs alone do not determine the MAF of a coupled network. Addressing the CS-core enumeration direction of Golnik, Gatter, Stadler and Vassena (arXiv:2603.02770, Section 6), we prove exact reconstruction from a complete list of ordinary-core anchor matchings, each unique on its vertex set, by alternating-path generation and certified rational semipositivity filtering. We establish existence of the certified test, its rejection of the empty matching, and an explicit nonempty instance for A → 2A. For the arbitrary-degradation question discussed by Nandan, Nghe and Unterberger (arXiv:2507.15546, Section 6), we characterize growth, criticality and extinction for irreducible linear diluted source networks with nonnegative unary reaction data and species degradation d ≥ 0: the real spectral bound of A − diag(d) is positive, zero or negative exactly when d is componentwise strictly below, equal to or strictly above (Av)_i/v_i for some positive v. We also characterize partial-actuation stabilizability of Metzler matrices through a positive-vector certificate on the unactuated block. records.name: erdos1220_not_provable
records.entry_name: Erdős Problem #1220 in Lean 4: the affirmative statement is not provable in ZFC
records.doc: Erdős problem #1220 (erdosproblems.com/1220; Erdős–Hajnal 1971): let λ be a singular cardinal such that both λ and cf(λ) are ℵ₀-inaccessible (μ^ℵ₀ < κ for all μ < κ); does λ → (λ, ℵ₁)² hold?  This formalization settles the question as asked on erdosproblems.com in the negative sense "not provable": ZFC does not prove that every such λ satisfies λ → (λ, ℵ₁)² (erdos1220_not_provable : ¬ (ZFC ⊨ᵇ Erdos1220)), i.e. there is a model of ZFC with a singular λ, λ and cf(λ) ℵ₀-inaccessible, and λ ↛ (λ, ℵ₁)².  Shelah and Stanley (Sh:258, Ann. Pure Appl. Logic 36 (1987)) showed that a negative answer is consistent with ZFC.  This project formalizes that consistency result: the comparator target erdos1220_not_provable : ¬ (ZFC ⊨ᵇ Erdos1220) is stated for literally the same first-order theory ZFC, language and ZFSet interpretation as elliotglazer/erdos501's comparator challenge (imported from its statement module Erdos501.FOL.Statement), together with a faithfulness theorem erdos1220_sentence_faithful: in Mathlib's ZFSet the sentence Erdos1220 holds iff the Mathlib-level statement Erdos1220.Problem1220 holds.  The witness is the ground-model singular strong-limit cardinal λ = ℶ_{𝔠⁺} (cf λ = 𝔠⁺; λ and cf λ are ℵ₀-inaccessible without any deep cardinal-arithmetic input), not ℵ_{𝔠⁺}.  The forcing is the Shelah–Stanley §3 forcing, formalized as block-preserving, block-covering histories of basic conditions (weak extension order), with the μ⁺-strategic closure (hence μ-distributivity) and the (2^μ)⁺-chain condition proved in ZFC without GCH (Δ-system lemma for (2^μ)⁺ sets of size ≤ μ, blueprint counting (2^μ)^μ = 2^μ).  In the Boolean-valued model of its regular-open algebra (built with the Lean 4 port of Han–van Doorn's Flypitch vendored by erdos501) the hypotheses on λ are preserved, the generic colouring of [λ]² has neither a red homogeneous set of size λ nor a blue homogeneous set of size ℵ₁, and Flypitch's completeness theorem turns this into a two-valued model of ZFC satisfying ¬Erdos1220.  Both targets are proved from propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound only and pass the Lean comparator.  Only the negative direction is claimed: independence (consistency of a positive answer) is NOT claimed.

records.name: MS.Palomar.myersonSatterthwaite
records.entry_name: Myerson-Satterthwaite impossibility theorem (continuous bilateral-trade version)
records.doc: Formalizes the continuous-type bilateral-trade impossibility result: no mechanism can satisfy ex post efficiency (almost surely), Bayesian incentive compatibility, interim individual rationality, and weak ex ante budget balance when buyer and seller supports overlap. The proof uses payoff equivalence and envelope identities, together with the strict rent-gap identity B + C > S.

records.name: Lovasz.hamiltonian_of_polylog_degree
records.entry_name: Hamilton cycles in Cayley graphs of polylogarithmic degree
records.doc: A complete Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the following theorem: there are absolute constants C, n0 > 0 such that every connected Cayley graph Cay(G, S) on n >= n0 vertices whose degree d = |S| is at least C (log n)^13 / log log n contains a Hamilton cycle (Lovasz.hamiltonian_of_polylog_degree). Here G is a finite group, S is a connection set (S = S^-1 and 1 not in S, so the graph is |S|-regular), log is the natural logarithm, and connectivity is equivalent to S generating G. The theorem is a case of the Lovász conjecture (every connected vertex-transitive graph has a Hamilton path) in its Cayley-graph form (every connected Cayley graph on at least three vertices is Hamiltonian). For arbitrary connected Cayley graphs the previously published degree thresholds were linear degree (Christofides, Hladký and Máthé, 2014) and degree at least n^(1-c) (Bedert, Draganić, Müyesser and Pavez-Signé, 2026). The proof follows the source manuscript: it extracts a connected bipartite template with spectral gap of order (log n)^-2, allocates the vertices to weighted translates of the template by signed rounding (a robust signed integrality theorem derived from the capacitated b-matching polytope, swap rounding, and a trace-exponential matrix concentration bound), connects the pieces by a sparse matching chosen by mutual nominations and a signed circulation, absorbs the outside matching inside every piece with Hamilton routers built from even-cycle comparators, and merges cycles. Every lemma of the manuscript is proved in the repository, as are the classical results it uses without proof (normalized Cheeger inequality, Haxell's hypergraph matching theorem, the b-matching polytope, Watkins's connectivity bound, the Nash-Williams–Tutte tree-packing theorem, Hoffman's circulation criterion, scalar Chernoff bounds); Hall's theorem is taken from Mathlib, and matrix Bernstein is avoided by deriving the one lemma that used it from the manuscript's own concentration bound. The source manuscript is an unpublished research draft that describes its own proof as not independently verified; this formalization is, to the maintainer's knowledge, the first verification of the theorem. The proved theorem has no sorry and depends only on propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.

records.name: T3.exists_bounded_nonamalgamation_witness
records.entry_name: Existence of a Model Companion for Groups of Exponent 3: Lean Formalization
records.doc: This project formalizes the existence of a model companion for the first-order theory of groups satisfying x^3 = 1. Its principal group-theoretic result gives a uniform, explicit bound on the number of generators needed to witness a failure of amalgamation with an existentially closed exponent-three group. The development follows the accompanying manuscript through free groups, associated graded Lie algebras, strict extensions, and the bounded-amalgamation criterion.

records.name: AllCenterMAP.map_two_fifteenths
records.entry_name: Uniform Minor-Arc Cancellation for Primes at the X^{2/15+ε} Scale
records.doc: We prove uniform cancellation in prime-weighted exponential sums at the 2/15 scale, improving the 8/33 local Fourier scale in the Matomäki–Radziwiłł–Tao machinery for averaged prime-pair correlations. On the minor-arc part of every centered arc of radius 1/(2H), the squared von Mangoldt exponential sum over X < n <= 2X has integral at most C X (log X)^(-A), for every A > 0 and epsilon > 0, once H >= X^(2/15+epsilon) and X is large enough. The center may lie anywhere on the circle. The same cutoffs and constants work for every center and are chosen before X and H. This gives uniform minor-arc cancellation at the 2/15 threshold. Since 2/15 < 8/33, the admissible H is smaller, so the frequency windows of length 1/H are wider and the shift-averaging intervals are shorter. The constants C and X0 are ineffective because the proof uses Siegel's theorem. The development also contains an internal proof of the epsilon-form of Guth–Maynard's large-value estimate for Dirichlet polynomials. The recorded 20 September Lean 4.30 kernel replays checked 100,596 declarations for MAP and 75,874 for Guth–Maynard, using only standard axioms. The formal statement is AllCenterMAP.map_two_fifteenths, manuscript Theorem 1.1.

records.doc: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the whole of P. Corvaja and U. Zannier, On the rational approximations to the powers of an algebraic number: solution of two problems of Mahler and Mendès France (Acta Math. 193 (2004)), built on the repository's libraries ArithmeticHeights and DiophantineApproximation, whose Subspace Theorem it uses. The library CorvajaZannier2004 is sorry-free and within Lean's three standard axioms. It proves the Main Theorem (finitely many non-pseudo-Pisot δqu that are very close to integers, u in a finitely generated group of algebraic numbers), Theorem 1 (Mahler's question: if ‖αⁿ‖ < lⁿ infinitely often, some power of α is a Pisot number), Lemmas 1–5, Theorem 2 (Mendès France's question: the period of the continued fraction of αⁿ tends to infinity unless α is a unit or a square root of a rational, and is bounded for units), and the Appendix (the word "algebraic" cannot be dropped from Theorem 1). Eleven statements are compared.

records.name: RAF.Frankl.elementary_core_exists_abundant
records.entry_name: Equivalence of the RAF abundance conjecture and Frankl's union-closed sets conjecture
records.doc: In a catalytic reaction system with finitely many reactions, a RAF is a nonempty set of reactions whose reactants are produced from the food set by iterated closure under the selected reactions and whose reactions are each catalysed by a molecule of that closure. Steel (arXiv:2305.16714v4, Section 4) asked whether some reaction always lies in at least half of the RAFs. Call a reaction food-ready if all its reactants are food, and abundant if it lies in at least half of the sets in the family formed by the RAFs and the empty set. If some RAF U consists entirely of food-ready reactions, then some reaction of U is abundant, with no condition on the other reactions. If every reaction of the system, except at most two, is food-ready and the system has a RAF, then some reaction is abundant. Finally, the statement that every catalytic reaction system with finitely many reactions and a RAF has an abundant reaction is equivalent to Frankl's union-closed sets conjecture in the form: every finite union-closed family containing the empty set and a nonempty set has an element lying in at least half of its members.

records.name: PetersenZeroForcing.zero_forcing_number_eq_eight
records.entry_name: Zero forcing number of the generalized Petersen graphs P(n,3)
records.doc: A Lean 4 proof that the zero-forcing number of the generalized Petersen graph P(n,3) is exactly 8 for every natural number n >= 13. The formalized result is the statement recorded as Conjecture 5 in Arnav Krishnan's July 2026 correction preprint; this repository supplies and kernel-checks a proof of that conjectured statement rather than formalizing a proof already given in the cited preprint.

records.name: FourColor.RealPlane.four_color
records.entry_name: The Four Color Theorem (Lean 4 port of Gonthier's Coq proof)
records.doc:
A Lean 4 and Mathlib formalization of the Four Color Theorem, ported from Georges Gonthier's Coq proof by Claude Opus 5.5, Anthropic's AI model, working as an agent under the direction of Robert D. Barish. The main theorem, FourColor.RealPlane.four_color, states that every simple map of the real plane can be colored with at most four colors so that adjacent regions get different colors. The map may have infinitely many regions, bounded or not; each region must be open and connected, and two regions are adjacent when their closures share a point that lies in the closure of no third region. As in Coq, a compactness argument reduces the theorem to finite maps, which are turned into planar bridgeless hypermaps. A smallest hypermap that cannot be four-colored cannot exist: discharging shows that it would contain one of the 633 configurations of Robertson, Sanders, Seymour and Thomas, and each of these is reducible.
The port differs from the Coq proof in three main ways. Its statement uses Mathlib's real numbers rather than an arbitrary model of Coq's axiomatized reals; the two are equivalent, because all such models are isomorphic and the definitions use only the order. Coq checks that the 633 configurations are reducible with a procedure on trees of colorings, run by its virtual machine. The port replaces it with a new bit-parallel engine whose certificates, generated during the build, are checked by the Lean kernel itself. Finally, the case analysis of the unavoidability proof, written as tactic scripts in Coq, becomes case trees checked by a checker proved correct once. Every computation is carried out by the Lean kernel, without native_decide, and the proof uses only the axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.

records.name: PeterfalviProblem.not_hypothesisB_three
records.entry_name: Péterfalvi's Problem for p = 3: No Group Satisfies Hypothesis (B)
records.doc: Glauberman and Norton (Proc. Amer. Math. Soc. 119, 1993) end their paper on a combinatorial problem that arises in the proof of the Feit–Thompson odd order theorem with a question of Péterfalvi: can the hypothesis of their Proposition 9 be satisfied for p = 3? The same question is Problem 1 in Appendix C of Bender and Glauberman, Local Analysis for the Odd Order Theorem (1994). Let F be the field with p^q elements, P its additive group, U its group of units of norm one over the prime field, H the semidirect product P ⋊ U, and P₀ the image of the additive group of the prime field in H. Hypothesis (B) asks for an injective homomorphism σ from H into a group G, a finite abelian subgroup Q of G whose order is prime to p, and an element y of Q, such that σ(P₀) normalizes Q and σ(P₀)^y normalizes σ(U). Proposition 9 also assumes condition (A): q does not divide p − 1. This project proves in Lean 4 that the answer is negative: for every prime q with q ∤ 3 − 1, no group G, finite or infinite, satisfies hypothesis (B) with p = 3. It also proves Péterfalvi's example from the same paper, which shows that SL(2, 2^q) satisfies hypothesis (B) with p = 2, so the hypothesis is not empty. The proof is new. It turns a witness of hypothesis (B) into relations between three copies of the additive group of the field with 3^q elements, and it rules out these relations by arithmetic in that field.

records.name: ClassFieldTheory.GlobalClassFieldComparison.finiteAbelianGlobalReciprocity_relativeNormQuotient
records.entry_name: Global class field theory in Lean 4.35.0-rc2
records.doc: For every finite abelian extension L/K of number fields, the idèle class group C_K modulo the image of the idèle-class norm from C_L is isomorphic as a topological multiplicative group to Gal(L/K). The Challenge defines the norm as the determinant on the relative adèle algebra and descends it through principal idèles; the included ClassFieldTheory development supplies the proof of the resulting reciprocity theorem.

records.name: ClassFieldTheory.finiteAbelianLocalReciprocity_quotient
records.entry_name: Local class field theory in Lean 4.35.0-rc2
records.doc: For every finite abelian extension L/K of a nonarchimedean local field, the multiplicative group K× modulo the field-norm subgroup N_{L/K}(L×) is isomorphic as a topological group to Gal(L/K). The registered declaration is the finite norm-quotient form of local reciprocity proved in the included ClassFieldTheory development. Stronger compatibility, normalization and existence results in that development are documented separately and are not part of the compared declaration.

records.name: Scott2026.csl2026
records.entry_name: Lean Formalization of Interpreting Lambda Calculus in Domain-Valued Random Variables (CSL 2026)
records.doc: Formalization in Lean 4 / mathlib of the existing paper by Furber, Mardare, Panangaden, and Scott, Interpreting Lambda Calculus in Domain-Valued Random Variables (LIPIcs, Vol. 363, CSL 2026, Article 48). This repository formalizes that published mathematics; it does not present the paper's results as new mathematics originating in this repository. Three capstones sit on top of the rest of the paper: Theorem 26 (internal λ-interpretation in SetoidF_A), Corollary 34 (the Engeler model with numerals in V^A), and Theorem 43 (two fair-coin subsets of ℕ that are incomparable under the λ-definable many-one preorder). Domain-theory background is imported from a vendored copy of scott1972. The Palomar Challenge locks Theorem 43 as csl2026 and proposition_36_i on the Engeler graph model. Full Corollary 34 remains kernel-checked in the library and is not represented by a weaker Mathlib-only proxy. Lean is written by AI agents under the direction and review of the author. Dana Scott gave the author the paper. This formalization does not claim that the paper's authors participated in it or endorsed it. There is no sorry outside the deliberate holes in Challenge.lean, no project-defined axiom, and Mathlib is the only Lake require.

records.name: PalomarPaperN.main
records.entry_name: Conditional Hilbert-space classification of Gromov--Hausdorff space
records.doc: A Lean formalization of the implication from five explicitly stated literature inputs to a homeomorphism between the ordinary Gromov--Hausdorff space of nonempty compact metric spaces and real square-summable sequences. The proof constructs invariant full-support probability assignments, finite dimensional local models, global AR domination and discrete approximation. The five literature inputs are assumptions, not theorems proved in this snapshot.

records.name: PalomarQuantumQuery.strong_duality
records.entry_name: Adversary bounds and the polynomial method for quantum queries
records.doc: Lean proofs of strong duality and exact block composition for the negative-weight adversary bound on total Boolean functions, explicit constant-factor characterizations of bounded-error quantum query complexity in value and Boolean XOR oracle models, and uniform extraction of query algorithms from supplied promise dual certificates. The submission also proves that every output probability of a q-query algorithm on Boolean inputs has a real polynomial representation of degree at most 2q in each model. Seven statements are compared against a standalone Mathlib-only specification of the finite quantum model.

records.name: EDP.erdos_discrepancy
records.entry_name: A Lean formalization of the Erdős discrepancy theorem
records.doc: A formalization in Lean 4 and Mathlib of the Erdős discrepancy theorem, proved by Terence Tao in 2015: for every sequence f(1), f(2), … of signs ±1 and every C there are d ≥ 1 and n with |f(d) + f(2d) + ⋯ + f(nd)| > C, so every ±1 sequence has unbounded discrepancy along homogeneous arithmetic progressions. This is the original ±1 formulation, Corollary 1.2 of Tao's paper; its Hilbert-space-valued Theorem 1.1 is not formalized. The proof follows the architecture of Tao's argument: a Fourier-analytic reduction from a sequence of bounded discrepancy to a stochastic completely multiplicative function with bounded mean-square partial sums; a van der Corput argument, driven by the logarithmically averaged two-point Elliott estimate, forcing such a function to pretend to be a twisted Dirichlet character; and a generalized Borwein–Choi–Coons argument excluding that case. The analytic number theory these steps use is proved in the same development rather than assumed: the entropy-decrement proof of the two-point Elliott estimate from Tao's companion paper, the Matomäki–Radziwiłł short-interval estimate on the major arcs via the Dirichlet-polynomial route of Matomäki, Radziwiłł and Tao, the Halász–Montgomery large-values inequality, a large-values bound for Dirichlet polynomials over primes from a zero-free region of the Riemann zeta function, that zero-free region from Weyl-sum bounds on zeta, and a form of Vinogradov's mean value theorem. Where a published route did not fit, the development adapts it; the adaptations are documented. The theorem depends only on Lean's three standard axioms. This is a formalization of a published result, not a new proof; it was produced by AI agents working through pull requests checked by continuous integration in the ProofFleet repository (formerly MoltResearch).

records.name: DigraphRealizability.publication_resolution
records.entry_name: Characterizing digraph support families by rooted-interval deletion
records.doc: We answer the set-theoretic characterization question for digraph support families posed by Mike Steel in Section 4 of Interior operators and their relationship to autocatalytic networks (arXiv:2305.16714v4, 2023). A digraph on a finite set E is given by a predecessor map P assigning to each vertex e a set P(e) of in-neighbours, loops allowed, and a set S is supported when every element e of S has some element of S in P(e). The characterization refers only to the family F. Start from the full power set of E with no roots used. A legal step chooses a remaining set S outside F that is inclusion-maximal among the remaining sets outside F, chooses a root r in S that has not been used before and lies in no member of F contained in S, and deletes every remaining set X with r in X and X contained in S. A family F of subsets of E is exactly the support family of some predecessor map on E if and only if some finite sequence of legal steps ends exactly at F.

records.name: Langford.twoFold_exists_iff
records.entry_name: Two-fold Langford sequences exist exactly when 3l ≥ 2d − 1; the m-fold counting bound and its attainment, and a residue bound
records.doc: A Lean 4 characterization of two-fold Langford sequences. An m-fold Langford sequence of order l and defect d fills the positions 1, ..., 2ml so that every p in [d, d + l - 1] occupies the endpoints of m pairwise disjoint pairs of positions at distance p. For d, l >= 1 a two-fold sequence exists exactly when 3l >= 2d - 1. For every m, (2m - 1)l >= 2d - 1 is necessary, with l(2d + l + 1) = 0 (mod 4) for odd m, and the bound is attained whenever 2d + l = 2ml + 1; the row of order one exists exactly when d divides m; no three-fold sequence of order 3 and defect 6 exists; and for every m >= 3 the necessary conditions are not sufficient. For every T >= 1, with r = ml mod T, every m-fold sequence satisfies the residue bound r(T - r) <= m * sum |p - T| over p in [d, d + l - 1], which contains the counting bound and the necessity half of the order-one theorem. Every m-fold sequence satisfies the forced-endpoint bound 6mld + ml <= 4d^2 + 2(ml)^2 + ml^2. For every m >= 3 the cell (d, l) = (3m - 3, 3) meets the necessary conditions and admits no m-fold sequence. Equality 2d + l = 2ml + 1 holds exactly when every pair straddles the middle, that is ml < i + s_i for every position i <= ml. Alkasasbeh, Dyer and Howell define these sequences and ask for necessary and sufficient conditions when m >= 2; this repository answers the question for m = 2. Necessity is a distance sum. Sufficiency at m = 2 is strong induction on l: sixteen literal cells, concatenation, and otherwise a mirror-symmetric sequence built by Lemma S from a signed permutation, which is found on the whole cone by inversion, the reversal, a descent along lines of fixed mu, and in the band by 21 block-reversal families plus the two-block reversal tau_l, eight sporadic cells and three bases. The tight line is m interleaved copies of the source's Table 1.

records.name: erdos_1219
records.entry_name: Erdős Problem #1219 in Lean 4: Σ_k 2^{ℵ_{n_k}} → (ℵ_ω)² (Shelah 1975)
records.doc: Erdős problem #1219 (erdosproblems.com/1219; Erdős–Hajnal 1971, Problem 3, asked by Erdős, Hajnal and Rado): let (n_k) be an increasing sequence of integers such that 2^{ℵ_{n_k}} is strictly increasing and 2^{ℵ_{n_0}} > ℵ_ω; is it true that Σ_k 2^{ℵ_{n_k}} → (ℵ_ω)²?  Shelah (Notes on partition calculus, 1975, §1) proved that the answer is yes.  This project formalizes that proof in Lean 4 with Mathlib: the comparator target erdos_1219 states that for every strictly increasing n : ℕ → ℕ with k ↦ 2 ^ ℵ_(n k) strictly increasing and ℵ_ω < 2 ^ ℵ_(n 0), the binary partition relation PartitionArrow (Σ_k 2 ^ ℵ_(n k)) ℵ_ω holds, i.e. every 2-colouring of the 2-element subsets of a set of cardinality Σ_k 2 ^ ℵ_(n k) has a monochromatic subset of cardinality ℵ_ω (PartitionArrow is the binary case of formal-conjectures' Combinatorics.cardinalPartitionRel).  The proof follows Shelah's Canonization Lemma 1.1 and Theorem 1.2: the unbalanced Erdős–Rado theorem (2^μ)⁺ → ((2^μ)⁺, μ⁺)² (proved here with a critical-ordinal / closure-point argument), a canonization of the colouring across blocks of sizes (2^{ℵ_{n_k}})⁺ by means of guides generic over all small subsets of the earlier blocks, and Ramsey's theorem for pairs on ℕ.  The target is proved from propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound only and passes the Lean comparator (landrun sandbox, NanoDa kernel).

records.name: Erdos809.main_result
records.entry_name: Erdős Problem 809: rainbow odd cycles
records.doc: A Lean proof resolving the Burr–Erdős–Graham–Sós conjecture (Erdős Problem 809): for every fixed odd cycle of length at least seven, the maximal anti-Ramsey threshold at floor(n²/4) + 1 edges is n²/8 + o(n²). The seven-cycle case is new to our knowledge. The development proves it and formalizes the stronger full-density result of Bucić, Chen, and Ma for odd cycles of length at least nine.

records.name: Magma1518.table
records.entry_name: One-generated (1518 + 3862)-magmas are trivial or the Z/3 shift; an explicit family of finite 1518-magmas violating laws 47, 614, 817, 3862
records.doc: Lean 4 results (core Lean, no dependencies, no axioms beyond the standard three) about law 1518 of the Equational Theories Project, x = (y ◇ y) ◇ (x ◇ (y ◇ x)). Theorem A: in every magma satisfying 1518 and 3862 (x ◇ x = (x ◇ (x ◇ x)) ◇ x), writing S x = x ◇ x, the set {x, S x, S (S x)} is closed under ◇ with u ◇ v = S v and S (S (S x)) = x; hence every one-generated such magma is the trivial magma or the three-element cyclic shift x ◇ y = y + 1. This proves a classification conjectured by Terence Tao on the Lean Zulip on 2024-11-29 (message 485148288). That message assumed 1518 together with all four of 47, 614, 817 and 3862 and carried no finiteness hypothesis; assuming 3862 alone is no weaker, because Matthew Bolan reported the same day (message 485153888) that 1518 and 3862 already imply the other three. What is added here is a machine-checked proof, not a weaker hypothesis: no proof of the classification was found in the venues searched. Theorem A is what the compared declarations state. Outside them the repository holds an explicit family of finite 1518-magmas that do violate the four targets, with two members checked by kernel evaluation, and kernel-checked certificate identities behind a cohomological obstruction theorem (every 1518-cocycle over the shift with finite fibre is a coboundary), whose reduction is a written proof, and the computations classifying base-dependent extensions of the shift.

Theorem A: in every magma satisfying 1518 and 3862 (x ◇ x = (x ◇ (x ◇ x)) ◇ x), writing S x = x ◇ x, the set {x, S x, S (S x)} is closed under ◇ with u ◇ v = S v and S (S (S x)) = x; hence every one-generated such magma is the trivial magma or the three-element cyclic shift x ◇ y = y + 1. This proves a classification conjectured by Terence Tao on the Lean Zulip on 2024-11-29 (message 485148288). That message assumed 1518 together with all four of 47, 614, 817 and 3862 and carried no finiteness hypothesis; assuming 3862 alone is no weaker, because Matthew Bolan reported the same day (message 485153888) that 1518 and 3862 already imply the other three. What is added here is a machine-checked proof, not a weaker hypothesis: no proof of the classification was found in the venues searched. Theorem A is what the compared declarations state. Outside them the repository holds an explicit family of finite 1518-magmas that do violate the four targets, with two members checked by kernel evaluation, and kernel-checked certificate identities behind a cohomological obstruction theorem (every 1518-cocycle over the shift with finite fibre is a coboundary), whose reduction is a written proof, and the computations classifying base-dependent extensions of the shift.

records.name: CSeparatedNPComplete.partition_gadget_schedule_partition_iff
records.entry_name: NP-hardness of Gaussian c-separation
records.doc: A Lean 4 proof development of reduction idea toward NP-hardness of feature selection for relative Gaussian c-separation in the formulation of Borozan et al. The argument starts from NP-completeness of equal-cardinality partition of positive squares, giving integral Gaussian data via integer roots and an even paired total. Three Gaussians enforce partition balance, and a schedule of d+1 Gaussians enforces binary selectors. Explicit separation of the two blocks makes cross-block hinge penalties vanish. The fixed threshold is (dot s 1 / 2)*d*(d+1)/2 - 3*d/4, an integer multiple of 1/4 for natural input weights. Here d is the full dimension. The main proved result is the pointwise gadget iff. The full complexity reduction is not formalized. The threshold depends only on the input. General Karamata inequality and an unconditional ordinary-PARTITION to perfect-square equal-cardinality partition equivalence are auxiliary results stated in Solution.lean. The square encoding has proved injectivity and numerical size bounds; its NP-completeness argument is documented prose. The original Gaussian gadget predicate also has a proved binary certificate verifier with soundness, completeness, and quadratic work in a bit-cost model. The Gaussian gadget equivalence and square-partition reduction were developed and first presented by the author in this formalization. Their mathematical novelty and priority relative to earlier literature are unknown; no systematic literature search or comparison establishing them has been documented.

records.name: ZetaWindow.zeta_7_to_21_not_all_rational_palomar
records.entry_name: At least one of ζ(7), ζ(9), …, ζ(21) is irrational
records.doc: A Lean 4 and Mathlib proof that at least one of the eight values ζ(7), ζ(9), ζ(11), ζ(13), ζ(15), ζ(17), ζ(19), ζ(21) of the Riemann zeta function is irrational. The statement uses only Mathlib's riemannZeta, the theorem has no hypotheses, and its proof uses only the axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. The shortest list of odd zeta values starting at ζ(7) that our literature search found proved to contain an irrational number was ζ(7), ζ(9), …, ζ(35) (W. Zudilin, Math. Notes 2001). The proof uses the very-well-poised linear forms of Zudilin (J. Théor. Nombres Bordeaux 2004, §8) with five derivatives, 23 factors and the direction vector η₀ = 160, η = (47, 47, 47, 47, 48, 50, 50, 51, 52, …, 66); they are linear forms in 1, ζ(7), ζ(9), …, ζ(21) with rational coefficients. Zudilin anticipated such an improvement but could not prove the asymptotics of his forms (his Lemma 20) for more than three derivatives. The proof here does not need them. The denominators of the coefficients are bounded by Zudilin's arithmetic lemma, the prime number theorem (proved from a vendored Lean proof of the Wiener–Ikehara theorem) and a kernel-checked table of 2602 pieces of Zudilin's function φ. For large n the forms are bounded by e^(−748.1n), through a contour integral on a fixed vertical line, pointwise estimates and certified numerical inequalities, without saddle-point analysis. They are non-zero if the eight values are rational, because at the auxiliary primes ℓ = 63n − 1, of which there are infinitely many by Dirichlet's theorem, the constant term has ℓ-adic valuation −5 while the coefficients of the zeta values are ℓ-integral. The theorem does not say which value is irrational. The mathematics and the Lean code were produced by AI agents under human direction and have not been refereed.

records.name: FutileCycle.resolution
records.entry_name: Determinants and unstable cores in sequential distributive phosphorylation
records.doc: Vassena and Stadler (arXiv:2308.11486v3, Supplementary Example D) conjectured that sequential distributive phosphorylation cycles have only unstable-positive cores and that every invertible child-selection matrix has determinant of absolute value one. The determinant assertion is proved, and the restriction to unstable-positive cores is disproved. In the n-site cycle, every child-selection matrix has determinant 0, 1 or -1. For every n >= 3, a six-species child-selection matrix is minimally Hurwitz-unstable and has determinant 1, giving an unstable-negative core. For every n >= 2, there is an unstable-positive core on 2n+1 species, so their sizes are unbounded; every proper principal submatrix remains nonunstable under every positive column scaling. For every n >= 3, there is also a five-species D-unstable core: a positive column scaling makes it unstable, while every proper principal submatrix remains nonunstable under all such scalings.

records.name: ThreeSitePhosphorylation.AllSiteAttractingFamily.all_site_attracting_hopf
records.entry_name: Attracting oscillations in sequential distributive phosphorylation
records.doc: Vassena (arXiv:2608.27081v2, Section 8) left open whether sequential distributive phosphorylation cycles with three or more sites admit Hopf bifurcation under mass-action kinetics. For every n >= 3, a componentwise-affine family of positive rate constants is constructed for the n-site cycle with one kinase and one phosphatase and a fixed positive equilibrium. A family of strictly positive, nonconstant periodic orbits bifurcates from this equilibrium, with amplitudes tending to zero and periods tending to a finite positive limit. Each orbit is orbitally asymptotically stable within its compatibility class: sufficiently nearby states with the same kinase, phosphatase and substrate totals have unique positive forward solutions that remain close to the orbit and converge to it.

records.name: Real.tendsto_complexity_div_atTop
records.entry_name: Adamczewski–Bugeaud 2007: the complexity of algebraic numbers in integer bases
records.doc: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of B. Adamczewski and Y. Bugeaud, On the complexity of algebraic numbers I. Expansions in integer bases (Ann. of Math. 165 (2007)), built on the repository's libraries ArithmeticHeights, DiophantineApproximation and ForMathlib, whose Subspace Theorem with algebraic coefficients it uses. The library AdamczewskiBugeaud2007 is sorry-free and within Lean's three standard axioms. It proves Theorem 1 (the complexity of an irrational algebraic number in an integer base satisfies p(n)/n → ∞, with (1), p(n) − n → ∞), Theorems 2–4 (automatic and morphic expansions), Theorem 5 in full (β Pisot or Salem, bounded integer digits satisfying Condition (∗)_w: the number lies in ℚ(β) or is transcendental), Lemma 1, Theorems 1A–5A on β-expansions with K. Schmidt's periodicity theorem, and the p-adic Theorems 6 and 1B–4B, together with the finite automata and morphisms of §3, and Theorem 7 in corrected form (u_k < min(b, p)) with Christol's theorem (algebraic ⇒ automatic) and a counterexample to Theorem 7 as printed. The counterexample and the corrected hypothesis were worked out during this formalization, not taken from the cited works (see limitations). Thirty-two statements are compared.

records.doc: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of B. Adamczewski and Y. Bugeaud, On the complexity of algebraic numbers I. Expansions in integer bases (Ann. of Math. 165 (2007)), built on the repository's libraries ArithmeticHeights, DiophantineApproximation and ForMathlib, whose Subspace Theorem with algebraic coefficients it uses. The library AdamczewskiBugeaud2007 is sorry-free and within Lean's three standard axioms. It proves Theorem 1 (the complexity of an irrational algebraic number in an integer base satisfies p(n)/n → ∞, with (1), p(n) − n → ∞), Theorems 2–4 (automatic and morphic expansions), Theorem 5 in full (β Pisot or Salem, bounded integer digits satisfying Condition (∗)_w: the number lies in ℚ(β) or is transcendental), Lemma 1, Theorems 1A–5A on β-expansions with K. Schmidt's periodicity theorem, and the p-adic Theorems 6 and 1B–4B, together with the finite automata and morphisms of §3, and Theorem 7 in corrected form (u_k < min(b, p)) with Christol's theorem (algebraic ⇒ automatic) and a counterexample to Theorem 7 as printed. The counterexample and the corrected hypothesis were worked out during this formalization, not taken from the cited works (see limitations). Thirty-two statements are compared.

records.name: ACRZeroDivisors.question313_necessity_counterexample
records.entry_name: Zero-divisor criteria for absolute concentration robustness
records.doc: García Puente et al. (arXiv:2401.00078v3, Question 3.13) asked whether a unique positive zero-divisor value is necessary or sufficient for absolute concentration robustness (ACR) in at-most-bimolecular mass-action networks. Explicit networks with positive rational rates answer both questions negatively. A further three-species example shows that their candidate algorithm can miss a zero-divisor ACR value under an admissible elimination order, refuting the unrestricted elimination-order form of Conjecture 4.7. For block orders that compare the other species before the distinguished species, completeness is established: every real zero-divisor ACR value is returned when the finite basis consists of nonzero steady-ideal elements whose leading monomials cover the ideal. ACR includes existence of a positive steady state; zero-divisor values include coordinate differences lying in the steady-state ideal.

records.name: KissingNumber.kissingNumber_three
records.entry_name: kissing-number-lean
records.doc: The kissing number of Euclidean 3-space is 12: at most twelve unit balls with disjoint interiors touch a given unit ball, and twelve do. The upper bound follows Musin's extension of the Delsarte linear-programming method. The Delsarte machinery on the sphere (positive-definite zonal kernels up to degree 9 and the LP bound, which by itself gives only 13) is built from scratch, since Mathlib has no spherical harmonics. The lower bound is the cuboctahedron.

records.name: li2_one_half_irrational
records.entry_name: Irrationality of Li₂(1/2)
records.doc: A Lean formalization of the irrationality of Li₂(1/2) = Σ_{n≥1} 2^(-n)/n². The proof is inspired by A. Fauzan's work on the irrationality of ζ(5) and builds on Moritz Firsching's Lean formalization in mo271/Zeta5. The central idea is to establish the irrationality of a real number r by constructing a sequence of integer polynomials P_n whose values P_n(r) decay rapidly as n tends to infinity, while for every rational q, P_n(q) ≠ 0 for infinitely many n. Analytic umbral calculus was used to find suitable polynomials Q_n with rational coefficients. Random matrix theory provides rapid decay of Q_n(r) as n tends to infinity. Estimates of p-adic valuations, together with the prime number theorem, ensure that the values P_n(r) of the corresponding primitive integer polynomials also decay rapidly as n tends to infinity, completing the proof. Similar methods may apply to other values Li₂(1/n), but those cases are not included here. The compared theorem depends on propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound and on nothing else, and there is no sorry outside the one deliberate hole in Challenge.lean.

records.doc: The red-blue pebble game of Hong Jia-Wei and H. T. Kung (STOC 1981) models a computation on a directed acyclic graph run with S words of fast memory and unlimited slow memory: a red pebble on a vertex is its value held in fast memory, a blue pebble its value held in slow memory, and each load or store costs one I/O operation. This formalisation defines the game, complete calculations and the minimum I/O time Q, and proves three families of results from the paper, with explicit constants and, where the paper states one, in its asymptotic form. Q is 0 by convention where no complete calculation exists, so each statement about Q is made only where one does. First, the partition lemma (Theorem 3.1 and Lemma 3.1): every complete calculation with at most S red pebbles and q I/O operations yields a 2S-partition of the graph into h sets with q <= S h <= q + S, so that Q >= S (P(2S) - 1) wherever a complete calculation exists. Read literally, the paper's Theorem 3.1 is false in two ways, since its rules let inputs be computed free of charge and let inputs be vertices other than the sources; here, as in Elango et al. (2014), the inputs are exactly the sources and cannot be computed. Second, the n-point FFT graph, for n = 2^k with k >= 1: every S-dominator partition has h sets with n (log2 n + 1) <= h S log2(2S) (Theorem 4.1, with a per-set bound sharper than the paper's, which also closes a gap in its proof), a complete calculation exists exactly when S >= 3, and every complete calculation has q >= 2n and n log2 n <= 5 q log2 S (Corollary 4.1 with an explicit constant); Q log S = Omega(n log n) holds with one constant for all such n and all S >= 3, and P_D(S) = Omega(n log n / (S log S)) with one constant for all such n and all S >= 2. Third, matrix multiplication by the ordinary algorithm, for every graph in which the m k n products A_il B_lj are vertices of their own, each with an edge from its two factors, and no vertex can be reached from the products of two different entries of the result; for m, k, n >= 1 this class contains every independent evaluation in the paper's sense. Every complete calculation has m k n <= 2 q sqrt(S) (Corollary 6.2 with an explicit constant), and for k >= 1 also q >= mk + kn + mn; Q sqrt(S) = Omega(m k n) holds with one constant over any collection of such graphs, for every graph of the collection and every S at which that graph has a complete calculation; and for all m, k, n >= 1 some such graph has a complete calculation exactly when S >= 3. Kung (STOC 1981) models a computation on a directed acyclic graph run with S words of fast memory and unlimited slow memory: a red pebble on a vertex is its value held in fast memory, a blue pebble its value held in slow memory, and each load or store costs one I/O operation. This formalisation defines the game, complete calculations and the minimum I/O time Q, and proves three families of results from the paper, with explicit constants and, where the paper states one, in its asymptotic form. Q is 0 by convention where no complete calculation exists, so each statement about Q is made only where one does. First, the partition lemma (Theorem 3.1 and Lemma 3.1): every complete calculation with at most S red pebbles and q I/O operations yields a 2S-partition of the graph into h sets with q <= S h <= q + S, so that Q >= S (P(2S) - 1) wherever a complete calculation exists. Read literally, the paper's Theorem 3.1 is false in two ways, since its rules let inputs be computed free of charge and let inputs be vertices other than the sources; here, as in Elango et al. (2014), the inputs are exactly the sources and cannot be computed. Second, the n-point FFT graph, for n = 2^k with k >= 1: every S-dominator partition has h sets with n (log2 n + 1) <= h S log2(2S) (Theorem 4.1, with a per-set bound sharper than the paper's, which also closes a gap in its proof), a complete calculation exists exactly when S >= 3, and every complete calculation has q >= 2n and n log2 n <= 5 q log2 S (Corollary 4.1 with an explicit constant); Q log S = Omega(n log n) holds with one constant for all such n and all S >= 3, and P_D(S) = Omega(n log n / (S log S)) with one constant for all such n and all S >= 2. Third, matrix multiplication by the ordinary algorithm, for every graph in which the m k n products A_il B_lj are vertices of their own, each with an edge from its two factors, and no vertex can be reached from the products of two different entries of the result; for m, k, n >= 1 this class contains every independent evaluation in the paper's sense. Every complete calculation has m k n <= 2 q sqrt(S) (Corollary 6.2 with an explicit constant), and for k >= 1 also q >= mk + kn + mn; Q sqrt(S) = Omega(m k n) holds with one constant over any collection of such graphs, for every graph of the collection and every S at which that graph has a complete calculation; and for all m, k, n >= 1 some such graph has a complete calculation exactly when S >= 3. Mathlib has no pebble games, so the statements rest on twelve definitions of the formalisation's own, which the Challenge restates for the reader. Not formalised: the paper's upper bounds (its Theorem 2.1 and section 8, which it states without proof), its sections 5 and 7, and its Theorem 6.1 for general expressions.

records.name: PalomarLovasz.vertex_transitive_long_cycle
records.entry_name: Near-linear cycles in connected vertex-transitive graphs
records.doc: A Lean formalization of the near-linear cycle theorem in "Lovász conjecture holds asymptotically". For every positive ε, sufficiently large connected finite vertex-transitive graphs contain a simple cycle with at least n^(1−ε) edges. The development includes a weaker-constant Bondy–Locke path-to-cycle comparison and the finite approximate-group and expansion arguments used in the path proofs.

records.name: FKSEdgeThreshold.Palomar.target
records.entry_name: Frankl-Kupavskii-Swanepoel Theorem 3: fewer than C(d+2,2) edges embeds in R^d
records.doc: For every integer d ≥ 4, every finite simple graph with fewer than C(d + 2, 2) edges has an injective placement in Euclidean d-space under which every edge has length 1, and the complete graph K_{d+2} has exactly C(d + 2, 2) edges and has no such placement. Equivalently, f(d) = C(d + 2, 2), where f(d) is the least number of edges in a finite simple graph with no unit-distance representation in R^d. Non-edges may also lie at distance 1. Finite simple graphs are represented as SimpleGraph (Fin n), including the empty graph. The proof is Frankl–Kupavskii–Swanepoel Theorem 3, already proved in the GraphDimension library and imported here. The spherical half of the same theorem is not stated. The question belongs to discrete geometry and extremal graph theory, specifically the study of unit-distance representations and the dimension of graphs.

records.name: KrohnRhodes.krohn_rhodes_prime_decomposition
records.entry_name: Krohn–Rhodes decomposition of finite monoids into aperiodic and simple-group factors
records.doc: A Lean 4 and Mathlib formalization of the Krohn–Rhodes prime decomposition theorem for finite monoids, in a form with aperiodic factors: every finite monoid M divides an iterated wreath product of finite monoids, each of which is aperiodic or a simple group, and every simple group among the factors divides M. The proof follows the local-divisor proof of Diekert, Kufleitner and Steinberg. Unlike the classical statement, the aperiodic factors are not reduced to copies of the three-element flip-flop monoid U₂; for an aperiodic M the statement holds with M as its only factor, and in general it separates the group structure of M, as simple groups dividing M, from aperiodic factors.

records.name: Zeta2.Z7.zeta2_7_irrational_palomar
records.entry_name: The 2-adic zeta value ζ₂(7) is irrational
records.doc: A Lean 4 and Mathlib proof that the 2-adic zeta value ζ₂(7) is irrational. The theorem has no hypotheses, and its proof uses only the axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. The value is defined through the Volkenborn integral: zeta2 s = J(s−1)/((s−1)·2^s), where J(s) is the 2-adic limit of the Riemann sums 2^(−N) Σ_{x<2^N} (x+1/2)^(−s), so zeta2 7 = J(6)/768; the theorem also proves that these limits exist. By Lemma 2.8 of Lai, Sprang and Zudilin (IMRN 2026), zeta2 s is the Kubota–Leopoldt value ζ₂(s) = L₂(s, ω^(1−s)) for s ≥ 2. That identification is cited, not formalised; it only involves a non-zero rational factor, which does not affect irrationality. ζ₂(3) and ζ₂(5) are known to be irrational, and L. Lai (Int. J. Number Theory 2025) proved that at least one of ζ₂(7), ζ₂(9), ζ₂(11), ζ₂(13) is irrational; the theorem here implies that result and the two registered formalisations of the same maintainer for {ζ₂(7), ζ₂(9), ζ₂(11)} and {ζ₂(7), ζ₂(9)}. An unrefereed draft by C. D. Long claims, by a different method, that ζ₂(s) is irrational for every odd s with 3 ≤ s ≤ 29; it is not used here, and an internal review of it (docs/long_review.md) found a gap in its large-prime step, so we do not regard it as settling the question. No refereed proof that ζ₂(7) is irrational is known to us. The proof uses the linear forms S_n = ∫ R_n'''(t+1/2−n/2) dt = ρ_n + Z_n ζ₂(7) of the rational functions R_n(t) = (2t+n) Π_{m=1}^{6} Π_{c∈C_m} (t+1/2+c) / Π_{k=0}^{n} (t+k)^(a_k), with six nested well-poised numerator blocks C_m = [η_m n, (1−η_m) n − 1], η = (5, 7, 7, 9, 11, 13)/40, and pole orders a_k ∈ {1, 2, 3, 4} that ramp up from both ends; the evaluation at the centred point t + 1/2 − n/2 leaves ζ₂(7) as the only zeta value. The 2-adic size of S_n comes from Lai's and Sprang's Δ-calculus, and the size of the coefficients from residue-level Cauchy bounds and a certified maximum of an explicit potential. The odd part of the denominators is bounded by a residue-class analysis of the partial fractions (a class lemma, a kernel identity and per-pole bounds, evaluated on local models of the residue classes whose values are certified in Lean on finitely many intervals) and the prime number theorem, proved here from a vendored Lean proof of the Wiener–Ikehara theorem. If ζ₂(7) were rational, the valuations at the auxiliary prime ℓ = 19n/20 − 1 (an idea of Lai and Sprang) would make S_n non-zero for infinitely many n, and Lai's irrationality criterion gives the contradiction. The mathematics and the Lean code were produced by AI agents under human direction and have not been refereed.

records.name: DStabilityHardness.dStability_coNP_reduction
records.entry_name: Deciding D-stability is coNP-hard
records.doc: The computational difficulty of D-stability, raised by Chen, Fan and Yu (1995, doi:10.1016/0167-6911(94)00036-U), is addressed by an explicit integer-matrix reduction from PARTITION. For positive weights of total 2T, the construction produces a matrix of order m + 4 that is D-stable exactly when no subset has weight T. When an equal split exists, some positive diagonal scaling has an eigenvalue with strictly positive real part. A Pell recursion supplies the parameters, with a logarithmic search bound and an explicit bound on every matrix entry. These bounds give polynomial binary output length. Together with the classical NP-completeness of PARTITION, the reduction yields coNP-hardness of D-stability and D-semistability, and NP-hardness of strict D-instability, even for a four-dimensional core with attachments at one coordinate.

records.name: DStability5x5.dStable_iff_explicit
records.entry_name: A critical-point criterion for D-stability in every dimension
records.doc: Johnson's contact criterion for D-stability is expressed as an explicit principal-minor critical-point system. For every real square matrix and every choice of positive barrier weights, D-stability is equivalent to Hurwitz stability and the absence of positive solutions of the associated Fritz-John equations. The proof applies a proper exhaustion of the positive orthant to Johnson's contact variety, so that every nonempty contact set contains a critical point. In dimension five, the criterion is written explicitly as a Lagrange system and a tangency system, with coefficients given by principal minors. Both equivalences are formalized in Lean. The result applies the classical critical-point method to the characterization problem discussed by Kanovei and Logofet (1998) and Kushel (arXiv:2604.16526).

records.name: SumDifferenceResults.pair_bound
records.entry_name: Improved sum–difference inequalities in abelian groups
records.doc: For all finite subsets X,Y of an abelian group,  |X-Y| <= |X+Y|^λ with λ = (9451e-3286)/(5378e+787) = 1.454277448906…, less than the classical exponent 3/2. A multiscale transfer gives the upper bound (13524e-7359)/(9451e-3286) = 1.312373302115… for the Gyarmati–Hennecart–Ruzsa small-sumset exponent, less than their exponent 4/3. The proof of the first result combines a coupling with distinct differences, entropy inequalities for independent sums, a finite certificate using non-Shannon inequalities, and an explicit limiting certificate. The transfer uses localization and the Plünnecke-Ruzsa inequality over a sequence of scales.

records.name: SolidLean.Palomar.tower_theory_solid
records.entry_name: solid-lean
records.doc: The tower theory H is the many-sorted first-order theory of a tower of ZFC universes Z_0, Z_1, ... cut at consecutive inaccessible cardinals, with transition maps j_n identifying Z_n with the rank segment V(kappa_n) of Z_{n+1}.  H is solid in Enayat's sense.  For models M, N, P, with N interpreted in M and P interpreted in N, and an M-definable isomorphism between M and P, there is an M-definable isomorphism between M and N.  The registered statement (Palomar/Challenge.lean) writes out the many-sorted first-order logic of H from scratch, with structures, formulas, satisfaction and definability with parameters.  It states the axioms of H with Separation and Replacement as schemes over all definable classes, finitary interpretations in one-coordinate normal form (each interpreted sort is a definable subset of a single sort modulo a definable equivalence; the reduction from tuple domains is not formalized), presentations, and definable isomorphisms.  The theorem is Theorem 2.1 of the accompanying paper, "Solid idealized Lean", where it is the tower half of the bi-interpretability of an idealized Lean with H.  The proof (Palomar/Solution.lean) reduces the statement to the development's semantic solidity theorem tower_solid.

records.name: ProbStack.Palomar.nonstackable_exists_directedMessage_le
records.entry_name: ProbStack — Random Stacking on Trees
records.doc: Lean 4 formalization of a deterministic finite-path necessity theorem for graph-pebbling stackability: a positive-mass nonstackable path configuration above an explicit mass threshold must contain an actual directed integer branch message at most -h.  The package also verifies the exact fixed-total corollary at total n*mu, forcing a message at most -(2*mu-1).  The project's two-sided random path threshold theorem is not part of this Palomar result.

records.name: HorizonEinsteinClosure.geometricHodgeGeneration
records.entry_name: Local Hodge generation of sl(15) and scalar response rigidity
records.doc: An explicit local Hodge operator on the oriented coordinate four-plane 0123, extended by zero, together with the fifteen adjoint basis actions of the orthogonal algebra for diag(1,1,1,-1,1,-1), generates sl(15,K) over every field of characteristic different from two. A finite integral commutator certificate produces signed skew matrix units and one symmetric seed; a general propagation lemma then produces all trace-free matrices. Dimension 224 follows from generation. As a consequence, an endomorphism of this algebra commuting with the commutator actions of the same sixteen generators is scalar, with determinant c^224. The proof includes characteristics three and five without a simplicity assumption. The contribution is this constructive generation-and-rigidity theorem. PDT motivates the chosen operators; assigning a physical response magnitude or gravitational coupling is outside the selected claim.

records.name: MixedDegradation.paper_mixed_degradation_unistationarity
records.entry_name: Unistationarity of Type II_l and Type V normal forms with nonnegative degradation
records.doc: Nandan, Nghe and Unterberger (arXiv:2507.15546, Theorem 5.2 and the following remark) left uniqueness with degradation unresolved for Type II_l cores with l > 2 and, when some degradation rates vanish, for Type V cores. For the source-minimal Type II_l normal forms with l ≥ 3 and the Type V normal forms, unistationarity is established for reversible mass-action kinetics with positive forward and reverse rate constants and arbitrary nonnegative linear degradation. Any two strictly positive stationary concentration vectors coincide, including all internal species of the reversible unit chains. The Type II_l class includes separated stems and the coincident three-fork case. The proof combines passive-chain elimination and a ratio argument for Type V with boundary Jacobian nonsingularity and an implicit-function argument for Type II_l.

records.name: FKSProblem2.Palomar.target
records.entry_name: FKS Problem 2 in dimension three
records.doc: A Lean-checked proof of the d = 3 case of FKS Problem 2: for every simple graph G on seven vertices, G or its complement has an injective placement in Euclidean three-space under which every edge has length 1. Non-edges are unconstrained and may also have length 1. The full question, for graphs on 2d + 1 vertices in dimension d, is stated and marked open. In the notation of Alon and Kupavskii, the proved case gives f_D(7) ≤ 3; together with the published lower bound it implies f_D(7) = 3. The formal target is the seven-vertex disjunction, not a definition or equality for f_D. The research audience is discrete geometers and extremal graph theorists studying unit-distance representations, graph dimension and distance Ramsey questions.

records.name: UnconstrainedPACDetection.complexity_root
records.entry_name: Unconstrained detection of productive autocatalytic cores is NP-complete
records.doc: Kosc, Kuperberg, Rajon and Charlat (PNAS 122, e2421274122, 2025, Section 2.1) left open the complexity of detecting an autocatalytic core without a prescribed target species or allowed-food set. For finite reversible reaction networks with literal nonnegative integer reactant and product matrices, this unconstrained detection problem is proved NP-complete. A core is a nonempty entity/reaction pair, minimal under componentwise inclusion, with a selected reactant and product in every selected reaction and a signed real flow that strictly produces every selected entity. The input uses a canonical binary encoding. NP membership and a total polynomial-time many-one reduction from SAT are formalized using Complexitylib’s multi-tape Turing machines, including the Cook–Levin theorem.

records.name: FKSProblem1.Palomar.target
records.entry_name: FKS Problem 1 on at most twice the dimension vertices
records.doc: A Lean-checked proof of FKS Problem 1 for graphs on at most 2d vertices, for every d ≥ 4: every finite simple graph of maximum degree at most d with no connected component isomorphic to K_{d+1} has an injective placement in Euclidean d-space, with every vertex of norm 1/√2 and every edge at distance exactly 1. Non-edges are unconstrained and may also have length 1. The unrestricted question is false at d = 4: Mishra and Senthilkumar (2026) showed that the square of the nine-cycle, on 2d + 1 = 9 vertices, has no such placement. The bound proved here is therefore sharp at d = 4. Neither result settles the question restricted to d ≥ 5. The exception is interpreted componentwise: a K_{d+1} component already precludes such a placement even when other components are present. The research audience is discrete geometers and extremal graph theorists studying spherical unit-distance representations, graph dimension and bounded-degree embedding problems.

records.name: PalomarBlackScholes.black_scholes
records.entry_name: Black-Scholes pricing via Girsanov change of measure
records.doc: Formal proof of the time-zero Black-Scholes formula for a European call on any strong solution of the geometric Brownian motion SDE, with positive initial price, strike, volatility and maturity, and constant drift and interest rate. The change of measure uses the constant-drift case of the general predictable (dynamic) Girsanov theorem. The discounted stopped asset is a martingale under one fixed terminal measure, and the call-payoff expectation equals the closed-form Black-Scholes expression.

records.name: one_zeta_two_zeta_three_linearIndependent
records.entry_name: Linear independence of 1, ζ(2), ζ(3) over ℚ
records.doc: A Lean formalization of the linear independence of 1, ζ(2) and ζ(3) over ℚ. The proof is inspired by A. Fauzan's work on the irrationality of ζ(5) and builds on the Lean formalization of the irrationality of Li₂(1/2), registered in Palomar as PALOMAR-2026-09-30-000013. It shows that the method of that proof can be pushed further. The main difference from the Li₂(1/2) proof is that the rational functions appearing here are allowed to have poles of order two. The remaining details are similar, with some minor modifications. The compared theorems depend on propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound and on nothing else, and there is no sorry outside the deliberate holes in Challenge.lean.

records.entry_name: Evertse 1984: sums of S-units and linear recurrences
records.doc: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the whole of J.-H. Evertse, On sums of S-units and linear recurrences (Compositio Math. 53 (1984)), built on the repository's libraries ArithmeticHeights and DiophantineApproximation, whose p-adic Subspace Theorem (Schlickewei's, the paper's Theorem 4) it uses. The library Evertse1984 is sorry-free and within Lean's three standard axioms. It proves Theorem 2 (a lower bound for S-integral sums without vanishing subsums, at any set of places), Theorem 1 (finitely many admissible projective solutions of x₀ + ⋯ + xₙ = 0), Corollaries 1 and 2, Lemmas 1 and 2 (polynomial values and shifted polynomial quotients that are S-units), Theorem 3 (for a non-degenerate linear recurrence with at least two characteristic roots, the largest prime ideal norm of u_r / u_s tends to infinity), and Corollaries 3 and 4 (P(u_r) → ∞; u_r = u_s has finitely many solutions r ≠ s). It also compares the paper's cited Theorem 4, the repository's p-adic Subspace Theorem. Fourteen statements are compared.

records.name: TheoremA.palomarStatement
records.entry_name: Embedding countable groups into groups of type FP_n
records.doc: A Lean formalization of Theorem A: every countable group embeds in a group of type FP_n over the integers for each finite n >= 2. The proof uses a 23-index, 15-triple Fano-plane construction to supply the finite input to geometric, homological, and relative Leary arguments. It does not assert the existence of one FP_infty overgroup.

records.name: PascalExtremesPalomar.targetA_attainment
records.entry_name: Pascal Extremes
records.doc: A Lean 4 formalisation of sharp p-adic extremal behaviour for the restricted binomial gcd G(N;m) = gcd{C(N,k) : 0 < k < N, m divides k}. For every prime p and m >= 2 with p not dividing m, it proves that the maximum of v_p(G(N;m)) over admissible rows is the least r >= 1 with m < p^r, with constructive attainment proved before the least extremal row T is used. It then proves, for every prime p and a >= 2, the exact least-row formula T_p(p^a+1) = p^(3a)+1.

records.name: discrete_carleson_stein_wainger
records.entry_name: Formalization of a discrete Carleson theorem of Stein-Wainger type
records.doc: This is a Lean 4 formalization of the main theorem of the papers arXiv:1907.00405 and arXiv:2107.14616 by Ben Krause and Joris Roos. The result concerns l^p boundedness for a  discrete maximal singular oscillatory operator of Stein-Wainger type, also called a discrete Carleson operator.

records.name: PDTGeometry.jointClassification
records.entry_name: Metric–Pfaffian Stabilizers and Fixed-Hodge Field Recovery
records.doc: For the explicit bivector metric induced by diag(1,1,1,-1,1,-1) and the Pfaffian cubic on fifteen real coordinates, the joint infinitesimal stabilizer is exactly the uniquely parameterized fifteen-dimensional orthogonal adjoint span. Under the metric condition, ninety specified cubic derivative checks certify preservation at every point. Within the joint stabilizer, commutation with a displayed local Lorentz Hodge operator is equivalent to annihilating its complementary reference and yields a unique six-plus-one decomposition, of dimension seven. Within this fixed-Hodge space, exactly the complementary line acts trivially on all extracted four-plane fields; six specified scalar readings reconstruct the entire visible action. The contribution is the explicit constructive classification and recovery certificates, situated in classical Pfaffian-preserver theory. The metric, cubic and four-plane are supplied data. PDT motivates the construction; selecting a physical coupling is outside these claims.

records.doc: For the explicit bivector metric induced by diag(1,1,1,-1,1,-1) and the Pfaffian cubic on fifteen real coordinates, the joint infinitesimal stabilizer is exactly the uniquely parameterized fifteen-dimensional orthogonal adjoint span. Under the metric condition, ninety specified cubic derivative checks certify preservation at every point. Within the joint stabilizer, commutation with a displayed local Lorentz Hodge operator is equivalent to annihilating its complementary reference and yields a unique six-plus-one decomposition, of dimension seven. Within this fixed-Hodge space, exactly the complementary line acts trivially on all extracted four-plane fields; six specified scalar readings reconstruct the entire visible action. The contribution is the explicit constructive classification and recovery certificates, situated in classical Pfaffian-preserver theory. The metric, cubic and four-plane are supplied data. PDT motivates the construction; selecting a physical coupling is outside these claims.

records.name: CountablyInfiniteCrystallineMeasures.exhaustiveCardinalClaim
records.entry_name: A complete crystalline-measure space of countably infinite Hamel dimension
records.doc: There exists a locally finite set Λ in the real line such that the complete complex vector space of tempered distributions locally given by atomic measures on Λ, whose distributional Fourier transforms are also locally atomic on Λ, has Hamel dimension ℵ₀. A countable family gives a unique finite linear expansion of every admissible distribution, and every finite expansion is admissible. The theorem includes the equivalence between a Schwartz-vanishing-ideal definition and the local atomic formulas on both Fourier sides. Temperedness is distributional; no additional polynomial total-variation bound is assumed. This is an exhaustive occurrence result for one constructed carrier, not a classification of arbitrary carriers.

records.doc: Formalization of 18 claims from manuscript Theorems A, B, C, E (extension direction), F, G, H (hierarchy inclusions and characteristic-zero strictness), I, and J. records.name: OptimalAffinity.optimalAffinity_seedLowerBound_false
records.entry_name: A two-reaction counterexample to the gross-amplification affinity bound
records.doc: Despons, De Decker and Lacoste (https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.02366, conjecture following Eq. (33)) proposed that the affinity at maximum production flux is bounded below by the logarithm of the gross amplification ratio in seed-dependent autocatalytic networks. A two-species reversible mass-action counterexample is given by X ⇌ Y with forward/reverse rates (3, 2) and 2Y ⇌ 2X + Y with rates (7, 6). On the positive Y-stationary set, the production current has its unique global maximum at (X, Y) = (1, 1). At this point the exponential of the overall affinity is 7/4, strictly below the gross amplification ratio 2. The network has positive rates, an invertible net stoichiometric matrix, unit production mode and a positive detailed-balance state. The formal theorem establishes the counterexample; the correspondence with the published conjecture is supplied by the witness’s stationary branch and reactant matrix, together with the source’s affinity and chemostat conventions.

records.name: PlankProblem.ball_plank_theorem
records.entry_name: A Short Proof of Ball's Plank Theorem
records.doc: Formalization in Lean 4 of the paper 'A Short Proof of Ball's Plank Theorem' by Arseniy Akopyan and Alexander Polyanskii (arXiv:2609.36163). The paper gives a short proof of Keith Ball's 1991 theorem: if a centrally symmetric convex body in R^d is covered by finitely many planks, the sum of their relative widths with respect to the body is at least 1. The proof is based on a simple proof of a core theorem about linear functionals on R^n and an orthonormal basis. It also yields a short proof of Davenport's problem for centrally symmetric convex bodies (interior-disjointness of a homothet K/(n+1) from n hyperplanes).
