records.name: GreedyUniformity.tree_greedyLawEqUniform_iff_isK1OrK2
records.entry_name: Greedy Uniformity on Trees
records.doc: Formalization of exact distributional results for the random-permutation greedy maximal-independent-set process on finite trees. For every finite nonempty tree, the complete greedy output law is uniform over maximal independent sets exactly for K1 and K2. For the mixed-spider family T_{k,l}, the development counts maximal independent sets, proves exact output probabilities, and for l=2^k-k proves positive total-variation bias with decay O(sqrt(k)/4^k), equivalently O(sqrt(log n_k)/n_k^2) along n_k=2^k+k+1. The Stage-4 novelty classification is "plausibly new with bounded uncertainty"; no worldwide-priority, global-optimality, matching lower-bound, all-n extremal, or other stronger claim is made.

records.name: Minimax.Palomar.maxmin_le_minmax
records.entry_name: minimax-theorem-lean
records.doc: A Lean formalization of von Neumann's 1928 finite two-player zero-sum minimax theorem, a foundation of modern game theory and a cornerstone of mathematical economics. Nash equilibrium existence builds directly on its mixed-strategy solution concept by extending equilibrium existence beyond the two-player zero-sum case; this is historical motivation, not a claimed Lean proof of Nash's theorem. The formal result is Minimax.minimax_theorem {A B : Type*} [Fintype A] [Fintype B] [Nonempty A] [Nonempty B] (u : A → B → ℝ) : maxminValue u = minmaxValue u. The reported Palomar registry API search on 2026-09-29 for "minimax" returned zero entries. The M1 Mathlib survey found no finite zero-sum game specialization in the pinned Mathlib, whose general Sion saddle-point theorem is reused here.

records.name: LocalConjugacy.theorem_1_1
records.entry_name: Local conjugacy in prosolvable groups
records.doc: Lean 4 formalization of all eleven numbered results and both counterexamples in Local conjugacy in prosolvable groups, arXiv:2609.37678v1. Closed supplements of a pronilpotent normal subgroup are conjugate exactly when locally conjugate under the stated structural hypotheses. Continuous nonabelian cohomology has the stated primary restriction decomposition. Local inclusion and fixed-point results, the GL(2,3) quaternion counterexample, and the order-162 Heisenberg wreath-product counterexample are formalized.

Continuous nonabelian cohomology has the stated primary restriction decomposition. records.name: DiscriminativeKalmanFilter.theorem2
records.entry_name: Discriminative Kalman Filter Formalized
records.doc: Asymptotic correctness of the discriminative Kalman filter for a stationary linear Gaussian state model with nonlinear and non-Gaussian observations. Formalizes Appendix B, Theorem 2, Lemma 1, and Remarks 1–4 of Burkhart et al. (2020): weak convergence, eventual Gaussian well-definedness, L1 consistency, the exact Gaussian parameter update, the robust update, and the extension to random input distributions with convergence in probability.

records.name: Roberts.roberts_theorem
records.entry_name: roberts-theorem-lean
records.doc: A Lean formalization of Roberts theorem: for finite nonempty agent and alternative types with at least three alternatives, every onto dominant-strategy incentive compatible choice function is an affine maximizer. The proof follows the modular route: the taxation principle and weak monotonicity, reduction to strong monotonicity by tie-breaking, no-veto-power range analysis, the two-agent affine price representation, and induction on the number of agents.

records.name: VCG.vcg_greenLaffont
records.entry_name: vcg-mechanism-lean
records.doc: A Lean formalization of the Green-Laffont characterization: for finite, nonempty agent and alternative types, efficiency and dominant-strategy incentive compatibility imply that payments have Groves form. The project also verifies four standard properties of the finite VCG mechanism with Clarke pivot payments.

records.name: gleason_theorem_finite
records.entry_name: gleason-finite-lean
records.doc: A machine-checked proof of Gleason's theorem in finite dimensions. On a complex Hilbert space of dimension at least 3, every frame function on the orthogonal projections has the form P ↦ Re Tr(ρP) for exactly one density operator ρ. The statement is Kim Morrison's lean-eval problem gleason_theorem_finite, unchanged. The proof follows Cooke, Keane and Moran's elementary proof of Gleason's core lemma for matrices on ℂᴺ, then moves the result to operators by taking matrices in an orthonormal basis.

records.name: RevenueEquivalence.Palomar.envelope_integral
records.entry_name: revenue-equivalence-lean
records.doc: A Lean formalization of Myerson's 1981 revenue equivalence theorem in a single-parameter Bayesian mechanism-design model with continuous real types. The formal result is RevenueEquivalence.Palomar.revenueEquivalence (X P1 P2 : ℝ → ℝ) (h1 : BIC X P1) (h2 : BIC X P2) (hU : interimUtility X P1 0 = interimUtility X P2 0) (t : ℝ) (ht : 0 ≤ t) : P1 t = P2 t: two Bayesian incentive-compatible mechanisms with the same interim allocation rule and the same interim utility at the reference type (type zero) charge the same interim payments at every nonnegative type. Types range over all of ℝ; there is no lowest type, and zero is only the normalization point for the payment identity. The envelope lemma RevenueEquivalence.Palomar.envelope_integral and the expected-revenue corollary RevenueEquivalence.Palomar.expectedRevenueEqual are proved alongside; the corollary requires both interim payment rules to be integrable with respect to the prior ((hInt1 : Integrable P1 μ) (hInt2 : Integrable P2 μ)), so its conclusion is an equality of finite expected revenues rather than a vacuous totalized-integral identity. The Palomar registry API search on 2026-10-01 for "revenue equivalence" returned zero entries; the queries "Myerson" and "auction" returned only different theorems (see related_formalizations note). These are dated, limited observations, not universal prior-art claims.

records.name: MyersonOptimalAuction.Palomar.virtualSurplusIdentity
records.entry_name: Myerson's Optimal Auction Theorem
records.doc: A Lean formalization of Myerson's 1981 optimal auction theorem, regular case, in a single-parameter independent-private-values model with real types. Finitely many bidders draw independent types from TypeDist priors: probability measures on ℝ with a continuous monotone CDF and a nonnegative Lebesgue density that vanishes for negative types, so each prior's mass lies on [0, ∞). The formal results are MyersonOptimalAuction.Palomar.virtualSurplusIdentity: under BIC, the support hypothesis (hsupp : ∀ t : ℝ, 0 < t → 0 < D.F t, i.e. the prior puts positive mass in (0, t] for every t > 0 so zero is in the support), and five integrability hypotheses, the expected payment equals the expected virtual surplus minus the interim utility at the reference type (type zero), expectedPayment p D = expectedVirtualSurplus x D - interimUtility x p 0; and MyersonOptimalAuction.Palomar.optimalAuction: for regular priors (hreg : Regular D, i.e. each bidder's virtual value ψ(t) = t - (1 - F t) / f t is nondecreasing on nonnegative types), the auction that allocates the item to the least-index bidder attaining the highest virtual value whenever that value is strictly positive (no sale otherwise), with envelope payments normalized to zero utility at type zero, is Bayesian incentive compatible and interim individually rational, and raises at least as much expected revenue as any feasible BIC and interim-IR mechanism. Independence is the product measure over type profiles; feasibility is pointwise (∑ i, X i t ≤ 1 for every profile t). Types range over all of ℝ; zero is only the reference/normalization type, never a lowest type. The Bochner integrals defining expectations are totalized, so every expectation claim carries the integrability hypotheses that make it non-vacuous. Ironing for irregular distributions is out of scope. The Palomar registry API searches on 2026-10-01 for "optimal auction", "virtual surplus", and "virtual value" returned no existing Myerson optimal auction formalization ("optimal auction" matched only PALOMAR-2026-10-01-000007, Bulow-Klemperer, a different theorem). These are dated, limited observations, not universal prior-art claims.

records.name: FailureOfComposition.Palomar.obstruction_four_properties
records.entry_name: Pointwise provable equality and the failure of composition
records.doc: In their study of pathologies in recursion categories, Montagna (1989) and Di Paola–Montagna (1991) introduce the algebraic systems S′ and S′_T, respectively, and claim that they are categories. We show that the proposed composition is not independent of the choice of representatives. For every consistent recursively enumerable extension T of Peano arithmetic (PA), we exhibit two unary programs whose partial functions are provably equal in T, separately at each standard input. Composing each after a program that searches for a T-proof of contradiction and returns its code yields programs that are not equivalent in this sense. An alternative proof uses the productivity of the complement of the diagonal halting set. Montagna's S′ is the case T = PA. More generally, for consistent T ⊇ PA, pointwise provable equality is a composition congruence exactly when T proves every true Π⁰₁ sentence, in which case it is extensional equality. This completeness condition fails for every consistent recursively enumerable T ⊇ PA by Gödel's second incompleteness theorem. For every extension T ⊇ PA, the least composition congruence containing pointwise provable equality is extensional equality if T is Σ⁰₁-sound and the universal relation otherwise.

records.doc: In their study of pathologies in recursion categories, Montagna (1989) and Di Paola–Montagna (1991) introduce the algebraic systems S′ and S′_T, respectively, and claim that they are categories. We show that the proposed composition is not independent of the choice of representatives. For every consistent recursively enumerable extension T of Peano arithmetic (PA), we exhibit two unary programs whose partial functions are provably equal in T, separately at each standard input. Composing each after a program that searches for a T-proof of contradiction and returns its code yields programs that are not equivalent in this sense. An alternative proof uses the productivity of the complement of the diagonal halting set. Montagna's S′ is the case T = PA. More generally, for consistent T ⊇ PA, pointwise provable equality is a composition congruence exactly when T proves every true Π⁰₁ sentence, in which case it is extensional equality. This completeness condition fails for every consistent recursively enumerable T ⊇ PA by Gödel's second incompleteness theorem. For every extension T ⊇ PA, the least composition congruence containing pointwise provable equality is extensional equality if T is Σ⁰₁-sound and the universal relation otherwise.

records.name: Av12453.count_1342_literal
records.entry_name: Counting recurrences for the permutation classes Av(1342) and Av(12453)
records.doc: For a permutation pattern τ, let Av_n(τ) be the set of permutations of length n that avoid τ.  This formalization proves, for every n, that four recurrences from the source paper compute |Av_n(1342)| and |Av_n(12453)|. For 1342 they are the one-threshold recurrence W and the scalar kernel recurrence G, and for 12453 the literal two-threshold recurrence H and the transfer-kernel recurrence G.  These are the cases d = 1 and d = 2 of the paper's counting recurrences for the classes Av(12...d ⊕ 231), the direct sum of an increasing pattern and 231, whose kernel form gives polynomial-time algorithms for every fixed d (the complexity bounds themselves are not formalized).  The counting sequence of Av(1342) has been known since Bóna (1997).  That of Av(12453) was previously known only up to n = 38, from a program of Biers-Ariel that evaluates the recurrence H, and the paper uses its kernel algorithm to compute it up to n = 150 (that computation is not formalized).

records.name: TTC.Palomar.ttcTerminates
records.entry_name: Gale's Top Trading Cycles (Shapley-Scarf Housing Market)
records.doc: A Lean formalization of Gale's top trading cycles algorithm (1974) for the Shapley-Scarf housing market. Finitely many agents (Fin n) each own exactly one house (the endowment is a bijection endow : Fin n ≃ Fin n) and have strict preferences over houses, given most-preferred-first as per-agent permutations rank i : Fin n ≃ Fin n; agent i strictly prefers house a over house b iff (rank i).symm a < (rank i).symm b. The comparator-checked results are TTC.Palomar.ttcTerminates: the TTC procedure (each remaining agent points to the owner of their favourite remaining house, each house points to its owner; each round removes the single directed cycle reachable from a chosen remaining agent, whose members trade and leave) removes every agent within n rounds, since each round deletes at least one nonempty directed cycle from the finite functional pointing graph. This one-cycle-at-a-time form computes the same allocation as the simultaneous version (see the remark in README.md); TTC.Palomar.ttcInCore: the TTC allocation is in the ordinary core, i.e. no coalition S can reallocate its own endowments (Set.BijOn y S (M.endow '' S)) so that every member strictly prefers the deviation; TTC.Palomar.ttcUniqueStrictCore: strict-core uniqueness, i.e. for (x : Fin n → Fin n) with (hxb : Function.Bijective x) and (hx : StrictCore M x) the conclusion is x = ttcAllocation M. This is uniqueness among bijective strict-core allocations (no coalition can weakly block), not a singleton claim about the ordinary core. The library also proves the TTC allocation Pareto optimal (TTC.ttcPareto), individually rational (TTC.ttcIR), in the strict core (TTC.ttcInStrictCore), and strategyproof (TTC.ttcStrategyproof, Roth 1982: no unilateral misreport is profitable); these four are library-only and are not on the comparator surface. The Palomar registry API was searched on 2026-10-01 for "top trading cycles", "housing market", "shapley scarf", "TTC", and "trading cycles" and returned no existing TTC formalization among 397 entries; this is a dated, limited observation, not a universal prior-art claim.

records.name: Rochet.pathWeights_nonempty
records.entry_name: Rochet's Cyclic-Monotonicity Characterization
records.doc: For any nonempty report type T, any outcome type X, any real-valued valuation v : T -> X -> Real and allocation f : T -> X, DSIC payments exist exactly when every finite closed walk has nonnegative sum of weights l(s,t) = v(t,f(t)) - v(t,f(s)). The proof constructs payments as the infimum of finite path weights from a fixed anchor. Direct edges establish nonemptiness; a return edge supplies an explicit real lower bound before using the infimum's order properties. The payments are zero at the anchor and satisfy every implementing difference inequality. The characterization also holds for arbitrary agents with heterogeneous nonempty report spaces and decidable agent equality, by fixing other reports and assembling anchored slice payments. A three-type example satisfies all two-cycle inequalities but has a negative three-cycle and admits no DSIC payment.

records.name: HordijkSteelThreshold.palomar_critical_window_variable_intensity
records.entry_name: A nontrivial critical window for RAF emergence in the binary polymer model
records.doc: Hordijk and Steel (https://arxiv.org/abs/1605.03919, Section 7, Eq. (21)) conjectured a zero-one threshold for RAF emergence at linear mean catalysis. In the uniform reversible binary-polymer model with split-position reaction identities and food consisting of monomers and dimers, a nontrivial limiting law is established. Each molecule independently catalyzes each reaction, with one catalysis coordinate shared by both directions. If the mean catalysis parameter f(n) satisfies f(n)/n → λ > 0, the probability of a reflexively autocatalytic and food-generated (RAF) set converges to L(λ). The function L is continuous and nondecreasing, with 0 < L(λ) ≤ 1 − exp(−36λ) < 1. Thus no finite positive threshold separates limiting RAF probability zero from one in this model.

records.name: UnitDistanceSqrt241Submission.target_of_wide_zeta_bound
records.entry_name: An Exponent of 1.043 for the Unit Distance Problem: Lean formalization at exponent 1.04315, conditional on one zeta inequality
records.doc: Lean formalization accompanying the paper An Exponent of 1.043 for the Unit Distance Problem by Eric Naslund (cited under sources), which proves the exponent 1.043171 unconditionally with a computer-assisted certificate. Conditional theorem on unit distances in the Euclidean plane. Let B = Q(sqrt 241) and let E be the number field of degree 512 generated over Q by sqrt 241 and square roots of the eight elements -1, -71011068 + 4574225 sqrt 241, (-6101 - 393 sqrt 241)/2, (6101 - 393 sqrt 241)/2, 31 - 2 sqrt 241, 31 + 2 sqrt 241, 326 - 21 sqrt 241 and 326 + 21 sqrt 241 of B (a basis of the {2,3,5}-units of B modulo squares). Let E_W be the field of degree 8192 obtained from E by adjoining square roots of four explicit elements beta_1, ..., beta_4 of E, each generating with two of the square roots a dihedral extension of B of degree 8 (the elements are written out in the Challenge). Hypothesis (H_W) is one displayed numerical inequality for the Dedekind zeta function of E_W: log(Re zeta_{E_W}(1 + 1/4411))/8192 + (1/4411)((L - gamma - log(4 pi))/4 - Re((zeta_{E_W}'/zeta_{E_W})(2))/8192) < 50969/1000000, where L = (9/4) log 2 + (1/2) log 3615 and gamma is Euler's constant. The compared theorem proves that (H_W) implies the existence of finite sets U_j in the plane with |U_j| -> infinity such that the number of unordered pairs of points of U_j at distance one, divided by |U_j|^(20863/20000), tends to infinity. The exponent is exactly 20863/20000 = 1.04315. The conclusion is a sequence statement only; no bound at every sufficiently large cardinality is asserted. The infinite pro-2 tower over B with Frobenius caps at both primes above 29 and at one prime above 41 (generators, relation bound, presentation, Golod-Shafarevich infinitude, local data), its fields, which are Galois over B and over a fixed base field but not over Q, their local types and signature, the root-discriminant bound, the field E_W with its degree, its embedding in the base field and its local data, the passage from (H_W) to the analytic ceiling, the numerical margin and the planar construction are proved in Lean over Mathlib; (H_W) itself is not proved. Outside Lean, a rigorous computation (certified values of the 576 L-functions of degrees 4 and 8 in the factorization of zeta_{E_W} and an Euler product with explicit tail) bounds the left side of (H_W) by 0.0509172; that computation is not part of the formal proof. The earlier formalization registered as PALOMAR-2026-10-01-000018 version 1 proved the exponent 10427/10000 from a different inequality, for the field E.

records.name: Border.border_feasibility
records.entry_name: Border's Finite Auction Feasibility Theorem
records.doc: For arbitrary finite bidders with heterogeneous finite type spaces, a nonnegative normalized real joint prior, and an interim allocation rule with values in [0,1], a randomized allocation of at most one item realizes the weighted interim masses if and only if every collection of bidder-specific type subsets satisfies Border's union-probability inequality. Weighted feasibility is proved equivalent to conditional feasibility on positive marginal support. Null-type interim values remain unrestricted within [0,1]. For a product of nonnegative normalized distributions, the independent-prior corollary has right side 1 minus the product of the complementary marginal probabilities. Full real-valued sufficiency is proved by finite threshold decomposition and compact convex separation; no sufficiency oracle is assumed.

records.entry_name: Border's Finite Auction Feasibility Theorem
records.doc: For arbitrary finite bidders with heterogeneous finite type spaces, a nonnegative normalized real joint prior, and an interim allocation rule with values in [0,1], a randomized allocation of at most one item realizes the weighted interim masses if and only if every collection of bidder-specific type subsets satisfies Border's union-probability inequality. Weighted feasibility is proved equivalent to conditional feasibility on positive marginal support. Null-type interim values remain unrestricted within [0,1]. For a product of nonnegative normalized distributions, the independent-prior corollary has right side 1 minus the product of the complementary marginal probabilities. Full real-valued sufficiency is proved by finite threshold decomposition and compact convex separation; no sufficiency oracle is assumed.

records.name: GradedNear.graded_near_lemma
records.entry_name: Linnik's constant is at most 3.99: A formalization of a weighted version of Heath-Brown's near-density estimate, and of the proof's certificate checker
records.doc: Two components of the proof, in the paper "Linnik's constant is at most 3.99" (paper/linnik399.pdf in this repository), that every reduced residue class modulo q contains a prime below q^3.99 for all large q. That bound itself is NOT formally verified here: the paper's zero-location arguments, case analysis and exterior regimes have conventional proofs and computer checks only. (1) The graded near lemma: fix test data (a detector f satisfying Heath-Brown's Condition 1, a Gram test g satisfying his Conditions 1 and 2, a Selberg-sieve weight with heights h_k >= 0 on cells [t_k, t_{k+1}) with t_0 > 1/3 + 2 eps', finitely many nonnegative anchor offsets, a positive lower bound for the weight omega where f is nonzero, and I_B > 0) and eta > 0. For all large q, take a finite family of entries (chi_j, gamma_j, delta_j) of non-principal characters mod q with heights |gamma_j| <= T <= (log q)/3 and a safe anchor at height 2T+1, whose characters are pairwise distinct whenever some sieve height h_k is nonzero (condition (iii) of the paper's Theorem 8.4; without sieve weights a character may repeat, and repeated characters enter through the pair excess e_j). Then the prime-sum responses satisfy (sum_j a_j R_j)_+^2 <= (1+eta) I_B [sum_j (D(delta_j) - d_1 + e_j) a_j^2 + (d_1 + eta)(sum_j a_j)^2] for all a_j >= 0. This is a weighted version of Heath-Brown's Lemma 12.1 (1992), which Heath-Brown remarks (section 16, item 9) no neat way of achieving "seems available". Its zero form: the response lemma (a response is bounded below by the zeros it keeps, via the local explicit formula), the threshold form exists tau: sum_j (v_j - tau)_+^2 / D_j <= 1 - tau^2/d with features computed from kept zeros, provided every diagonal numerator D(delta_j) - d_1 + e_j is positive, the entry bounds F(hi - s_j) of the rows, the normalization used by the leaf builders, and the vanishing of the pair excess for separated same-character pairs. (2) The leaf LPs: an exact integer checker for the certificates of the leaf linear programs (bisection trees over threshold boxes, first-order and tangent relaxations with safe rounding, exclusions, weak duality with a free dual) is proved sound: if it accepts a certificate with value v, every feasible point of the LP has objective at most v < 10^16. A bridge lemma turns the threshold form into the LP's near rows. Seven certificates (six leaves of the 3.99 corpus and the program of the large first-zero range) are checked by the kernel (decide +kernel) in the repository (not part of the compared theorems). The analytic part is conditional on four published estimates, stated as explicit hypotheses in the Challenge, each no stronger than its source: Xylouris's Lemmas 3.1 and 3.2 (= Heath-Brown's Lemmas 5.3 and 5.2), Burgess's character-sum bound with k = 3 as printed for primitive characters (Heath-Brown's Lemma 2.1; the form for all non-principal characters is derived), and Graham's asymptotic for Selberg-sieve sums. Mertens' estimate, Abel and partial summation, the Selberg majorant, the decay of Laplace transforms, the finiteness and multiplicities of zeros in a disc, the equality of multiplicities of conjugate zeros for real characters, and all error bookkeeping are proved.

records.name: PhamSauermann.theorem_1_2
records.entry_name: On Graham's rearrangement conjecture (Pham–Sauermann)
records.doc: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of H. T. Pham and L. Sauermann, "On Graham's rearrangement conjecture" (arXiv:2602.15797v1). Graham conjectured in 1971 that for every prime p, every subset S of Z_p \ {0} has an ordering whose partial sums are pairwise distinct. The formalization proves the paper's main theorem (Theorem 1.2): for every 0 < α < 1 there is a constant C_α > 0 such that, for every prime p, every S ⊆ Z_p \ {0} with C_α ≤ |S| ≤ p^(1-α) has such an ordering. It also proves the paper's anticoncentration bounds for the sum of a uniformly random m-element subset R of a set S ⊆ Z_p with |S| ≥ 2: the probability that the sum of R equals any given z is at most 1/p + C/(|S|√m), for an absolute constant C > 0, when C log|S| ≤ m ≤ 10^-3 |S|/log|S| (Theorem 1.3), and, for every 0 < ε < 1, at most 1/p + C_ε √(log|S|)/(|S|√m) for every positive integer m ≤ (1-ε)|S| (Corollary 1.4). Every result that the paper proves is formalized, following its argument, and so are the two hypergeometric tail bounds that its proofs take from the Chernoff bound of Janson, Łuczak and Ruciński.

records.name: SquaresInCircles.optimal_radius
records.entry_name: Optimal packings of one to seven unit squares in a disk
records.doc: For n = 1, …, 7: the least radius of a closed disk holding n unit squares with disjoint interiors, each placed and rotated freely, and every packing that attains it. The radii are √2/2, √5/2, 5√17/16, √2, √(5/2), √q* ≈ 1.68854 and √13/2, where q* is a quartic irrational. Up to rotation about the disk centre and relabelling, the optimal packing is unique for n ≤ 6: the square, the 2 × 1 rectangle, the T, the 2 × 2 block, the plus, and for six squares a central square with four neighbours, two of them pushed along its sides, and a sixth square turned by π/4 between those two. For n = 7 the optimal packings form a three-parameter family: two columns of two squares and, between them, a column of three whose heights vary independently, at least 1 apart and within √3 − 1/2 of the disk centre. The proofs for three to six squares bound the arcs the squares occupy on a small circle about the disk centre. For six squares this finds the square that contains the disk centre; five fixed points label the others, and a weighted sum of separating inequalities, with estimates uniform in the angles of the squares, forces the optimal radius. For seven squares, each square avoiding the disk centre gets a direction from it, and in the optimal disk two disjoint such squares get directions at least π/3 apart. We found no earlier proof for five, six or seven squares, and no exact one for three, where a computer-assisted enclosure of the radius and the optimal arrangements was known. Four squares, uniqueness included, were settled by hand in 2026, by the same idea as here.

records.name: CremerMcLean.separating_lottery
records.entry_name: Cremer-McLean Full Surplus Extraction Theorem
records.doc: A Lean 4 formalization of the Cremer-McLean full surplus extraction theorem (Econometrica, 1988): for a single indivisible object with finitely many bidders, finite type spaces, and a correlated joint prior with full support, if every bidder's family of conditional distributions over the others' types is convex independent (no conditional lies in the convex hull of the rest), then there exists a Bayesian incentive compatible, interim individually rational direct mechanism that allocates ex post efficiently and extracts the full surplus: every bidder's interim expected utility is zero, so expected seller revenue equals the expected maximum value. The proof hinges on constructing side-bet lotteries with zero own-conditional expectation and strictly positive cross-conditional expectation, obtained by strict separation of each conditional from the convex hull of the others, scaled to dominate any misreport gain.

records.name: Erdos274.Palomar.herzog_schonheim_solvable
records.entry_name: The Herzog–Schönheim conjecture for solvable groups
records.doc: A Lean 4 formalization of the Herzog–Schönheim conjecture (the index form, which implies the cardinality form asked in Erdős problem 274) for every solvable group, finite or infinite: if a solvable group is partitioned into finitely many, and at least two, left cosets of subgroups, then two of the subgroups have the same index (hence, in the cardinality form, the same cardinality). The conjecture for arbitrary groups is open and is not claimed. The infinite case reduces to a finite solvable quotient by the common core of the parts; the finite case is proved for a least counterexample by considering its largest prime divisor p, using the subgroup generated by the p-prime-part elements, divisibility restrictions on local indices obtained from fixed-point counts in a primitive solvable quotient, and an extra closure argument at p = 7. The statements use the same exact covering structure as the formal-conjectures file for Erdős problem 274.

records.name: Maskin.maskin_necessity
records.entry_name: maskin-nash-implementation-lean
records.doc: Lean 4 formalization of Maskin's theorem on Nash implementation: necessity of Maskin monotonicity and sufficiency of monotonicity plus no-veto power via the canonical mechanism. Alternatives form a finite nonempty type, agents are indexed by Fin n, preferences are complete preorders, and the social choice correspondence is nonempty-valued. Sufficiency requires at least three agents; implementation is in pure strategies.

records.name: AGV.agv_efficient
records.entry_name: agv-mechanism-lean
records.doc: Lean 4 formalization of the AGV (d'Aspremont-Gérard-Varet-Arrow) expected-externality mechanism: with independent types, ex post efficiency, Bayesian incentive compatibility, and budget balance are jointly attainable. Agents are indexed by Fin n with 2 ≤ n; each agent has a finite nonempty type space with an independent PMF prior; alternatives form a finite nonempty type; values are private. The efficient rule xmax maximizes utilitarian welfare, and agvTransfer pays each agent its expected externality minus an equal share of the other agents' receipts. Interim individual rationality is not claimed.

records.name: BayesCorrelated.finite_characterization
records.entry_name: Finite Bayes Correlated Equilibrium, Information Expansions and Information Order
records.doc: Bergemann–Morris Theorem 1 for arbitrary finite players and states with heterogeneous action and original-signal spaces: a normalized decision rule is obedient if and only if a finite marginal-preserving information expansion supports a valid mixed Bayes–Nash strategy profile inducing its joint law. The recommendation expansion and the converse for arbitrary extra signals and independent behavioral randomization are proved. Null fibers are handled without conditioning, and exact induction is equivalent to the paper's positive-support quotient. Zero prior masses are permitted, extending the paper's full-support assumption. The one-player decision-problem specialization and explicit examples are included. Theorem 2 proves that individual sufficiency is equivalent to BCE outcome inclusion across all finite basic games with arbitrary heterogeneous actions and utilities and full-support common priors, on a nonempty finite state space. Its converse constructs actual couplings from finite quadratic-scoring games and weighted compactness.

The recommendation expansion and the converse for arbitrary extra signals and independent behavioral randomization are proved. Null fibers are handled without conditioning, and exact induction is equivalent to the paper's positive-support quotient. Zero prior masses are permitted, extending the paper's full-support assumption. The one-player decision-problem specialization and explicit examples are included. Theorem 2 proves that individual sufficiency is equivalent to BCE outcome inclusion across all finite basic games with arbitrary heterogeneous actions and utilities and full-support common priors, on a nonempty finite state space. Its converse constructs actual couplings from finite quadratic-scoring games and weighted compactness.

records.name: Baek.gerver_params_exists
records.entry_name: Optimality, uniqueness and stability of Gerver's sofa from one coercive certificate, formalized in Lean 4
records.doc:
The moving sofa problem asks for the largest area of a planar shape that can be moved around the right-angled corner of a hallway of unit width. Jineon Baek proved (arXiv:2411.19826) that Gerver's sofa G, of area 2.2195..., is optimal. His proof bounds the area of every large moving sofa by a concave functional Q of a triple (K, B, D) of convex bodies built from a cap K of the sofa, and shows that Q is largest at Gerver's triple, where it equals |G|.

This entry proves one estimate for Q, the coercive certificate, and derives three results from it. On an enlarged domain of triples, on which the cap need not satisfy Baek's injectivity condition, Q(K, B, D) <= |G|, and the cap K lies within Euclidean Hausdorff distance 2 sec(phi) sqrt(|G| - Q(K, B, D)) of the horizontal translate of Gerver's cap with the same leftmost point, where phi = 0.039... is Gerver's angle. The proof writes |G| - Q as a sum of nonnegative terms, and the energy terms among them also bound that distance. The bound is attained: Gerver's triple lies in the enlarged domain, and Q equals |G| there.

From the certificate: optimality, Baek's theorem, proved without his Theorem 1.1.1 and without the balance argument of his Chapters 4 to 6; uniqueness, every moving sofa with the area of G is mapped onto G by a rotation and a translation (a translation suffices); and stability, after a translation a moving sofa of area |G| - epsilon lies within Euclidean Hausdorff distance C sqrt(epsilon) of G, their symmetric difference has area at most C' sqrt(epsilon), its rotation angle misses a right angle by at most C'' epsilon, and the exponent 1/2 cannot be improved. The Challenge also states the correspondence between Baek's definitions and those of Google DeepMind's formal-conjectures, and formal-conjectures' statements, among them the uniqueness, which it lists as open; here they are proved through the certificate.

Versions 1 to 4 of this entry registered the formalization of Baek's paper with a first proof of uniqueness that uses his Theorem 1.1.1; they state the same optimality, uniqueness and formal-conjectures theorems, proved through Baek's argument, and the repository keeps their Challenge and Solution in baek/. This version proves those theorems through the certificate and adds the certificate and the stability. A script in the repository, scripts/AuditCoerciveRoute.lean, run by the continuous integration, checks that its proofs reach neither Baek's Theorem 1.1.1, nor the results of his balance argument, nor the main theorem and the equality analysis of the first proof of uniqueness.

records.entry_name: Optimality, uniqueness and stability of Gerver's sofa from one coercive certificate, formalized in Lean 4
records.doc:
The moving sofa problem asks for the largest area of a planar shape that can be moved around the right-angled corner of a hallway of unit width. Jineon Baek proved (arXiv:2411.19826) that Gerver's sofa G, of area 2.2195..., is optimal. His proof bounds the area of every large moving sofa by a concave functional Q of a triple (K, B, D) of convex bodies built from a cap K of the sofa, and shows that Q is largest at Gerver's triple, where it equals |G|.

This entry proves one estimate for Q, the coercive certificate, and derives three results from it. On an enlarged domain of triples, on which the cap need not satisfy Baek's injectivity condition, Q(K, B, D) <= |G|, and the cap K lies within Euclidean Hausdorff distance 2 sec(phi) sqrt(|G| - Q(K, B, D)) of the horizontal translate of Gerver's cap with the same leftmost point, where phi = 0.039... is Gerver's angle. records.name: AVChallenge.anomalous_dissipation_full
records.entry_name: Anomalous diffusion by fractal homogenization
records.doc: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of S. Armstrong and V. Vicol, "Anomalous diffusion by fractal homogenization" (arXiv:2305.05048). For every alpha in (0, 1/3) it constructs one divergence-free, Z^2-periodic drift b in C^0_t C^{0,alpha}_x intersect C^{0,alpha}_t C^0_x on [0,1] x T^2, and proves three properties of the advection-diffusion equation with this drift: anomalous dissipation of scalar variance for every mean-zero H^1 datum (Theorem 1.1 of the paper); a uniform C^{0,mu}([0,1]; L^2) bound by C times the H^1 norm of the datum along a set of diffusivities accumulating at zero (Remark r.LeBron.2); and non-uniqueness of vanishing-diffusivity limits for a class of data containing cos(2 pi n x_1) for infinitely many n (a corrected form of the paper's no-selection principle). The three properties are combined in one theorem, restated in a Mathlib-only comparator challenge. The formalization also proves existence and uniqueness of weak solutions and the classical facts the paper uses without proof.

records.name: GGKMS.finite_bayesian_dominant_equivalence
records.entry_name: Finite Bayesian-to-Dominant-Strategy Equivalence
records.doc: Finite Gershkov–Goeree–Kushnir–Moldovanu–Shi (2013) Theorem 2 for arbitrary finite agents and alternatives, heterogeneous ordered finite scalar type supports, arbitrary independent positive support masses, and linear private values with nonnegative slopes and arbitrary constants. The library constructs a feasible dominant-strategy mechanism preserving every support type's interim expected utility and ex ante social surplus. Weighted monotone lifting is proved by a compact feasible quadratic minimizer and an improving perturbation. Adjacent transfer bounds imply full-report IC by telescoping. Selected results are finite equivalence, weighted monotone lifting and optimizer monotonicity; scalar IC and support-restriction facts remain in the library as supporting lemmas. Validation evidence is recorded separately for the exact candidate.

records.name: C4.theoremA_slice
records.entry_name: Uniqueness of four-body convex central configurations for all masses
records.doc: A Lean 4 and Mathlib formalization of Theorems A and B of arXiv:2609.35632 on the central configurations of the planar Newtonian four-body problem. For every choice of four positive masses and every cyclic order of the bodies there is exactly one strictly convex central configuration with that cyclic order, up to similarity, so there are exactly three convex central configurations up to similarity. This answers Problem 10 in the list of Albouy, Cabral and Santos (2012). The main step of the paper is Theorem B: at every strictly convex central configuration of positive masses, the Hessian form Q of U + (λ/2)I is at least one quarter of its radial part K. It follows that every convex central configuration is a nondegenerate local minimum of U I^(1/2), whose Hessian vanishes exactly on the tangent space of the orbit of the similarities. The computer-assisted step, a branch and bound with interval arithmetic over the three-dimensional set of normalized convex central configurations in the coordinates of Corbera, Cors and Roberts, proves tr S < 3/4 and is checked by Lean's kernel with `decide +kernel` in 7307 certificate theorems. No compiled code is trusted, and the proofs use only Lean's three standard axioms.

records.name: RAFReactionQuotient.palomar_quotient_critical_window
records.entry_name: Critical-window emergence of autocatalytic sets under reaction-channel quotienting
records.doc: Hordijk and Steel (https://arxiv.org/abs/1605.03919, Section 7, Eq. (21)) conjectured a zero-one threshold for RAF emergence at linear mean catalysis. An interior limiting law is established for the reversible binary-polymer model with monomer/dimer food and reaction channels obtained by identifying the split descriptions u + v and v + u precisely when uv = vu. Each molecule independently catalyzes each channel, with one catalysis coordinate shared by both directions. For every real sequence f(n)/n → λ > 0, the clamped channel parameter eventually equals f(n)/|J_n|, and the probability of a reflexively autocatalytic and food-generated (RAF) set converges to a limit L(λ) depending only on λ. The function L is nondecreasing and satisfies 0 < L(λ) ≤ 1 − exp(−34λ) < 1 at every positive finite intensity. Thus a zero-one step threshold is excluded in this channel model.

records.name: Complexity.sat_np_complete
records.entry_name: NP-completeness of SAT, 3-SAT and their variants (the Cook–Levin theorem) in Lean 4
records.doc:
A Lean 4 proof of the Cook–Levin theorem and of the NP-completeness of several variants of satisfiability, for an explicit machine model, using only Lean's core library. The compared theorems state that the following languages are NP-complete: SAT, the set of binary codes of satisfiable CNF formulas (Complexity.sat_np_complete); 3-SAT, with at most three literals per clause (threeSAT_np_complete); exactly-3-SAT, with exactly three literals per clause on three distinct variables (exactThreeSAT_np_complete); (≤1,≤2)-SAT, with two or three literals per clause and every variable occurring at most once positively and at most twice negatively (leOneLeTwoSAT_np_complete); SAT with variable indices written in binary (binarySAT_np_complete); planar 3-SAT, whose variable–clause incidence graph is planar (planarThreeSAT_np_complete); and Lichtenstein's planar 3-SAT, whose incidence graph stays planar with the cycle through the variables added (cyclePlanarThreeSAT_np_complete). Planarity is Gonthier's from the formal proof of the Four Color Theorem: a graph is planar when a hypermap on its half-edges embeds it with genus zero, the genus being computed from the Euler formula. NP-complete means: in NP, and every language in NP reduces to it by a polynomial-time many-one (Karp) reduction. A further compared theorem, inNP_iff_nondeterministicPolyTime, proves that NP, defined by verifiers, is the class of languages accepted in polynomial time by nondeterministic machines with two transition tables. Languages are sets of binary words. Computation is by deterministic Turing machines with a single two-way infinite tape over a four-symbol alphabet, and time is the number of machine steps. NP is defined by polynomial-time verifiers and polynomially bounded certificates, the standard certificate characterization; a reduction is a function computed by such a machine within a polynomial number of steps. Formulas are coded with unary variable indices and list lengths (binary indices for the binary variant); words that code no formula belong to none of the languages.
For an arbitrary NP verifier, the hardness proof builds a CNF formula describing the computation tableau of the verifier on the input and an unknown certificate; it is satisfiable exactly when some certificate makes the verifier accept. The reduction is itself implemented as a machine: it is written in a small language of loops over unary counters, compiled through finite programs on Boolean stacks to the single-tape model, and its running time is proved by counting the executed steps. SAT is reduced to 3-SAT by replacing each clause with a chain of clauses of at most three literals linked by fresh variables, and the reductions are composed as machines. Exactly-3-SAT and (≤1,≤2)-SAT are reached by transforming the Cook–Levin formula generator itself: every literal occurrence gets its own copy variable, a cycle of implications links the copies of each variable, long clauses are split by chains, and short clauses are padded. records.name: PascalCofactorsPalomar.coefficient_scaling
records.entry_name: Pascal Cofactors
records.doc: A Lean 4 formalisation of p-adic valuation laws for alternating cofactors C_d(p^a) = (p^(ad)+1)/(p^a+1) with odd d. It proves finite-window coefficient scaling and an exact pre-extremal restricted-binomial-gcd formula, identifies the sparse endpoint, proves the least extremal row T_p(C_d(p^a)) = p^(ad)+1 for odd d >= 5, and gives the full cubic classification for p^(2a)-p^a+1. The Palomar Challenge records coefficient scaling, the exact bounded gcd formula, the odd-degree least-row theorem, and the cubic classification.

records.name: PalomarALCS.zero_class
records.entry_name: Continuity of solutions to abstract linear control systems
records.doc: Formalization of all the numbered statements of F. Marbach, "Continuity of solutions to abstract linear control systems" (2026), https://hexagonmath.org/2610.00022. For abstract linear control systems in the sense of Weiss (a strongly continuous semigroup T on a Banach space X and bounded input maps Phi_t : L^p(R_+; U) -> X satisfying the concatenation identity), the main results are: for p = infinity, every system is zero-class, i.e. the operator norm of Phi_t tends to zero as t -> 0+ (Theorem 1.5), and t -> Phi_t u is continuous on [0, infinity) for every u in L^infinity (Corollary 1.6), a positive answer to Weiss' 1989 Problem 2.4. No integral representation of the input maps is assumed. The proof packs nearly extremal controls into one bounded operator on l^infinity and uses Phillips' lemma (Lemma 2.2), which is proved here. The development also covers the continuity of semigroup orbits (Proposition 1.2), the classical case p < infinity (Proposition 1.3), and the examples of Section 3: a non zero-class system for p < infinity (Proposition 3.1), an exotic invariant mean on periodic L^infinity functions (Lemma 3.2), and a scalar system with p = infinity without integral representation and not E_F-admissible for any Young function F (Proposition 3.3).

records.name: JM.Quantitative.welfare_incentive_bound
records.entry_name: Continuous binary implementation congruence and sharp finite welfare frontier
records.doc: A general two-alternative implementation characterization on own-type domains containing an open ball: affine private and social valuation differences, nonzero social linear form, one active welfare cut, and a fixed independent opposing probability law force nonnegative coefficient alignment. Arbitrary measurable efficient lotteries have integrable Bayesian incentive compatible transfers exactly under alignment, with explicit ex-post truthful-opponent transfers and a measurable efficient allocation witness. Arbitrary distributions including atoms are covered. A genuine independent uniform-square auction model rules out efficiency even under only agent 0 incentive compatibility for every a,b>0. The separately proved finite sharp welfare/error frontier and original example corollary are retained. This does not formalize arbitrary-alternative Theorem 4.3 or genericity, and makes no novelty claim.

records.name: HittingTimeLooseHamilton.main_result
records.entry_name: The hitting time for loose Hamilton cycles in r-graphs
records.doc: A Lean formalisation of a hitting time theorem of Wanfang Chen, Jared León and Xizhi Liu. For every fixed integer r ≥ 3, assume all r-element subsets of n vertices are exposed in a uniformly random order. As n tends to infinity through multiples of r − 1, with probability tending to one, a loose Hamilton cycle first emerges exactly when the last isolated vertex disappears.

records.name: CIVChallenge.mainTheorem
records.entry_name: Regularity of asymptotically axisymmetric Navier–Stokes solutions with analytic forcing
records.doc: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the main results of Constantin, Ignatova and Vicol on the regularity of asymptotically axisymmetric solutions of the three-dimensional Navier-Stokes equations with analytic forcing (arXiv:2609.20803). A suitable weak solution on the unit parabolic cylinder, smooth before the blow-up time, whose force is bounded in C^2 up to the blow-up time and real analytic in space, whose angular mean satisfies anisotropic Type II bounds, and which is exactly axisymmetric on a ball around the axis at every time, is axisymmetric and regular at the putative singular point (Theorem 1.1); the axisymmetric theorem (Theorem 1.3), the meridional smallness proposition, the consequences for the force (Corollary 2.3) and the lemmas of Sections 3 and 5 are formalized with it. The interior analyticity theorem of Kahane, the interior estimates of Serrin and the regularity criterion of Gustafson, Kang and Tsai, in the forms the paper uses, are proved rather than assumed. The thirteen results use only the standard axioms and build on the Lean formalization of the Caffarelli-Kohn-Nirenberg theorem; five of them are restated in a Mathlib-only comparator challenge and proved from the library theorems.

records.name: BayesianPersuasion.economic_payoff_regular
records.entry_name: Optimal Information and Concavification in Bayesian Persuasion
records.doc: Kamenica and Gentzkow's finite-state persuasion theorem from economic primitives: nonempty compact metric actions, continuous sender and receiver utilities, and a full-support common prior. Receiver best replies and sender-preferred tie actions exist. The induced sender payoff is bounded and upper semicontinuous. Finite signals realize exactly finite Bayes-plausible posterior splittings, with prescribed posteriors recovered only at nonnull messages. An optimal finite signal with at most the number of states plus two messages exists and dominates every finite experiment. Its value is the least concave majorant of the induced payoff on the entire belief simplex; strict persuasion gain is exactly the concavification gap. This covers the signal/splitting part of Proposition 1 and Corollary 2, including attainment. The straightforward recommendation branch and compact-state extension are outside this scope. Related finite splitting and abstract attainment are already formalized in Daniel Lyng's Econlib; no first-formalization or novelty claim is made.

records.name: ESSChallenge.essLocal
records.entry_name: Escauriaza–Seregin–Šverák and Ladyzhenskaya–Prodi–Serrin regularity
records.doc: A Lean formalization of two classical regularity theorems for the three-dimensional incompressible Navier–Stokes equations. The Escauriaza–Seregin–Šverák theorem states that a Leray–Hopf solution whose spatial L³ norm remains bounded in time is smooth at positive times and unique among Leray–Hopf solutions with the same initial data. The Ladyzhenskaya–Prodi–Serrin theorem gives the corresponding conclusion under a family of mixed space-time integrability conditions. The development includes the local regularity theorem, L⁵ space-time integrability under the endpoint L³ condition, and the supporting Carleman inequalities, unique continuation and backward uniqueness. It builds on the Caffarelli–Kohn–Nirenberg formalization and includes a manuscript presenting the proofs.

The Ladyzhenskaya–Prodi–Serrin theorem gives the corresponding conclusion under a family of mixed space-time integrability conditions. The development includes the local regularity theorem, L⁵ space-time integrability under the endpoint L³ condition, and the supporting Carleman inequalities, unique continuation and backward uniqueness. It builds on the Caffarelli–Kohn–Nirenberg formalization and includes a manuscript presenting the proofs.

records.name: MS1994.monotonicity_iff
records.entry_name: Milgrom–Shannon's Monotonicity Theorem: the Full Characterization
records.doc: Milgrom and Shannon (1994), Theorem 4, in both directions: for an arbitrary lattice X, partially ordered parameter space T, and real-valued objective, strong-set monotonicity of constrained maximizers over every pair of strongly ordered feasible subsets is equivalent to quasisupermodularity of every section and both weak and strict preference-preservation clauses of single crossing. The theorem imposes no finiteness, completeness, topology, continuity, compactness, nonemptiness, or optimizer existence assumptions. Supporting results and counterexamples distinguish crossing clauses and fixed-domain from varying-feasible-set monotonicity. Earlier Lean sufficiency results in Econlib and nonmathlib4 are explicitly cited.

records.name: Falmagne.falmagne_blockMarschak
records.entry_name: Falmagne–Block–Marschak Random-Utility Characterization
records.doc: A full constructive formalization of the Falmagne–Block–Marschak theorem for any finite nonempty alternative set, without a cardinality bound. A normalized stochastic choice rule on all nonempty menus is generated by a single probability distribution over complete strict rankings if and only if all Block–Marschak alternating-sum coefficients are nonnegative. The proof derives Boolean-lattice flow conservation, constructs a finite ranking mixture by positive-path subtraction, and proves exact lower-contour probability identities by Möbius inversion. Compiled adversarial examples show that regularity alone is insufficient.

records.name: PalomarResults.Grid.gridRobust_iff_intervalCuts
records.entry_name: Distance-Shell Tomography: Geometric Certificates for Fault-Tolerant Sensing, Moment Compression, and Hypercube Equalization
records.doc: Substantive Lean development for labelled distance-shell observations of anonymous integer populations. The focused 14-statement interface covers six result groups. Square grids have an exact four-corner interval-cut characterization of recovery of all populations of mass at most two after one erased report, an equivalent distance-sum compression contract, and exact corner-constrained optimum ceil(3(n+1)/2) for every n at least 3. For every positive q, the actual-distance equalizer cardinality of Q_(4q) lies between 2^(4q-1)+2q-1 and 2^(4q-1)+2q; explicit prefixes also give the infinite contradiction to the sourced exponential formula. Further selected results prove the long-rectangle optimum, ordinary 2-domination on every positive even bishop board, two exact Petersen double-total-domination values, and a connected real fractional-face counterexample. The complete library is included, not an external or assumption-based wrapper. Supporting algebra and geometric lemmas remain proved but unselected. The public README explains mathematical scope, antecedents, and limitations without treating known ingredients or all supporting lemmas as separate original results.

records.name: Potential.monderer_shapley_characterization
records.entry_name: Monderer–Shapley Exact-Potential Characterization
records.doc: The full cycle characterization for arbitrary finite player types and arbitrary nonempty player-dependent action spaces. A real-valued exact potential exists if and only if deviators' payoff differences sum to zero around every finite closed path, every finite simple closed path, every simple four-cycle, or every two-player rectangle. The construction uses finite-subset induction and imposes no finiteness restriction on actions. Exact potentials are unique up to an additive constant. With finite actions, the cycle condition yields a pure Nash equilibrium. Adversarial examples distinguish matching pennies, infinite actions, unequal dependent actions, and the finite-action boundary.

records.name: Covering.Palomar.covering_24_14_4_lower_bound
records.entry_name: Lower bounds for the covering numbers C(24,14,4) and C(25,15,5)
records.doc: A Lean proof that every family of 14-element subsets of a 24-element set covering all 4-element subsets has at least 20 members, so the covering number C(24,14,4) is at least 20, improving the previously tabulated lower bound of 19. Point derivation (the Schönheim bound) then gives C(25,15,5) >= 34, improving the tabulated 32. The proof excludes a hypothetical 19-block covering using degree and codegree counting, a Gram-matrix rank argument that forces balanced bipartite components, and a structural analysis of the two resulting cases.

records.name: ADR11.Challenge.unrootedDist_nonneg
records.entry_name: Identifying the rooted species tree from unrooted gene trees under the coalescent
records.doc:
A formalization of E. S. Allman, J. H. Degnan and J. A. Rhodes, "Identifying the rooted species tree from the distribution of unrooted gene trees under the coalescent", J. Math. Biol. 62 (2011) 833-862. The multispecies coalescent is defined from Kingman's coalescent on forests of gene lineages (its generator, the matrix exponential, and a recursion over the species tree).

Proved: the distribution of unrooted topological gene trees, with one lineage sampled per taxon, determines the rooted species tree and its internal branch lengths when there are at least five taxa (Theorem 9); on four taxa it determines exactly the unrooted metric species tree (Proposition 3); with several lineages per taxon it also determines the corresponding pendant branch lengths (Corollary 10); and all of this holds for nonbinary species trees (Proposition 11). Every other result of the paper is proved too, with the explicit gene tree distributions, linear invariants and inequalities for five taxa, and the cited results that the proofs use: Tavare's formula, the reconstruction of trees from quartets, and Cayley's count of tree shapes.

records.name: Gallai.Submission.prescribed_endpoint
records.entry_name: Gallai's conjecture with two exceptional even vertices
records.doc: Every connected finite simple graph admits an edge partition into at most ceil(|V(G)|/2) simple paths when at most two vertices of its induced even-degree graph have degree greater than three. One positive designated even vertex can be exposed twice at the ceiling budget. Two designated even vertices can be exposed twice simultaneously within floor(|V(G)|/2)+1 paths, giving simultaneous ceiling exposure at odd order. Exceptional and ordinary degrees are unrestricted. Simultaneous even-order ceiling exposure and the unrestricted Gallai conjecture are not claimed.

records.name: RAF.Concrete.reaction_length_add
records.entry_name: Effective approximation and low-intensity flatness of RAF critical-window profiles
records.doc: The critical-window laws for autocatalytic emergence in reversible binary-polymer networks lead to survival profiles for independent open reaction channels. For both the ordered split-position and commuting-factor quotient models, with all binary words of length at most two as food, explicit total algorithms enclose each survival probability at every rational openness in [0,1] to any prescribed positive rational accuracy. Computable seed lengths and finite-record contraction estimates provide uniform truncation bounds on intervals bounded away from zero. The associated intensity profiles S(1 − exp(−λ)) are smaller than every fixed power of λ as λ tends to zero from above. Rational interval bounds also compare these profiles with finite-network RAF-existence probabilities under explicit catalyst-pool and input-probability conditions. These results extend the split and quotient critical-window laws with certified approximation and quantitative control.

records.name: Erdos956.Palomar.erdos_956_superlinear
records.entry_name: Erdős 956: unit distances between disjoint convex translates
records.doc: A complete Lean 4 proof of the affirmative answer to Erdős problem 956: for all sufficiently large n, there exist n pairwise-disjoint translates of a compact convex planar set with more than n^(1+c) unordered pairs at Euclidean set-distance 1 (for c = 1/4). Adapting the parabolic construction announced by Valtr (2005) and detailed in Chojecki's April 2026 manuscript, the formalization proves the supporting-hyperplane theorem for a centrally symmetric signed parabolic cap and constructs a four-layer parabolic grid of disjoint translates. This establishes the explicit lower bound h(n) > (1/26) n^(4/3) for all n ≥ 80 and the sharper eventual bound h(n) > (2/5) n^(4/3).

records.name: Challenge.init_valid
records.entry_name: Dynamic MCS Ordering Maintenance
records.doc: A fully-dynamic Maximum-Cardinality-Search (MCS) ordering algorithm that, on a single-edge insertion or deletion into a loop-free undirected graph, scans the affected window between the two endpoints for the first step at which the current ordering's choice stops being a legal MCS pick, and only then regreedies the suffix (probe-then-repair). Correctness - every order produced stays a valid MCS ordering of the updated graph, and in fact equals the from-scratch canonical ordering - is machine-checked in Lean 4 / Mathlib, together with locality (the first position whose choice can change lies inside the window between the endpoints; after a break the suffix is regreedyed, so positions past the window may also change), an executable boolean-adjacency implementation proved to refine the abstract update, and per-update cost in a unit-cost query model (counting legality checks and pick steps along the real executable control flow): at most n units for an insertion and n + 1 for a deletion, so the worst case matches static recomputation. A stability-boundary result is also proved: if the neighbour count of every vertex in one graph exceeds that in the other by at most one along every chosen prefix, the two graphs admit a common MCS ordering; in particular inserting or deleting a matching, or flipping a single edge, always preserves a common MCS ordering.

Correctness - every order produced stays a valid MCS ordering of the updated graph, and in fact equals the from-scratch canonical ordering - is machine-checked in Lean 4 / Mathlib, together with locality (the first position whose choice can change lies inside the window between the endpoints; after a break the suffix is regreedyed, so positions past the window may also change), an executable boolean-adjacency implementation proved to refine the abstract update, and per-update cost in a unit-cost query model (counting legality checks and pick steps along the real executable control flow): at most n units for an insertion and n + 1 for a deletion, so the worst case matches static recomputation. A stability-boundary result is also proved: if the neighbour count of every vertex in one graph exceeds that in the other by at most one along every chosen prefix, the two graphs admit a common MCS ordering; in particular inserting or deleting a matching, or flipping a single edge, always preserves a common MCS ordering.

A stability-boundary result is also proved: if the neighbour count of every vertex in one graph exceeds that in the other by at most one along every chosen prefix, the two graphs admit a common MCS ordering; in particular inserting or deleting a matching, or flipping a single edge, always preserves a common MCS ordering.

records.name: erdos_546_original_statement
records.entry_name: Erdős 546: sparse graph Ramsey numbers
records.doc: A complete Lean 4 proof of the affirmative answer to Erdős problem 546 (Sudakov's theorem): there exists an absolute constant C > 0 such that every finite simple graph G with m edges and no isolated vertices has diagonal Ramsey number R(G) ≤ 2^(C √m). Formalizing Sudakov's 2011 proof—including high-degree vertex deletion, greedy bounded-degree embedding and hereditary sparse cuts, low-density monochromatic-pair extraction, and iterative clique-reservoir amplification. This proves the uniform explicit bound R(G) ≤ 2^(4000 √m) across all finite simple graphs without isolated vertices (including m = 0), together with the exact Formal Conjectures statement.

records.name: CellAttachment.two_cell_attachment
records.entry_name: Fundamental Groups of Arbitrary Two-Cell Attachments
records.doc: The full arbitrary-family two-cell attachment theorem for ordinary topological fundamental groups. For any path-connected topological space X, any basepoint, and any indexed family of continuous circle attaching maps, a genuine adjunction quotient is constructed from X and the coproduct of closed complex unit disks. The actual inclusion-induced fundamental-group homomorphism is surjective and its kernel is precisely the normal closure of the once-around attaching loops, transported along the specified basepoint paths. A quotient group isomorphism is proved compatible with the actual inclusion map. No finiteness, CW, separation, local-connectivity or semilocal-simple-connectivity hypotheses are added.

records.name: HigherCellAttachment.higher_cell_attachment
records.entry_name: Fundamental Groups of Arbitrary Higher-Cell Attachments
records.doc: Higher-cell attachment invariance for ordinary topological fundamental groups. For any path-connected topological space X, any basepoint, an index type in an independent universe, independently varying cell dimensions at least three, and arbitrary continuous unit-sphere attaching maps, the genuine adjunction quotient of X and the coproduct of closed Euclidean unit balls is constructed with its quotient topology. The actual inclusion-induced fundamental-group homomorphism is bijective and is the underlying homomorphism of the displayed multiplicative equivalence. Mixed dimensions and the empty family are included. No finiteness, countability, CW, separation or local-connectivity hypotheses are added, and no retraction, simple-connectivity or kernel oracle is assumed.

records.name: Erdos2.Standalone.erdos_2
records.entry_name: Erdős 2: minimum modulus of distinct covering systems
records.doc: A complete Lean 4 proof of the negative answer to Erdős problem 2 (Hough 2015; Balister–Bollobás–Morris–Sahasrabudhe–Tiba 2022): there is an absolute constant B such that every finite covering of the integers by distinct moduli > 1 contains a modulus ≤ B. For any finite set D of moduli above B with N = lcm(D), the proof builds a probability measure on ZMod N prime by prime via the BBMST half-cap fiber update, preserving the progression bound w(z ≡ a mod d) ≤ 2^ω(d)/d while bounding each prime-p loss by C (log p)^6 / (p - 1)^2 via Euler factorization and Mertens' third theorem. Combining this summable tail with Euler's product bound on A-smooth reciprocals keeps the covered mass below 1/2, proving the Formal Conjectures ideal statement (erdos_2), its direct negation (not_arbitrarilyLarge_ideal_coverings), the uniform minimum-modulus bound (minimum_modulus_bound), and finite-set noncoverage (finite_noncoverage_bound).

records.name: Chazelle.linear_time_triangulation
records.entry_name: Linear-Time Triangulation of Simple Polygons (Chazelle's Algorithm) in Lean 4
records.doc: A formalization and provably correct implementation of a linear-time algorithm for triangulating a simple polygon.  The implementation is a concrete program for an explicit exact real RAM.  Lean proves that on every simple polygon with n vertices the program halts within C(n+1) steps, with natural-number words at most K(n+1), and outputs a conforming triangulation with exactly n - 2 triangles on the input vertices.  No general-position assumption is made.  The proofs use exactly Lean's three standard axioms (propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound), with no sorry and no native_decide.  They are checked by the Lean kernel and replayed by independent kernels.  The algorithm is a variant of Chazelle's (B. Chazelle, Triangulating a simple polygon in linear time, Discrete & Computational Geometry 6 (1991), 485-524), and the main theorem is the triangulation conclusion of his Theorem 4.3.  The program follows the structure of Chazelle's algorithm: visibility maps of polygonal chains, merging with conformality restoration and granularity enforcement, ray-shooting and arc-cutting oracles built with planar separators, the up phase and the down phase, and the final stage from the visibility map to the triangulation.  It departs from the paper's algorithm in documented ways; in particular its down phase recurses only for n >= 2^30 + 2.  The running-time bound is proved for this program, not for the algorithm as the paper describes it.  The program is also given by name with explicit (very large) constants, and a merge-level refinement theorem shows that its run follows an abstract model of the algorithm written from the paper.

records.name: Erdos958.Palomar.erdos_958
records.entry_name: Erdős 958: planar point sets with distance multiplicities {1, ..., n - 1}
records.doc: A complete Lean 4 proof of the negative answer to Erdős problem 958: for every n ≥ 4, there exists an n-point configuration in the Euclidean plane determining n - 1 distinct interpoint distances with multiplicities {1, 2, ..., n - 1} that is neither equidistant on a line nor equidistant on a circle. Formalizing the May 2025 construction of Clemen, Dumitrescu, and Liu, the proof places n - 1 equally spaced points on a short arc of the unit circle together with the center (0, 0), uses strict monotonicity of chord lengths on [0, π/3) to compute the exact distance-multiplicity profile, and eliminates collinear and concyclic progressions algebraically. It also proves the positive baseline results that every equidistant collinear configuration of size n ≥ 2 has n - 1 distinct distances with multiplicities {1, ..., n - 1}, and that for every n ≥ 2 there exists an n-point circular equidistant configuration with that distance-multiplicity profile.

records.name: Erdos1054.Palomar.answer_i
records.entry_name: Erdős 1054: sums of smallest divisors
records.doc: A complete Lean 4 proof of all three parts of Erdős problem 1054. For the least integer f(n) whose k smallest divisors sum to n, we prove that f(n) is not o(n), is not o(n) on any density-one set, and satisfies limsup f(n)/n = ∞ on every density-one subtype. records.name: Dixmier.Palomar.massSixGeneration
records.entry_name: The rank-one Dixmier conjecture for elements of mass at most six
records.doc: Over any characteristic-zero field, two elements P and Q of the first Weyl algebra satisfying QP-PQ=1 generate the algebra when P has at most six nonzero homogeneous components for deg X=1 and deg Y=-1. The degree, order and mass of Q are unrestricted. The proof combines sparse-polynomial rigidity with internally proved Newton and Weyl-algebra structural results.

records.name: WeilClasses.Challenge.Kd_Nm
records.entry_name: Weil classes on abelian sixfolds and the Hodge conjecture for abelian fourfolds (Markman)
records.doc:
A conditional Lean 4 formalization of E. Markman, "Cycles on abelian 2n-folds of Weil type from secant sheaves on abelian n-folds" (arXiv:2502.03415v2). The paper proves that the Hodge-Weil classes of polarized abelian sixfolds of Weil type with discriminant -1 are algebraic (Theorem 1.5.1) and deduces the Hodge conjecture for abelian fourfolds (Corollary 1.6.1).

Every result of the paper about cohomology classes, Clifford algebras, spin representations, Hodge structures and period domains is proved in a linear-algebra model of the cohomology of abelian varieties (abelian varieties up to isogeny as polarizable rational Hodge structures of weight one), by the paper's arguments except the departures listed under fidelity (notably Proposition 6.1.2 and Lemma 4.0.2, proved by other arguments with the owner's approval): rational secant lines to the spinor variety and the abelian 2n-folds of Weil type they give (Sections 2-4), the Spin(V)-equivariance of Orlov's equivalence (Section 6, Proposition 6.1.2), Theorem 1.4.1(3) and (4) (the characteristic class of the secant-square sheaf stays of Hodge type on every Weil-type deformation of X x X^, and its K-translates with h^3 span Q h^3 + HW), Corollary 1.3.2, the cohomological results of Section 8, and Section 10. The results the paper cites from Chevalley, Igusa (Lemmas 1-2, Section 2, Proposition 3 except the orbits over subfields in which -d is not a square), Golyshev-Lunts-Orlov, Orlov, Huybrechts, Trautman, van Geemen (Def. 4.9, and Th. 5.2(3) through Landherr's theorem and Meyer's theorem), Markman (2023) and Schoen (Prop. 10, from push-forward of cycles, by Voisin's argument) are proved in the case the paper uses.

Theorem 1.5.1 and Corollary 1.6.1 are proved assuming, as named hypotheses in their statements, the paper's own sheaf-theoretic Sections 7-9 (in the form: the class kappa_3(E) is algebraic near X x X^ wherever kappa(E) is of Hodge type) and results from algebraic geometry not yet available in Lean: about algebraic cycles, pullbacks, push-forwards along projections and products of algebraic classes, the Lefschetz (1,1) theorem, Voisin's algebraicity loci and a theorem of Ramon-Mari; about Hodge structures, two theorems of Moonen-Zarhin. Remark 10.1.2(1) assumes part of Igusa's Proposition 3 when -d is not a square. Eleven statements of the paper are false or misprinted as printed and are formalized in corrected form (the basis of Example 10.2.2 is also misprinted, with no effect on the value computed there); REPORT.md audits the paper.

records.doc:
A conditional Lean 4 formalization of E. Markman, "Cycles on abelian 2n-folds of Weil type from secant sheaves on abelian n-folds" (arXiv:2502.03415v2). The paper proves that the Hodge-Weil classes of polarized abelian sixfolds of Weil type with discriminant -1 are algebraic (Theorem 1.5.1) and deduces the Hodge conjecture for abelian fourfolds (Corollary 1.6.1).

Every result of the paper about cohomology classes, Clifford algebras, spin representations, Hodge structures and period domains is proved in a linear-algebra model of the cohomology of abelian varieties (abelian varieties up to isogeny as polarizable rational Hodge structures of weight one), by the paper's arguments except the departures listed under fidelity (notably Proposition 6.1.2 and Lemma 4.0.2, proved by other arguments with the owner's approval): rational secant lines to the spinor variety and the abelian 2n-folds of Weil type they give (Sections 2-4), the Spin(V)-equivariance of Orlov's equivalence (Section 6, Proposition 6.1.2), Theorem 1.4.1(3) and (4) (the characteristic class of the secant-square sheaf stays of Hodge type on every Weil-type deformation of X x X^, and its K-translates with h^3 span Q h^3 + HW), Corollary 1.3.2, the cohomological results of Section 8, and Section 10. The results the paper cites from Chevalley, Igusa (Lemmas 1-2, Section 2, Proposition 3 except the orbits over subfields in which -d is not a square), Golyshev-Lunts-Orlov, Orlov, Huybrechts, Trautman, van Geemen (Def. 4.9, and Th. 5.2(3) through Landherr's theorem and Meyer's theorem), Markman (2023) and Schoen (Prop. 10, from push-forward of cycles, by Voisin's argument) are proved in the case the paper uses.

Theorem 1.5.1 and Corollary 1.6.1 are proved assuming, as named hypotheses in their statements, the paper's own sheaf-theoretic Sections 7-9 (in the form: the class kappa_3(E) is algebraic near X x X^ wherever kappa(E) is of Hodge type) and results from algebraic geometry not yet available in Lean: about algebraic cycles, pullbacks, push-forwards along projections and products of algebraic classes, the Lefschetz (1,1) theorem, Voisin's algebraicity loci and a theorem of Ramon-Mari; about Hodge structures, two theorems of Moonen-Zarhin. Remark 10.1.2(1) assumes part of Igusa's Proposition 3 when -d is not a square. Eleven statements of the paper are false or misprinted as printed and are formalized in corrected form (the basis of Example 10.2.2 is also misprinted, with no effect on the value computed there); REPORT.md audits the paper.

records.name: SuperdiffusionCLT.StatementAudit.TheoremA.theoremA
records.entry_name: Superdiffusive central limit theorem for a Brownian particle in a critically-correlated incompressible random drift
records.doc: A Lean formalization of the superdiffusive central limit theorem for a Brownian particle in a critically-correlated incompressible random drift (Armstrong, Bou-Rabee and Kuusi): the quenched superdiffusive invariance principle (Theorem A), quantitative homogenization of the Dirichlet problem (Theorem B), the large-scale C^{0,gamma} and C^{1,gamma} regularity theory (Theorems C and D) and the sharp asymptotics of the renormalized diffusivities (Theorem 5.1), with every result of Sections 2 to 8 of the paper that their proofs use. It is built on the public CoarseGraining homogenization library and the public MarkovProcess library.

records.name: Erdos1139.Palomar.uniform_maximal_gap
records.entry_name: Erdős 1139: large gaps between almost-primes
records.doc: A Lean 4 formalization of unconditional bounds and conditional reductions for Erdős problem 1139 on consecutive P_2 almost-primes (Ω(u_k) ≤ 2). Extending Chojecki's (2026) Erdős 689 double-covering construction via protected-reserve omission, it proves unconditionally that limsup (u_{k+1} - u_k) / log(k + 1) ≥ A > 1 and that every large height X contains an almost-prime-free interval of length ≥ c log X (c > 1), alongside the mixed prime/prime-square CRT bridge, PNT primorial asymptotics, and squared-core deficiency classification. Using a squared-prime core and scale-adaptive dyadic prime shells, it also derives the full infinite-limsup conjecture conditionally from the Green–Tao–Ziegler (2010–2012) linear-forms asymptotic and proves its reverse implication to arbitrary-length prime progressions.

records.name: ClassicalSchur.triangleRamsey_succ
records.entry_name: S(6) ≤ 1801 if R₄(3) ≤ 61: a centred Schur bound and the structure at the frontier
records.doc: A Lean 4 formalization, with Mathlib, of an upper bound for the Schur numbers in terms of the triangle Ramsey numbers, and of the structure of a colouring at the limit of that bound. If every colouring with k colours of the pairs of r points has a monochromatic triangle (R_k(3) ≤ r), then the interval [1, 2((k + 1)⌊(r − 1)/2⌋ + 1)] is not covered by k + 1 sumfree sets, so S(k + 1) ≤ 2(k + 1)⌊(r − 1)/2⌋ + 1. With R_2(3) ≤ 6 this gives S(3) ≤ 13, which is exact. Under the hypothesis R_4(3) ≤ 61, a computer-assisted claim of M. Tatarevic that this project does not prove, the pigeonhole step gives R_5(3) ≤ 302, and the bound then gives S(6) ≤ 1801; the hypothesis is an explicit argument (TriangleRamsey 4 61) of each theorem that uses it. The frontier theorems describe a Schur colouring of the largest interval that the bound allows. Let R_k(3) ≤ u + 1, (k + 1)u = 2t and m = (k + 2)t, and let c be a Schur colouring of [1, 2m + 1] with k + 2 colours. Then each colour occurs exactly t times in [1, m]; with q = c(m + 1), the neighbourhood of the centre m in the colour q is regular in every other colour; and c(m + 1 − d) = c(m + 1 + d) for every d in [1, m] with c(d) = q. For six colours under R_4(3) ≤ 61, a Schur colouring of [1, 1801] gives five sets of 60 points, each closed under x ↦ 1800 − x with no fixed point and with differences in at most four colours. These theorems do not exclude such a colouring and do not prove S(6) ≤ 1800. The arguments for the bound and for the frontier were first proposed by AI agents based on ChatGPT (OpenAI) in a project discussion. A Claude agent (Anthropic) audited the argument for the bound; the AI system Claude checked each step of the frontier argument, restated it with explicit hypotheses, and wrote all Lean proofs, under the direction of the author. The results have not been peer reviewed.
