records.name: Erdos575.not_erdos_575_corrected
records.entry_name: Erdős 575: bipartite extremal-graph compactness
records.doc: A complete Lean 4 disproof of Erdős problem 575 in both its unrestricted and cycle-containing formulations: a finite family F of forbidden graphs containing a bipartite member need not contain a bipartite H ∈ F with ex(n; H) = O(ex(n; F)). Proves the unrestricted case from scratch via the bipartite forest family F_0 = {K_{1,2}, 2K_2} (where ex(n; F_0) ≤ 1 while ex(n; K_{1,2}) ≥ ⌊n/2⌋ and ex(n; 2K_2) ≥ n - 1), and resolves the cycle-containing case by adapting OpenAI's all-bipartite cyclic counterexample family from Erdős problem 180 (where ex(n; F) = O(n^(21/16)) and ex(n; H) = Ω(n^(4/3)) for every H ∈ F).

Proves the unrestricted case from scratch via the bipartite forest family F_0 = {K_{1,2}, 2K_2} (where ex(n; F_0) ≤ 1 while ex(n; K_{1,2}) ≥ ⌊n/2⌋ and ex(n; 2K_2) ≥ n - 1), and resolves the cycle-containing case by adapting OpenAI's all-bipartite cyclic counterexample family from Erdős problem 180 (where ex(n; F) = O(n^(21/16)) and ex(n; H) = Ω(n^(4/3)) for every H ∈ F).

records.name: ClassicalSchurClaims.erL_four
records.entry_name: The Schur degree of block sums: L(4) = 16 and L(5) ≥ 49
records.doc: A Lean 4 formalization, with Mathlib, of the main results of the paper "The Schur degree of block sums: L(4) = 16 and L(5) ≥ 49" (paper/schur-degree-block-sums.md in this repository). Eliahou and Revuelta (Discrete Math. 344 (2021) 112332) defined a number L(n) through the Schur degree of the set of block sums of a sequence of positive integers, proved S(n−1) + 1 ≤ L(n) ≤ R_{n−1}(3) − 1 and S(n) ≤ n·L(n), and conjectured L(n) = S(n−1) + 1 (their Conjecture 5.6), that is, L(4) = 14 and L(5) = 45. The formalization proves L(4) = 16 (erL_four), 49 ≤ L(5) ≤ 65 (erL_five_bounds), the lift that turns a cover of the nonzero elements of ZMod m₁ × ZMod m₂ by q sets that are sumfree in the group into a sequence whose block sums have Schur degree at most q (lift_lemma), its corollary m₁m₂ ≤ L(n) (le_erL_of_groupPartition), and Theorem 4.1 and the upper bound of Proposition 5.3 of Eliahou and Revuelta, with the pigeonhole bound ramseyBound k in place of R_k(3) (le_sdeg_blockSums, erL_le). So Conjecture 5.6 is false for n = 4 and n = 5. The Lean upper bound for L(5) is 65, not the bound 61 of the paper: the formalization uses the pigeonhole bound R₄(3) ≤ 66 and not the bound R₄(3) ≤ 62 of Fettes, Kramer and Radziszowski. The finite checks use the Lean kernel (decide), with no native code. The sequence W, the lift, the proofs, the programs and the Lean formalization were produced with the AI system Claude (Anthropic; model Claude Opus 5.5) under the direction of the author.

records.name: FalconerPacking.exists_pin_volume_pinnedDistances_pos
records.entry_name: A Hausdorff–packing criterion for self-pinned distance sets
records.doc: For a Borel subset E of the Euclidean plane with Hausdorff dimension d in (1, 5/4], a strict upper bound on its packing dimension by the explicit piecewise curve B_H(d) ensures a point y in E whose pinned distance set has positive one-dimensional Lebesgue measure. The three branches are 2d-1, 1+r_2(d-1), and 1/(3-2d), with the transitions and algebraic root defined independently in Challenge.lean. This is a sufficient criterion with an additional packing-dimension hypothesis, not a resolution of the general planar Falconer conjecture.

records.name: PalomarCatalan.catalans_conjecture
records.entry_name: A Lean 4 formalization of Catalan's conjecture (Mihăilescu's theorem)
records.doc: A complete Lean 4 formalization of Catalan's conjecture, proved by Preda Mihăilescu: 8 and 9 are the only consecutive positive proper perfect powers. The formal proof follows the cyclotomic proof in Yuri Bilu's expositions. Cassels' relations, Stickelberger annihilation, and height and counting estimates exclude the case in which one exponent is congruent to 1 modulo the other. Thaine's theorem on circular units, together with a Runge-type approximation argument, settles the remaining case. The class-field-theoretic input comes from a fixed, vendored subset of the ClassFieldTheory library. The registered results are four theorems: Catalan's conjecture over the natural numbers, in the form stated in Google DeepMind's Formal Conjectures; the same equation for integer bases greater than one; the classification of solutions of x^p − y^q = 1 with nonzero integer bases of either sign; and Mihăilescu's theorem that x^p = y^q + 1 has no solution in nonzero integers when p and q are odd primes. All four depend only on the axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.

records.name: MonotoneLight.isClosed_fiberRel
records.entry_name: Monotone-Light Factorization of Compact Hausdorff Surjections
records.doc: Every continuous surjection between compact Hausdorff spaces factors through a compact Hausdorff quotient that collapses exactly the connected components of each original fiber. The first map has connected fibers and the second has totally disconnected fibers. Any two such factorizations have a unique commuting homeomorphism. Empty spaces are permitted.

records.name: GSPalomar.two_factor
records.entry_name: Structured orthogonal and unitary matrices: factorization, geometry and singularities
records.doc: Block-diagonal matrix factors interleaved with fixed coordinate permutations define low-parametric matrix families. This formalization proves orthogonal-factor sufficiency for two and three real layers, its complex unitary analogue, and explicit four-layer counterexamples over both fields. It establishes an exact two-factor cell-rank criterion and real and unitary cosine-sine exhaustion for the (p,2,p) shuffle family. Two-layer images with complete within-layer block sharing, arbitrary overlap and arbitrary fixed carriers have a smooth atlas in the inherited matrix topology, an exact tangent image, a smooth Frobenius projector, a whole-tangent-bundle Cayley retraction and smooth intrinsic gradient sections. Shared orthogonal block exponential curves have normal ambient acceleration and constant Frobenius speed under the no-off-diagonal-overlap condition. Three-layer (2,q,2) families have genuine topological singularities for every real q >= 3 and for odd unitary q >= 3. The full supported proof library is included; experimental special-unitary drafts and the explicitly listed remaining problems are not claimed.

It establishes an exact two-factor cell-rank criterion and real and unitary cosine-sine exhaustion for the (p,2,p) shuffle family. Two-layer images with complete within-layer block sharing, arbitrary overlap and arbitrary fixed carriers have a smooth atlas in the inherited matrix topology, an exact tangent image, a smooth Frobenius projector, a whole-tangent-bundle Cayley retraction and smooth intrinsic gradient sections. Shared orthogonal block exponential curves have normal ambient acceleration and constant Frobenius speed under the no-off-diagonal-overlap condition. Three-layer (2,q,2) families have genuine topological singularities for every real q >= 3 and for odd unitary q >= 3. The full supported proof library is included; experimental special-unitary drafts and the explicitly listed remaining problems are not claimed.

records.name: PalomarChallenge.independent_challenge
records.entry_name: A counterexample to Vaught's conjecture for infinitary logic
records.doc: There is a counterexample to Vaught's conjecture for L_{omega_1,omega}. This formalization is based on an unpublished draft by Robin Knight. It constructs a sentence in a countable relational language with exactly aleph-one isomorphism classes of countable models and no nonempty perfect set of pairwise nonisomorphic model codes. This is not a counterexample to the first-order Vaught conjecture.

records.name: PartialBalayage.interval_weakTypeConstant_le_two
records.entry_name: Two partial balayage principles for weak-type estimates
records.doc: A candidate Lean formalization of fifteen selected statements from Yongxi Lin's table of weak type (1,1) upper bounds for singular integrals and maximal operators. Bounds include full-vector complex-input Riesz, complex Beurling, full and traceless Frobenius Hessians, both projections, centred intervals and balls, and all six Poisson and heat maximal bounds. records.name: IncidenceBounds.arbitrary_charZero
records.entry_name: Explicit Szemerédi–Trotter bounds over arbitrary fields
records.doc: We formalize four explicit Szemerédi–Trotter incidence bounds for m distinct points and n distinct affine lines in a field plane. In characteristic zero the bound is 3(mn)^(2/3) + m + n. In positive characteristic p, an arbitrary field admits the additional term 2mn/p. This term is absent when mn ≤ p³. Over the prime field ZMod p the additional term improves to mn/p without a size restriction. The development adapts the author's polynomial-method argument, uses generic coordinates for the improved linear term, and proves a finite-plane counting estimate for the prime-field refinement.

records.name: SemigroupBetti.beta1_le_two_mul_normalizedWidth
records.entry_name: Linear upper bounds for the first Betti number of four-generated numerical semigroups
records.doc: A Lean 4 formalization, against Mathlib, of the theorem that the first Betti number (minimal number of generators of the toric ideal) of a numerical semigroup minimally generated by four elements n0 < n1 < n2 < n3 is at most 2W, where W = (n3 - n0) / gcd(n1 - n0, n2 - n0, n3 - n0); in particular at most twice the width n3 - n0.  This replaces the conjectured quadratic bound (w+1 choose 2) of Herzog–Stamate (2014) and Caviglia–Moscariello–Sammartano (2024) in embedding dimension four; the bound 2w is attained for every width w >= 4 (an informal companion result; sharpness is not formalized).

records.name: SemigroupBetti.beta1_le_two_mul_width
records.entry_name: Linear upper bounds for the first Betti number of four-generated numerical semigroups
records.doc: A Lean 4 formalization, against Mathlib, of the theorem that the first Betti number (minimal number of generators of the toric ideal) of a numerical semigroup minimally generated by four elements n0 < n1 < n2 < n3 is at most 2W, where W = (n3 - n0) / gcd(n1 - n0, n2 - n0, n3 - n0); in particular at most twice the width n3 - n0.  This replaces the conjectured quadratic bound (w+1 choose 2) of Herzog–Stamate (2014) and Caviglia–Moscariello–Sammartano (2024) in embedding dimension four; the bound 2w is attained for every width w >= 4 (an informal companion result; sharpness is not formalized).

records.name: PalomarMonotiles.T5_strongAperiodicity
records.entry_name: The CLARK Tile: An Aperiodic Monotile in Five Dimensions
records.doc: We give an explicit compact tile, called CLARK (Chair with Local Asymmetric Registration Keys), in five-dimensional Euclidean space. It modifies a chair of 31 unit five-cubes with 256 rational pyramidal keys. Copies may be translated, rotated or reflected. The selected theorem proves tiling existence, no nonzero translation period in any physical tiling, and a finite full Euclidean symmetry group of cardinality at most 3840 for every such tiling. No registration, matching-rule or hierarchy assumption is imposed. A trivial symmetry group is not asserted.

records.name: MatrixBounds.Numeric.SuppliedCertifiedPipeline.exponent_lt
records.entry_name: LeanMMBound: the matrix multiplication exponent is below 2.3710449
records.doc: The matrix multiplication exponent ω is the least exponent such that n×n matrices can be multiplied in n^(ω+o(1)) operations. This repository proves in Lean 4 / Mathlib that ω < 2.3710449 over every commutative ring, improving the previous bound ω < 2.371177 (Dupont et al. 2026). ω is defined via the exact tensor rank of n×n matrix multiplication. The new ingredient is shared extraction across recursion levels of the asymmetric laser method. The formalization covers the full argument, from the Coppersmith–Winograd degeneration to an exact rational certificate checked in the Lean kernel. The construction and proof were produced largely by AI systems under the authors' direction.

records.name: OrderArcs.exists_order_arc
records.entry_name: Order Arcs Between Subcontinua
records.doc: Properly nested nonempty compact connected subsets A and B of a compact metric space are the endpoints of a continuous embedded interval of nonempty compact connected subsets, strictly increasing under inclusion. The ambient space need not be connected.

records.name: DensityThreeQuarters.density_bound

records.name: SixConcyclic.six_concyclic_fieldCriterion
records.entry_name: Six concyclic points satisfy the Euclidean Ramsey tensor criterion, as does every spherical set of at most m + 4 points of affine dimension m and every algebraic spherical set; given the classification's sufficiency half, these sets are Ramsey (the algebraic ones when spanning)
records.doc: A Lean 4 development around the tensor criterion of the classification of finite Euclidean Ramsey configurations (openai/math, family 172). With the criterion's definitions restated character for character from that project's challenge file: every set of six distinct points on a circle satisfies the criterion, by an explicit certificate (the product of the two bilinear forms through the first three and the last three points of a homogeneous parametrisation of the circle, scaled and conjugated by the parametrisation); the sharp dimension theorem: every spherical set of at most m + 4 distinct points, m the dimension of its affine span, satisfies the criterion in its own space and coordinate field (either the augmented vectors admit real isolating quadrics and the sphere lifts by the adjugate, or a dependence among them is supported on six concyclic points while every other point adds a dimension, and the six-point certificate is carried into the ambient space, symmetrised, adjusted to the common sphere, extended point by point and descended from R tensor R to F tensor F), so every spherical set of at most six points satisfies it in any dimension with any affine span; every spherical set with algebraic coordinates satisfies it, of any size, by the separability idempotent of F tensor F; the criterion always implies sphericity, so for algebraic coordinates it is exactly sphericity. Given the sufficiency half of the classification as an explicit hypothesis (quantified as the source states its Theorem 1.1), every spherical set of at most six points, every spherical set of at most m + 4 points and every spanning spherical set with algebraic coordinates is Ramsey; given both halves, a spanning set with algebraic coordinates is Ramsey if and only if it is spherical. The source proves the Ramsey property for at most five circle points; six is the first case its method of independent quadratic rows cannot reach. With the seven-point non-Ramsey circle set of A cyclic non-Ramsey heptagon (arXiv:2609.23327), the least size of a non-Ramsey spherical set is seven, given the classification, and, for m at least 2, m + 5 the least size of one with affine span of dimension m, since the heptagon with m - 2 further sphere points fails the criterion and is not Ramsey; the research note in note/ states this, verifies by an exact derivation identity that the heptagon fails the criterion, and proves the sharpness on paper (nothing in Lean says that a set fails the criterion). The classification is not proved here. The restated definitions and a few adapted lemmas derive from Apache-2.0 work of OpenAI (NOTICE, LICENSES/Apache-2.0.txt); the rest is MIT.

records.name: SharpChaos.sharp_propagation_of_chaos
records.entry_name: Sharp Wasserstein propagation of chaos from correlated initial data
records.doc: A Lean 4 proof, checked against Mathlib, of a sharp quantitative propagation of chaos estimate for mean field diffusions dX_i = (a(X_i) + N^{-1} sum_j K(X_i, X_j)) dt + sqrt 2 dW_i with a globally Lipschitz one-body drift a and a bounded, globally Lipschitz pairwise interaction K. If every k-particle marginal of the (possibly correlated and singular) exchangeable initial law lies within squared quadratic Wasserstein distance C_0 (k/N)^2 of the corresponding power of the McKean-Vlasov initial law, then the same holds on every finite time interval [0, T] with an explicit constant C_T that depends neither on N nor on the dimension. No entropy bound, transport inequality or independence of the initial particles is assumed.

records.name: CountablyInfiniteStrongCrystallineMeasures.strongCardinalClaim
records.entry_name: A strongly tempered Meyer space of countably infinite Hamel dimension
records.doc: There exists a locally finite carrier Λ in the real line whose whole complex strongly tempered Meyer space has Hamel dimension ℵ₀. Both a tempered distribution and its distributional Fourier transform have local atomic formulas on Λ, with coefficient families whose absolute values are summable after division by some polynomial weight (1 + |x|)^N. The same carrier supports the entire space; finite-dimensional exponent layers prove the rank upper bound and independent original parity modes prove the lower bound. The radius schedule is selected classically. This is an existence theorem for one carrier, not an effective construction or a classification of all carriers.

records.name: ImprovedExponents.threeSum_pruned
records.entry_name: Improved exponents for 3SUM and APSP from triangles in sparse lopsided graphs
records.doc: A sorry-free Lean 4 formalization of improved running-time exponents for 3SUM, Exact Triangle, the (min,+)-product and all-pairs shortest paths (APSP), on the word RAM of the published formalization (anthropics/formal-math, 3sum-apsp) of the paper of Alman and Vassilevska Williams, "Truly Subquadratic 3SUM and Truly Subcubic APSP via Triangles in Sparse Lopsided Graphs" (arXiv:2610.06783). That paper gives deterministic algorithms for 3SUM in time O(n^1.9992) and for the (min,+)-product and APSP in time O(n^2.99942), through Exact Triangle in time O(n^(3 - 0.0017)). The project analyzes the same algorithm again and changes it in a few places: an exact count of the leaves of its recursion, a host that charges the solver at the true size of the middle part, and encodings restricted to the leaves that are read. The theorems submitted state, in exactly the sense of upstream's trusted file EndStatement.lean (programs of a word RAM with O(log n)-bit words, numbers of polynomial absolute value, every instance, every size), that 3SUM is solved in O(n^1.99896) steps and Exact Triangle in O(n^2.99791) steps, and, by carrying out the all-edges route that footnote 10 of the paper mentions, that the (min,+)-product and APSP are solved in O(n^2.99791) steps instead of O(n^2.99931) through the standard reductions. None of them has a hypothesis; every proof depends only on the axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. The library also proves general theorems for all admissible parameters, a closed form for the optimal saving of the method at each ratio of parameters, and that the supremum of that saving over all ratios lies in (0.002095, 0.002096], so that no choice of parameters gives 3SUM an exponent below 1.998952 with this method. The pruned encoder and the two new hosts are written as programs of the machine and their running times are proved on it. All Lean, Python and LaTeX was written by the language model Claude Fable 5.1 (Anthropic) in Claude Code, under the direction of the maintainer, who wrote no Lean by hand; the move to Lean v4.35.0-rc2, with the port of the included part of upstream, was made by Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic) in the same way. An accompanying paper (papers/improved-exponents/) states every result with its Lean name.

records.name: bezdek_annulus
records.entry_name: Area stability of planar plank covers and Bezdek's annulus theorem
records.doc: A complete Lean 4 formalization of Bezdek's annulus theorem and the quantitative area stability of planar plank covers based on the paper "Area stability of plank covers" by Egor Bakaev and Amir Yehudayoff (arXiv:2609.30409). The formalization proves that there exists an explicit positive radius r > 0 such that if finitely many planar planks cover the closed annulus r <= ||x|| <= 1, their total width is at least 2. The core theorem established is the quantitative overlap theorem, which bounds the excess overlap cost on the unit disk from below by a positive constant times the hole area divided by r.

records.name: ComparatorChecks.omega_bound
records.entry_name: Matrix multiplication exponent at most 9/4 over arbitrary fields
records.doc: This development extends OpenAI's Lean proof of the matrix multiplication exponent bound 9/4 from the complex numbers to every field, including finite fields and fields of positive characteristic. It generalizes Fourier separation and interpolation over each field's algebraic closure, descends tensor powers through one fixed finite coefficient algebra, and connects the resulting exact-rank bounds to the original division-free arithmetic-program model. The compared statements include the arithmetic exponent upper bound, nonvacuity and lower-bound checks, an explicit positive-epsilon operation-count theorem, and exact coordinatewise coefficient decompositions. The original numerical bound and complex-field construction are OpenAI's work; this fork contributes the arbitrary-field extension and its formal verification.

records.name: LiebThirringAudit.stability_of_matter
records.entry_name: Stability of Matter in Lean: Lieb–Thirring, Ionization, the Thermodynamic Limit and Thomas–Fermi Theory
records.doc: A Lean 4 and Mathlib formalization of the stability of non-relativistic Coulomb matter in three dimensions. For normalized antisymmetric L2 electron states with q >= 1 spin states and static nuclei with charges between zero and Z, it proves a lower energy bound -C(q,Z)(N+M), uniformly in particle counts and nuclear positions. The main estimate is an additive inequality between nonnegative extended energies, valid even for infinite kinetic energy and nuclear collisions. A real quadratic-form theorem proves Coulomb finiteness and the lower bound for states with finite kinetic energy and distinct nuclear positions. The library also proves the kinetic Lieb-Thirring inequality with Rumin's explicit coefficient (9/35)(6 pi^2)^(2/3) q^(-2/3), Baxter's electrostatic inequality with its positive nearest-other-nucleus correction, and equality of the Fourier kinetic form with the classical Dirichlet integral on spin-valued Schwartz functions. The kinetic normalization is -Delta. The proof combines Pauli projections and Rumin's layer cake, a Voronoi boundary-measure proof of Baxter's inequality, nearest-nucleus screening, and Hardy's inequality. Three extensions prove the atomic bound N < 2Z+1 for weak ground states and strict binding, the unique continuous convex canonical zero-temperature energy density of neutral matter with finite-mass bosonic nuclei in Dirichlet balls, and the molecular Thomas-Fermi large-charge limit for arbitrary fixed spin and every fixed TF mass nu>0. Thomas-Fermi theory also has a unique relaxed minimizer, mass saturation at the total nuclear charge, and exact-mass attainment precisely up to neutrality.

records.name: FourRowPrincipal.endpoint
records.entry_name: Sharp robustness and stability of the four-row permanent inequality
records.doc: A formalization of sharp balanced-law robustness and stability refinements of the classical four-row permanent inequalities of Carlen-Lieb-Loss and Bristiel-Caputo. It proves the exact total-variation radius 1/24, optimal variance-deficit coefficient (1-24r)/9, complete nonnegative equality cases, sharp endpoint entropy constants, and adaptive tensorization. The explicit interior exponent is sufficient rather than optimal; at radius zero it is weaker than the classical optimal uniform exponent. Lean checks exhaustive support coverage and exact rational Gram identities.

records.name: X2Y5Z7.theorem_1_1
records.entry_name: The generalized Fermat equation x² + y⁵ = z⁷
records.doc: A Lean 4 and Mathlib formalization of the main results of the paper "The generalized Fermat equation x² + y⁵ = z⁷" by Manvir Jaswal. Following Putz, a solution is a triple of integers (X, Y, Z) with X⁵ + Y² = Z⁷, gcd(X, Y, Z) = 1 and XYZ ≠ 0; put η = X⁵/Z⁷ and A_η = ℚ[t]/(f_η), where f_η(t) = 4t⁵ψ(t) − η(4t − 1) and ψ(t) = 25t³ + 20t² + 14t + 14. Theorem 1.1 says that A_η is never isomorphic to Putz's octic field L₈ = ℚ[x]/(h), where h(x) = x⁸ + 4x⁷ − 28x⁶ − 168x⁵ − 140x⁴ + 560x³ + 840x² − 480x − 940. Theorem 1.2 combines this with Putz's Theorem 4.33, which says that A_η is always isomorphic to L₈, to show that x² + y⁵ = z⁷, and equivalently x² + y⁷ = z⁵ and x⁵ + y⁷ = z², have no solution in nonzero coprime integers. The Lean theorems take two hypotheses: Putz's Theorem 4.33 (for Theorem 1.2 only), and that the class group of the ring of integers of L₂₄ = L₈[t]/(ψ) has no element of order 5, which follows from the paper's proof that L₂₄ has class number 1, a computation that is not formalized. The proof follows the paper: a fifth-power descent over L₂₄, completed by fifth-power residue symbols at the primes 101, 131, 181, 251 and 311, with every computation checked by the Lean kernel.

records.name: BourgainStatement.manuscript_main
records.entry_name: Explicit uniformly bounded bases of homogeneous holomorphic polynomials in every dimension
records.doc: We construct uniformly bounded orthonormal bases for homogeneous holomorphic polynomials on complex unit spheres. Fix d >= 2 and N >= 0, and put m = d-1 and L = N+d-1. For each multi-index alpha = (alpha_1,...,alpha_d) of nonnegative integers with sum N, define s_b(alpha) = b + alpha_1 + ... + alpha_b, 1 <= b <= m, and the normalized monomial M_alpha(z) = sqrt((N+d-1)! / ((d-1)! alpha_1! ... alpha_d!)) z_1^alpha_1 ... z_d^alpha_d. Let F be the normalized Fourier matrix, with entries F_(t,s) = L^(-1/2) exp(2 pi i t s/L), for 1 <= t,s <= L. For each increasing m-element subset T = {t_1,...,t_m} of {1,...,L}, define P_T(z) = sum_(|alpha|=N) det[F_(t_a,s_b(alpha))] exp(2 pi i sqrt(2) sum_r alpha_r^2) M_alpha(z), where the determinant is over 1 <= a,b <= m. These polynomials form an orthonormal basis with respect to surface measure of total mass one on the complex unit sphere. Their absolute values on the closed unit ball are bounded by a constant depending only on d, independently of N and T. The construction and proof are formalized in Lean.

records.name: DensityStronger.density_bound
records.entry_name: A zero-density estimate with exponent 3(1−σ)/(2σ) for the Riemann zeta function
records.doc: For every real sigma>3/4 and epsilon>0 there exists C>0 such that for all real T>=2, all actual Riemann zeta zeros with Re(rho)>=sigma and |Im(rho)|<=T, counted with analytic multiplicity, number at most C*T^(3*(1-sigma)/(2*sigma)+epsilon). The proof combines separately proved Type I Dirichlet-polynomial large-values and critical-line twelfth-moment bounds. The companion moment is the literal integral on [0,3T] bounded by K*T^(2+epsilon), eventually in T. No analytic premise remains in the final endpoints. Compared with Tao–Trudgian–Yang Table 2 and Kerr Theorem 6, the leading exponent improves for 3/4<sigma<23/29, agrees with the best located leading exponent on [23/29,7/8], and is weaker on (7/8,1). See docs/LITERATURE.md for scope and citations.

records.name: Erdos809Palomar.main_result
records.entry_name: Erdős Problem 809: an independent proof of the seven-cycle threshold
records.doc: For every fixed integer k >= 3, the minimum number of colors in an edge-coloring of an n-vertex simple graph with at least floor(n^2/4)+1 edges, in which every copy of C_(2k+1) is rainbow, is (1/8 + o(1))n^2. The minimum is attained. The development combines Asad Shahab's seven-cycle proof, using an exact rational five-vertex certificate, with a formalization of the Bucić-Chen-Ma argument for longer odd cycles.

records.name: PalomarPolyaNeumann.strict_neumann_polya
records.entry_name: Strict Neumann Polya inequality on simply connected planar domains
records.doc: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the strict Neumann Pólya inequality for bounded simply connected Lipschitz domains in the plane. The plane is identified with ℂ; the Neumann eigenvalues μ_0 ≤ μ_1 ≤ ... are defined by the Courant–Fischer min–max formula for the form ∫|∇u|² on H¹(Ω) (weak gradients in L²), indexed from 0 and repeated according to multiplicity, and N_N(E) = #{j ≥ 0 : μ_j < E}. The principal results are: for every bounded simply connected Lipschitz domain Ω and every integer j ≥ 1, |Ω| μ_j(Ω) < 4πj; and, equivalently, N_N(E) > |Ω| E / (4π) for every E > 0. The proof development (about 100,000 lines, namespace PolyaNeumann) also identifies the variational eigenvalues with the spectrum of the constructed self-adjoint Neumann operator, proves a quantitative smooth-domain estimate via boundary transport, Cayley/monodromy rank bounds and a Herglotz-wave reduction, and passes to Lipschitz domains by smooth approximation.

records.name: Whitehead.TheoremA
records.entry_name: Finite Chains of Two-Complexes and Acyclic Covers
records.doc: Whitehead's asphericity problem would have a negative answer if a non-aspherical two-complex began an infinite chain whose inclusions induce zero maps on second homotopy groups. This Lean formalization proves the article's main finite-length characterization: a connected two-complex K begins such chains of every finite length if and only if K has a connected acyclic regular cover. It also formalizes the finite acyclic enhancement.

records.name: GenusSix.brill_noether_existence_through_six
records.entry_name: Brill--Noether existence and rank for graphs through genus six
records.doc: This repository proves Baker's Brill--Noether existence conjecture for finite graphs of genus at most six.  The conjecture states that if G is a finite connected loopless multigraph, with genus defined to be g = E-V+1, then for all nonnegative integers d, r, there exists a configuration of d chips on G with Baker--Norine rank at least r provided that the Brill--Noether number rho = g - (r+1)(g-d+r) is nonnegative.  To the author's knowledge, this is a new result, extending a result of Atanasov and Ranganathan from genus five to six.  Two generalizations are also included.  First, in genus at most six, the Brill--Noether rank, in the sense of Lim--Payne--Potashnik, is at least the expected dimension of the Brill--Noether locus, when d is at most g+r. This is a combinatorial analog of the classical lower bound on the dimension of Brill--Noether loci, usually established on algebraic curves using intersection theory.  Second, the Brill--Noether existence conjecture for graphs with one marked vertex, as stated by Pflueger--Solomon, holds in genus up to five.  The proof synthesizes recent work of Christ--Ma and Draisma--Vargas. The work of Christ--Ma predicts the subdivision required to obtain special divisors on graphs, using enumerative geometry. The work of Draisma--Vargas provides a combinatorial construction to realize these special divisors.  The novel contribution in this repository is a descent argument, producing special divisors on the original graph from special divisors on an odd subdivision.  This work has not yet been written up for publication; the present repository is the first announcement of it.

records.name: Complexity.pcp_gap
records.entry_name: MaxSNP-completeness and APX-completeness of MAX-3-SAT and 3-OCCURRENCE MAX-3-SAT (the PCP theorem and hardness of approximation) in Lean 4
records.doc:
A Lean 4 proof of the PCP theorem and of its consequences for approximation, for an explicit single-tape Turing machine model. The compared theorems are: the PCP theorem in gap form, that for a fixed fraction num/den > 0 every NP language reduces in polynomial time to 3-SAT so that members give satisfiable formulas and non-members give formulas of which every assignment leaves at least that fraction of the clauses unsatisfied (Complexity.pcp_gap); the PCP theorem in verifier form, NP = PCP(O(log n), O(1)) (Complexity.pcp_theorem); that the problems of the syntactic class MaxSNP0 are in NPO (Complexity.npo_maxSNP0); that MaxSNP-hard problems have no polynomial-time approximation scheme unless P = NP (Complexity.maxSNPHard_not_hasPTAS), even when a separate algorithm is allowed for each precision (Complexity.maxSNPHard_no_ptas); that MAX-3-SAT and 3-OCCURRENCE MAX-3-SAT are MaxSNP-complete (Complexity.max3SAT_maxSNPComplete, Complexity.max3SAT3_maxSNPComplete); and that both are APX-complete (Complexity.max3SAT_apxComplete, Complexity.max3SAT3_apxComplete). The statement, Challenge.lean, imports only Lean core and defines everything it uses: the machine model, P, NP and polynomial-time functions; probabilistically checkable proofs and gap reductions; optimization problems, approximation algorithms and schemes; NPO; L-reductions, the syntactic class MaxSNP0 of Papadimitriou and Yannakakis (structures of fixed input and solution signatures on a finite universe, and a well-formed quantifier-free formula) and the class MaxSNP of NPO problems L-reducible to it; APX and PTAS-reductions in the sense of Crescenzi and Trevisan; and the two problems.
The gap form of the PCP theorem is proved by Dinur's gap amplification: the 3-CNF gap map, its soundness and its implementation as a polynomial-time multi-stack Turing machine are taken from the Lean formalization of the Unique Games theorem in the OpenAI mathematics repository (194 files, adapted to the Lean module system and to Lean v4.35.0-rc2), and composed with the Cook-Levin reduction of the Palomar entry PALOMAR-2026-10-02-000013 (whose library is included). A simulation theorem carries polynomial time from Mathlib's multi-stack machines to the single-tape model. The verifier form samples clauses of the gap formula with O(log n) random bits. MaxSNP-hard problems have no approximation scheme because MAX-3-SAT L-reduces to them and an approximation scheme for MAX-3-SAT would decide the gap. MAX-3-SAT is put in MaxSNP0 by an explicit quantifier-free formula, and every MaxSNP0 problem L-reduces to it by the Papadimitriou-Yannakakis clause construction (one clause per falsifying pattern of atoms, split into 3-clauses with fresh variables, with an averaging bound for the constant; assignments are mapped back to structures of the solution signature). The MaxSNP0 problems are in NPO by an explicit polynomial-time parser and feasibility check, and a size bound for structures of a fixed signature. 3-OCCURRENCE MAX-3-SAT is reached in two L-reductions: copies of each variable linked along an explicit constant-degree expander (from the same OpenAI development), and then a torus gadget of implications. APX-hardness under PTAS-reductions needs a witness-recovering PCP theorem, which is proved here: an explicit deterministic decoder, shown polynomial-time, turns every assignment of the gap formula that satisfies more than the fraction 1 - num/den of its clauses into an assignment of the original formula and then into an NP certificate. With it every APX problem reduces to MAX-3-SAT by a threshold construction. Membership in APX uses a 2-approximation. The proof uses only the axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.

records.name: InverseZeroSum.Candidate3.frozenClassification
records.entry_name: Inverse classification for innerly joint short zero-sum subsequences in C3^3
records.doc: We formalize an exact positional inverse classification in the elementary abelian group C3^3. For a sequence of 24 nonzero elements, every pair of nonempty zero-sum subsequences of length at most three has intersection sum zero if and only if the original sequence, up to a permutation of all 24 positions, consists of three copies of eight distinct elements having no short nonempty zero sum. The two implications, including the positional intersection condition, are proved in Lean. The existing literature review did not locate the exact inverse classification, but historical novelty, priority and significance are not certified.

records.name: MIPRE.Palomar.halting_reduces_to_value
records.entry_name: MIP* = RE
records.doc: A Lean 4 formalization of MIP* = RE (Ji, Natarajan, Vidick, Wright and Yuen): the class of languages decidable by a classical polynomial-time verifier interacting with two provers who share entanglement, with completeness 1 and soundness 1/2, is exactly the class of recursively enumerable languages. The development also contains the halting reduction behind it (a computable map from Turing machines to nonlocal games whose synchronous and quantum values are 1 if the machine halts and at most 1/2 otherwise) and its corollaries that the synchronous and the quantum value of a game are uncomputable. It builds on three other formalizations: the soundness of the classical low individual degree test (MIPStarRE, by Sirui Lu, Ruixuan Deng and Zhengfeng Ji, registered as PALOMAR-2026-08-18-000001), imported as a pinned Lake dependency, and the parallel repetition theorem for entangled strategies (ten-proofs, OpenAI) and the direct parallel repetition theorem for commuting-operator strategies (commuting-repetition), which are vendored with their provenance recorded. Palomar/Challenge.lean states the four compared theorems on top of Mathlib alone, in a tree-program model of polynomial time that the fidelity section describes; Palomar/Solution.lean proves them from the library.

The development also contains the halting reduction behind it (a computable map from Turing machines to nonlocal games whose synchronous and quantum values are 1 if the machine halts and at most 1/2 otherwise) and its corollaries that the synchronous and the quantum value of a game are uncomputable. It builds on three other formalizations: the soundness of the classical low individual degree test (MIPStarRE, by Sirui Lu, Ruixuan Deng and Zhengfeng Ji, registered as PALOMAR-2026-08-18-000001), imported as a pinned Lake dependency, and the parallel repetition theorem for entangled strategies (ten-proofs, OpenAI) and the direct parallel repetition theorem for commuting-operator strategies (commuting-repetition), which are vendored with their provenance recorded. Palomar/Challenge.lean states the four compared theorems on top of Mathlib alone, in a tree-program model of polynomial time that the fidelity section describes; Palomar/Solution.lean proves them from the library.

records.name: PalomarAT.replicaSymmetry
records.entry_name: Replica symmetry up to the de Almeida–Thouless line in the Sherrington–Kirkpatrick model
records.doc: A Lean formalization of the positive-field Sherrington–Kirkpatrick results in Patrick Lopatto's arXiv:2604.11921v2. The selected registry claims are convergence of the expected finite-volume free energy to the concrete replica-symmetric Gaussian formula for beta > 0, h > 0, and AT parameter at most one, including equality; and an exact description of the positive-field AT boundary as a positive strictly increasing smooth graph on beta > 1, tending to zero at beta = 1 from the right, together with (1,0). The repository also contains the numbered PDE, stochastic-process, moment, and variational results documented in COVERAGE.md and results.json.

records.name: HormanderChallenge.hormander_hypoellipticity
records.entry_name: Hörmander's hypoellipticity theorem and the Rothschild–Stein theory
records.doc: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the regularity theory of Hörmander operators: second-order operators built from smooth vector fields X_1, ..., X_q (and possibly a drift X_0) whose iterated commutators span the tangent space at every point. It proves Hörmander's 1967 theorem that such operators are hypoelliptic: every locally integrable weak solution of X_0 u + sum X_i^2 u + c u = g with smooth data is smooth. It then develops the Rothschild–Stein theory (Acta Math. 1976), following Bramanti and Brandolini's "Hörmander Operators" (2023): lifting and approximation of the fields by the generators of a homogeneous group; the homogeneous fundamental solution and singular-integral estimates on homogeneous groups; and the sharp interior estimates, by which a distributional solution of sum X_i^2 T = f with f in W^{k,p}_X or C^{k,alpha}_X is a function in W^{k+2,p}_X or C^{k+2,alpha}_X, for every k >= 0, and at k = 0 with a drift. The formalization also proves the formal Baker–Campbell–Hausdorff theorem, Chow–Rashevskii connectivity, and the Nagel–Stein–Wainger theorems on control balls (ball-box, volume and doubling, comparison of distances), uniformly over compact sets.

records.name: EndotacticSubmission.uniform_permanence
records.entry_name: Uniform permanence of endotactic reaction networks with measurable rates
records.doc: Uniform permanence is established for finite endotactic reaction networks with arbitrary real complexes and measurable rate coefficients bounded above and away from zero almost everywhere. Each positive stoichiometric compatibility class contains a compact convex forward-invariant absorbing set, with entry times uniform over compact sets of initial conditions and all rate histories within a fixed rate box. Global positive Carathéodory solutions exist and are unique, and an exponential continuous-dependence estimate holds for initial data under a common rate history on a compact positive region. The result resolves the Endotactic Permanence Conjecture stated as Conjecture 1.3 by Johnston, Pantea and Donnell (https://arxiv.org/abs/1412.4662), using an ordinary-endotactic drift estimate together with the finite affine barrier construction from OpenAI’s work on weakly reversible networks.

records.name: PlanarMidpoint.planar_dual_midpoint_rigidity
records.entry_name: Planar Euclidean midpoint rigidity
records.doc: A complete Lean proof of the dimension-two case of Nielsen–Okamura Conjecture 9.1. On any connected open planar Euclidean domain, complementarity of the actual canonical local affine-parameter midpoints of a smooth pair of dual torsion-free connections forces the symmetric cubic tensor to be constant. The proof constructs and identifies the short geodesic germs and derives the fourth-order obstruction, including the exceptional rank-deficient tensors. A second theorem needs only everywhere Frechet differentiability and vanishing of that obstruction; five fixed direction tests at every point suffice. Dimensions above two are outside the claim.

records.name: PalomarFRSB.fullRSB
records.entry_name: Full replica symmetry breaking in the Sherrington–Kirkpatrick model
records.doc: Lean formalization of Patrick Lopatto's zero-field Sherrington–Kirkpatrick results. The selected claims are full interval support, a nonnegative smooth density with a terminal atom for every inverse temperature beta > 1, and quantitative inequalities for that actual atom. The independent Challenge defines the Parisi functional through concrete bounded-gradient weak PDE solutions, with terminal log cosh and coefficient beta squared divided by two. Solution identifies that definition with the constructed Parisi potential. The repository retains the supporting PDE, diffusion, covariance, minimizer, and numbered-result development described in COVERAGE.md and results.json.

records.name: NearlyMinimax.Submission.paper_main
records.entry_name: Nearly minimax variance estimation under rough random design
records.doc: Minimax root-mean-square bounds for estimating a constant conditional variance from independent random-design regression observations. The design density has fixed positive lower and upper bounds but no smoothness; covariate-dependent errors have uniformly bounded conditional fourth moments. For 1 < s < d/4, the proved bracket identifies the polynomial exponent 2(s+1)/(d+4) and the common explicit stretched-exponential factor, with a remaining logarithmic gap. It also proves the exponent corollary, the exact low-smoothness rate, and the parametric regime.

records.name: KineticAleksandrovChallenge.kinetic_aleksandrov_timeVelocity
records.entry_name: Kinetic Aleksandrov estimates
records.doc: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalisation of Aleksandrov maximum principles for kinetic equations d_t u + v.grad_x u - A : D_v^2 u = f in non-divergence form, with measurable, uniformly elliptic diffusion acting only in the velocity. For coefficients A(t,v) the estimate holds for every source exponent p > 2d+1; for autonomous coefficients a(x,v) in one space dimension for every p above a threshold 1 + beta_*(Lambda/lambda) < 4, where no exponent below 4 works uniformly in the ellipticity ratio; and for general measurable coefficients A(t,x,v) for every p >= 1 + 128 d^2 (Lambda/lambda)^2 / 3. In each case the estimate implies interior Hölder continuity of solutions; for coefficients A(t,x,v) this is the kinetic Krylov–Safonov theorem. The library also proves the parabolic Aleksandrov estimate of Krylov, the parabolic Harnack inequality of Krylov and Safonov, the terminal solution operators of the kinetic equation, and classical Dirichlet solvability on ellipsoidal cylinders. Hörmander's hypoellipticity theorem is taken from the formalisation hoermander-rothschild-stein.

records.name: RoughRegimeSubmission.mainUpper
records.entry_name: Nearly Minimax Rates for Functional Estimation Under Rough Random Design
records.doc: A Lean development of upper and local lower minimax bounds for nonlinear functionals of conditional means under bounded, rough random design. The generic theorem covers the root-n regime and the subcritical regime with its density-dependent stretched-exponential correction, logarithmic upper and lower factors, and a one-quarter minimax probability lower bound. The substantive development also contains projection, polynomial-estimator, Poisson reduction, lattice-prior, application, and causal-identification results. The selected Comparator surface is the generic theorem's two parts. The remaining logarithmic gap is unresolved.

records.name: CoarseDeGiorgiAudit.Harnack.harnack
records.entry_name: De Giorgi–Nash–Moser theory under coarse ellipticity
records.doc: A Lean 4 formalization of the paper "Coarse ellipticity and De Giorgi–Nash–Moser theory in the optimal range" by S. Armstrong, B. Avelin, T. Kuusi and A. Turpeinen (arXiv:2610.11879). The paper extends the theory of De Giorgi–Nash–Moser to elliptic equations with symmetric coefficients a(x) which are possibly degenerate and unbounded but satisfy a coarse ellipticity condition: spatial moments of coarse-grained matrices, suitably discounted and summed across scales, are finite. Under this condition it proves local upper bounds for weak subsolutions, a weak Harnack inequality for nonnegative supersolutions, and a Harnack inequality for nonnegative solutions. The condition holds if a ∈ W^{-α,p} ∩ L^1, a^{-1} ∈ W^{-β,q} ∩ L^1 and (α+β)/2 + ((d-1)/2)(1/p + 1/q) < 1, for some α, β ≥ 0 and 1 < p, q < ∞. This range is sharp, including its boundary, in every dimension d ≥ 3: for α = β = 0, where it corresponds to the results of Bella and Schäffner, and for the corresponding Besov-type quasi-norms of negative order when α, β > 0. The formalization covers these results, together with the optimality of the powers of the coarse ellipticity ratio in the local bounds and of the range of exponents in the weak Harnack inequality. The statements are for dimension d ≥ 3 and are formulated on the unit cube; the limiting cases p = ∞ or q = ∞ are not formalized. CORRESPONDENCE.md gives the status of every numbered statement of the paper. Built on Mathlib and the CoarseGraining library, using only Lean's standard axioms.

records.name: Challenge.audit_sesc_open_dense
records.entry_name: Exponential separation of analytic self-conformal sets on the real line: Lean formalisation
records.doc: Lean 4 formalisation of exponential separation for analytic iterated function systems on the real line. Strong exponential separation holds on an open and dense subset in the C2 topology and follows from an explicit criterion involving dual projections. The development characterises conjugacy to self-similar systems and proves dimension consequences conditional on cited results of Rapaport and Bowen, including a drop in the L^q dimensions of the natural measure of a concrete three-map example.

records.name: SpernerCapacity.T7_isTournament
records.entry_name: A 7-vertex tournament whose Sperner capacity exceeds the order of its largest transitive subtournament: T₇, induced by the Paley tournament on 23 vertices on 0, 1, 2, 3, 9, 14, 18, has t = 4 and √18 ≤ C ≤ 5; every tournament on at most six vertices has C = t, so seven is the least order
records.doc: A Lean 4 development on the capacity of digraphs in the sense of Alon (1998): w(R^n) is the largest set of words of length n such that every ordered pair of distinct words has a coordinate carrying an arc from the first to the second, and C(R) is the supremum of w(R^n)^(1/n), which equals the limit; for a tournament T, t(T) is the order of its largest transitive subtournament and t(T) ≤ C(T). Conjecture 1.1 of Alon's paper, attributed to Körner and Simonyi, asserts C(T) = t(T) for every tournament; Alon disproved it with a random construction and with the Paley tournament on 67 vertices, and asked for the smallest tournament on which the equality fails. Let T7 be the subtournament of the Paley tournament on 23 vertices (x → y iff y − x is a nonzero square mod 23) induced on 0, 1, 2, 3, 9, 14, 18. Proved here: T7 is a tournament with t(T7) = 4; eighteen listed points of T7 × T7 form a transitive clique of its second Sperner power; hence, by the lift lemma (N injective points of the k-th power, each earlier one dominating each later one in some coordinate, give for every m a clique of the km-th power of size at least N^m / ((N − 1)m + 1), by words of fixed index sum), some Sperner power of T7 has a clique larger than 4^n, √18 ≤ C(T7), and t(T7) < C(T7); C(T7) ≤ 5, by an explicit rank-5 factorization over GF(2) of a matrix with nonzero diagonal and zeros on the arcs, through the rank bound (a clique of the n-th power indexes a nonsingular diagonal submatrix of the n-th Kronecker power, which factors through F^(r^n)); the general statements N^(1/k) ≤ C(R), t(R) ≤ C(R), C(R) ≤ r for any such factorization, and C(R) ≤ |V|; and, for the Paley tournament on 23 vertices, t = 5 and √29 ≤ C from a 29-point transitive clique of its second Sperner power; and every tournament on at most six vertices satisfies C(T) = t(T) (for each of the 1, 1, 1, 2, 4, 12, 56 isomorphism classes on 0 to 6 vertices, a representative with a rank-t factorization over GF(2) and a transitive t-chain, and a kernel check, by a bitset over all orientations, that every labelled tournament on at most six vertices is a relabelling of a representative), so a tournament with t < C has at least seven vertices and seven is the least order of a counterexample. The capacity is formalized in its supremum form. On paper, in the research note of the repository, with standard-library certificates: the square value 18 is exact; on seven vertices 455 of the 456 isomorphism classes have a rank-t matrix over GF(2) and the exception is T7, which is therefore the unique smallest counterexample up to isomorphism; every proper subtournament of T7 satisfies the equality; and the Paley tournament on 7 vertices has C = 3. The smallest example previously exhibited has 67 vertices (examples on 27 and 26 vertices follow from Alon's argument over GF(27) with a published value of t). Nothing in Lean is claimed about tournaments on seven or more vertices other than T7 and the Paley tournament on 23 vertices.

records.name: SKMeanBias.thermodynamic_limit
records.entry_name: Finite-size mean bias of the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick free energy
records.doc: Formalization of a fixed-temperature N^(-7/10) bound for the finite-size mean bias of the zero-field Sherrington-Kirkpatrick model with independent standard Gaussian couplings and the unnormalized partition function. For every beta > 1, a positive constant depending on beta bounds the nonnegative pressure gap for every integer N >= 2. The selected results also establish the thermodynamic limit for beta > 0, the corresponding free-energy-density and expected log-partition corrections, a positive exponent saving over 2/3, and a full-sequence little-o improvement. The independently readable interface defines the limiting pressure by a thermodynamic limit; Solution identifies it with the all-probability-profile Parisi variational value.

The selected results also establish the thermodynamic limit for beta > 0, the corresponding free-energy-density and expected log-partition corrections, a positive exponent saving over 2/3, and a full-sequence little-o improvement. The independently readable interface defines the limiting pressure by a thermodynamic limit; Solution identifies it with the all-probability-profile Parisi variational value.

records.name: ComparatorChecks.omega_bound
records.entry_name: Matrix multiplication: omega at most 9/4 over every ring
records.doc: An integral extension of OpenAI's matrix multiplication exponent bound and its previous all-fields extension. The formalization proves that the exact integer coefficient tensor-rank exponent is at most 9/4, yielding division-free arithmetic programs over every associative unital ring, including noncommutative rings. For every positive epsilon, one constant bounds the operation count at all positive matrix sizes by C*n^(9/4+epsilon). The arithmetic model is preserved apart from Field-to-Ring assumptions. The extension uses a primitive tensor spectrum, coefficient extraction, fixed finite-free descent, and coprime patching of Fourier and interpolation constructions. It does not improve the numerical exponent or assert an endpoint O(n^(9/4)) algorithm, efficient uniform generation, or bit complexity.

records.name: DOZZChallenge.dozz_formula
records.entry_name: Integrability of Liouville theory: the Kupiainen–Rhodes–Vargas proof of the DOZZ formula
records.doc: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the theorem of A. Kupiainen, R. Rhodes and V. Vargas (Annals of Mathematics, 2020) that the three-point structure constants of Liouville conformal field theory on the Riemann sphere are given by the DOZZ formula of Dorn–Otto and Zamolodchikov–Zamolodchikov. The structure constants are defined probabilistically: for 0 < gamma < 2, cosmological constant mu > 0 and charges satisfying the extended Seiberg bounds, C_gamma(alpha_1, alpha_2, alpha_3) = 2 mu^(-s) gamma^(-1) Gamma(s) E[rho^(-s)], where rho integrates explicit power weights against the Gaussian multiplicative chaos of the Gaussian free field pinned on the equator. The formalization proves C_gamma = C_gamma^DOZZ, expressed through the Zamolodchikov function Upsilon_{gamma/2}, at every point of the domain where Gamma(s) is finite, and at every point including the poles for the unit-volume constant; and it proves that the probabilistic reflection coefficient, built from Brownian motion conditioned to stay negative and lateral chaos, equals R^DOZZ (Theorem 3.5). The theorems hold for every model of the field and chaos, and models are constructed. All prerequisites are proved: the construction, uniqueness and moment theory of Gaussian multiplicative chaos and the extended Seiberg bounds (David, Kupiainen, Rhodes and Vargas, 2016); the BPZ equations for degenerate four-point functions and the classification of their real single-valued solutions by the Gauss hypergeometric function (Kupiainen, Rhodes and Vargas, 2019); analytic continuation of correlation functions, tail estimates for multiplicative chaos, fusion asymptotics, the shift equations and the quotient argument. Errata found in the three papers, and the places where the Lean statements differ from them, are recorded in docs/ERRATA-AND-DEVIATIONS.md.

records.name: SubdiffusiveProcessAudit.ProcessConvergence.theoremA
records.entry_name: Anomalous scaling limit of a Brownian particle in a log-correlated potential
records.doc: A Lean 4 formalization of the paper "Anomalous scaling limit of a Brownian particle in a log-correlated potential" by Armstrong, Bou-Rabee and Kuusi: the subdiffusive scaling limit of a Brownian particle whose drift is the gradient of a log-correlated random potential (Theorem A, in its introduction form and in its precise quenched form), quantitative homogenization of the Dirichlet problem uniformly in the infrared cutoff (Theorem B), and large-scale Hölder regularity with a Liouville theorem (Theorem C), together with the supporting coarse-graining, elliptic-regularity and Markov-process theory. The theorems hold for every random environment satisfying the paper's standing assumptions (a GMCModel). The development builds on Mathlib and on the public CoarseGraining and MarkovProcess libraries. The three headline theorems are independently checked by the comparator pairs under SubdiffusiveProcessAudit/.

records.name: GuthMaynardStatement.full_curve
records.entry_name: Zero-density estimates from an improved large-values bound
records.doc:
Let N(σ,T) count the nontrivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function with real part at least σ and imaginary part of absolute value at most T, counted with multiplicity. For every fixed σ ∈ [1/2,1] and every ε > 0, we prove N(σ,T) ≤ Cσ,ε T^(A(σ)(1−σ)+ε) for all T ≥ 2, where

| σ interval | A(σ) |
| --- | --- |
| [1/2,9/13] | 3/(2−σ) |
| (9/13,5/7] | 18/(7σ+3) |
| (5/7,3/4] | 9/4 |
| (3/4,1] | 3/(2σ) |

The maximum of this coefficient bound is 39/17, improving the coefficient 30/13 in the Guth–Maynard bound. We also prove the separate estimate N(σ,T) ≤ Cε T^((39/17)(1−σ)+ε) for every ε > 0, simultaneously for σ ∈ [1/2,1] and T ≥ 2, with a constant independent of σ and T. The improved large-values estimate and its zero-density consequences are formalized in Lean.

records.name: SharedResourceSubmission.realization_core
records.entry_name: Realizations and dynamics of shared-resource mass-action systems
records.doc: Ordinary mass-action realizations are characterized for a finite family of two-species modules coupled through a shared resource and buffer. Every positive parameter vector admits a strongly connected realization of the same polynomial field. A complex-balanced realization at a prescribed positive state exists exactly when the state is stationary and two explicit local flux inequalities hold, even when arbitrary finite auxiliary complexes on the same species are allowed. An explicit endpoint sign test determines the untransported heterogeneous parameter locus, and the state criterion extends to directed transfers of both private species. A homogeneous specialization has the sharp sharing threshold v <= n/8, including equality. Global positive solutions and permanence uniform over compact sets of initial conditions are established. For d >= 1, the positive equilibrium is unique and is locally exponentially stable in the homogeneous family. Complex-balanced realizations yield global convergence, including with transport, and local exponential stability is established for the transported complex-balanced family. An exact example at d = 1/10 has three positive equilibria, two locally exponentially stable and one unstable.

records.doc: Ordinary mass-action realizations are characterized for a finite family of two-species modules coupled through a shared resource and buffer. Every positive parameter vector admits a strongly connected realization of the same polynomial field. A complex-balanced realization at a prescribed positive state exists exactly when the state is stationary and two explicit local flux inequalities hold, even when arbitrary finite auxiliary complexes on the same species are allowed. An explicit endpoint sign test determines the untransported heterogeneous parameter locus, and the state criterion extends to directed transfers of both private species. A homogeneous specialization has the sharp sharing threshold v <= n/8, including equality. Global positive solutions and permanence uniform over compact sets of initial conditions are established. For d >= 1, the positive equilibrium is unique and is locally exponentially stable in the homogeneous family. Complex-balanced realizations yield global convergence, including with transport, and local exponential stability is established for the transported complex-balanced family. An exact example at d = 1/10 has three positive equilibria, two locally exponentially stable and one unstable.

records.name: Erdos993.erdos_993_forest
records.entry_name: Unimodality of the independence sequence of a finite forest (Erdős Problem 993)
records.doc: A Lean 4 and Mathlib formalization of the theorem that the independence sequence of every finite forest is unimodal: the numbers of independent sets with 0, 1, 2, ... vertices weakly increase up to some index and weakly decrease after it. This is the statement listed as Erdős Problem 993; later sources attribute the question to a 1987 paper of Alavi, Malde, Schwenk and Erdős. The first claimed proof for all finite forests is by T. Zhang and W. Li (self-archived preprints, September 2026). This repository formalizes a second proof, by W. Li, K. Vallier and T. Zhang: it adapts the public arXiv:2610.07943v1 and follows version 2.15 of that manuscript, deposited with restricted access and under revision. The Lean proof is computer-assisted and in two parts (at most 24 vertices; at least 25). About 13,700 finite computations are evaluated by the Lean kernel, without native_decide, on the three standard axioms. AI systems produced and reviewed all of the Lean; no human has read the Lean proofs. No manuscript cited is peer reviewed. No priority and no first formalization is claimed.

records.name: Michael.IsBiquotientMap.piMap
records.entry_name: Michael's biquotient-map product and characterization theorems
records.doc: Formalization of Michael (1968), Theorems 1.2 and 1.3: arbitrary indexed products of biquotient continuous surjections are biquotient, without separation assumptions; for a Hausdorff target, biquotience is equivalent to quotientness of the product with every identity map and to the same property for paracompact test spaces. The cover definition, filter and ultrafilter bridges, and an actual Hausdorff paracompact counterexample topology on the underlying target set are proved. Reverse tests use the target universe; the forward implication is separately universe-polymorphic.

records.name: EgyptianPalomar.explicit_counterexample
records.entry_name: An explicit computable transcendental counterexample for Erdős Problem #206
records.doc: A Lean formalization of a deterministic rational nested-interval construction defining a particular transcendental real x in (1/4,1/3). For this x, no strictly increasing infinite sequence of positive integer denominators is optimal among all distinct-denominator strict Egyptian underapproximations at every order from any finite starting order onward. The formalization includes the fully specified terminating construction, all prefix and polynomial enumerations, a total executable rational approximation function, and the error bound |x-q_n| <= 2^(-n-1) for every n >= 0. It also proves attainment of the best finite underapproximation values. The independent Palomar statement quantifies directly over all sequences and all competing positive increasing lists. This is a specific effective example; the measure-zero and prior existence results are not claimed as new.

records.name: E607.main_result
records.entry_name: Erdos607
records.doc: Machine-checked upper bound on Erdős problem 607. For n ≥ 2 let F(n) be the number of distinct multiplicity sets A(P) that can arise from a collection P of n points of the plane, where A(P) is the set of block sizes (point counts) of the lines determined by P. The proof shows that the lines of P form a pairwise-balanced design on the n points (every pair of points lies on exactly one line, and each line contains at least two points), so A(P) is exactly the set of block sizes of such a PBD. Hence F(n) is bounded by the number of PBD profile sets on n points, and the Colbourn–Phelps–Rödl (1984) Theorem 2.4 bound exp(c·√n) on that quantity gives F(n) ≤ exp(c·√n) for every n ≥ 2. The bound is stated for n ≥ 2 — the range where the bound is meaningful (a single point determines no line) — so the hypothesis is non-vacuous. The CPR-1984 PBD bound is a published theorem and is taken as the hypothesis hCPR; it is cited, not re-proved here. Together with the Szemerédi–Trotter (1983) lattice-grid lower bound F(n) ≥ exp(c'·√n) (also cited, not re-proved), the order of growth is F(n) = exp(Θ(√n)). This repository contains zero axioms and zero sorry in the proof development (the only sorry is the deliberate statement surface in Challenge.lean).

records.name: Erdos261.Palomar.borwein_loring
records.entry_name: Erdős 261: dyadic weighted representations n / 2^n = ∑ a_k / 2^(a_k)
records.doc: A Lean 4 formalization of the solved parts, extremal bounds, and finite verification up to 10000 for Erdős problem 261 on representing n / 2^n as a finite sum ∑_{k=1}^t a_k / 2^(a_k) of distinct positive integers a_k. Proves the Borwein–Loring telescoping family n = 2^(m+1) - m - 2 (resolving Part (i) that infinitely many positive integers n admit such a representation), verifies every integer 1 ≤ n ≤ 10000 via a coalesced dyadic block certificate forest (Theorem 3.5 of Tengely, Ulas, and Zygadło 2020), constructs infinitely many rationals with at least 2^m distinct infinite representations for every m ∈ ℕ, and proves the Tengely–Ulas–Zygadło sharp extremal bound n ≤ 2^(t+1) - t - 2 and its equality uniqueness, first-term localization a_k ∈ [n+1, n+3], 2-adic last-gap divisibility 2^(a_{t+1} - a_t) ∣ a_{t+1}, the punctured-interval infinite family n_k = (2^(4k+2) + 1)/5 - 4k, and arbitrary-length splicing.

Proves the Borwein–Loring telescoping family n = 2^(m+1) - m - 2 (resolving Part (i) that infinitely many positive integers n admit such a representation), verifies every integer 1 ≤ n ≤ 10000 via a coalesced dyadic block certificate forest (Theorem 3.5 of Tengely, Ulas, and Zygadło 2020), constructs infinitely many rationals with at least 2^m distinct infinite representations for every m ∈ ℕ, and proves the Tengely–Ulas–Zygadło sharp extremal bound n ≤ 2^(t+1) - t - 2 and its equality uniqueness, first-term localization a_k ∈ [n+1, n+3], 2-adic last-gap divisibility 2^(a_{t+1} - a_t) ∣ a_{t+1}, the punctured-interval infinite family n_k = (2^(4k+2) + 1)/5 - 4k, and arbitrary-length splicing.

records.name: ArbitraryRSB.arbitrary_finite_depth_open_set
records.entry_name: Replica symmetry breaking at arbitrary depth
records.doc: A Lean formalization of open phases with every prescribed finite replica symmetry breaking depth in mixed even-spin Ising models at zero external field and positive temperature. The first selected result constructs strictly increasing even degrees beginning at four and a nonempty open set of positive effective covariance coefficients, with an optimizing probability measure having exactly k+1 support points. The independent statement uses concrete Gaussian Cole–Hopf recursions and comparison against all finite schemes at every competing depth. The substantive development constructs minimizers over all probability measures and includes the revised quadratic-inclusive universal transition, exact phase geometry and asymptotics, atomic Hessian, entropy, and analytic comparison results.

records.name: FrobergPaper.main_result
records.entry_name: Fröberg's conjecture through degree 2d in sufficiently many variables
records.doc: For every positive generating degree d, there is a variable threshold depending only on d such that, over every infinite field and for every number of general degree-d generators, the quotient polynomial ring has Fröberg's predicted Hilbert function through degree 2d. The threshold is independent of both the field and the number of generators. The prediction uses positive truncation at the first nonpositive coefficient of (1-t^d)^r/(1-t)^n. The development includes a direct construction for d at least three and a separate quadratic argument in arbitrary characteristic.

records.name: ChiralGap.robustMinimum_spec
records.entry_name: Exact robust gaps in finite open chiral chains
records.doc: Exact worst squared spectral gaps for finite open chiral chains with inhomogeneous strong-bond lower bounds and weak-bond ratio intervals. The scalar optimum is the minimum over the ordered one-switch endpoint configurations, with a two-certificate reduction when cuts are allowed. Strictly positive weak lower bounds give a complete point-or-edge classification of scalar minimizers and an exact aligned-channel equality criterion for arbitrary complex matrix disorder. The sharp channel bound includes the finite chiral Hamiltonian spectral bridge.

records.name: ReverseRateLimits.general_quantitative_root
records.entry_name: Quantitative permanence and recovery with vanishing reverse rates
records.doc: Quantitative permanence and recovery bounds are established for mass-action systems with vanishing reverse rates. For a finite weakly reversible network with rates proportional to powers of epsilon, eventual concentration bounds depend on the spread of the rate exponents, with geometric constants chosen before the individual rates. For an explicit three-species network, a prepared region admits global positive solutions with three distinct concentration scales. Every prepared solution reaches and remains in a smaller target by time (31/10)/(p^2 h^7), while an explicit prepared solution cannot enter before 400/(1313 p^2 h^7). Inventory inequalities give additional necessary restoration and depletion times from arbitrary positive initial states. A continuous reverse-exponent family retains arbitrary admitted prefactors and yields matching worst-case prepared recovery orders, together with exact common-clock transport, preparation identities and cumulative reverse-reaction bounds. Abstract constant-capacity and open-range state-dependent inventory comparisons are included without assuming monotone inventories.

records.name: Palomar824.main_result
records.entry_name: Erdős Problem #824 under a smooth shifted-prime hypothesis
records.doc: A Lean formalization of the conditional lower bound for the number h(x) of pairs of coprime positive integers a < b < x with equal sums of divisors. Assuming Hypothesis A⁺, which supplies sufficiently many primes p with smooth p+1, h(x) exceeds x^(2-ε) for every ε > 0 and all sufficiently large natural x. The argument adapts Pollack and Pomerance's finite counting method. A⁺ itself, the squarefree strengthening, and the accompanying paper's argument relying on the WD preprint are not formalized here.

records.name: Erdos252.erdos_252
records.entry_name: Erdős 252: irrationality of the factorial divisor-sum series
records.doc: For every natural number k, the series whose nth term is the sum of the kth powers of the positive divisors of n, divided by n factorial, is irrational. This gives the positive-exponent statement of Erdős problem 252 and also includes exponent zero. The proof combines factorial-tail integrality, a finite coprime dilation grid with exact finite-difference cancellation, and incompatible progression means obtained by a fresh-prime refinement. It has no prime-pattern conjecture or unproved number-theoretic hypothesis. The Lean development also proves convergence and the equivalence of its natural-index series with the series starting at one.

records.name: SphericalAging.PalomarCompleteTheorems.exists_complete_conclusions
records.entry_name: Aging in Spherical Spin Glass Dynamics
records.doc: Lean formalization of the spherical Gaussian spin-glass dynamics and its positive-semidefinite Cugliandolo--Kurchan limit, including the physical variational response, entropy and Fisher estimates, stationary translated clusters, general-spin selection and aging bounds, and stationary relaxation. Theorem 11.4 covers every integer p >= 3 and beta > 0. The cubic product inequality includes beta = beta_d; strictly positive Fisher-cost conclusions require beta > beta_d. The root Challenge retains the original complete-conclusions theorem with the five principal theorem groups and all-spin forward theorem, sharing CK, stationary-profile, dimension-subsequence, density and Fisher-majorant witnesses. The same file separately retains the original Proposition 5.7 statement for every CK solution, every late sequence and every raw translated cluster.

records.name: Dowker.normal_countablyParacompact_iff_normal_interval_product
records.entry_name: Dowker's countable paracompactness, product normality and strict insertion characterization
records.doc: Formalization of Dowker (1951), Theorem 4: normality plus ordinary countable paracompactness of an arbitrary topological space X is equivalent to normality of X times the closed unit interval, and to strict continuous insertion between arbitrary real upper and lower semicontinuous functions h<g. No T1 or Hausdorff assumption on X, boundedness or uniform gap is added. Companion compact metrizable product theorem (Lemma 3) and countable-cover/decreasing-closed-sequence equivalences (Theorem 2) are included.

records.name: Palomar.evenRank_hasFGPositiveCone
records.entry_name: Finitely generated positive cones in F_n × Z
records.doc: This Lean 4 formalization proves that, for every integer n at least two, the direct product of the free group of rank n with the infinite cyclic group has a positive cone generated by finitely many elements as a semigroup if and only if n is even. It formalizes Theorem 1.1 and Corollary 1.2 of Hang Lu Su's arXiv:2608.31103v1. The even-rank construction passes a positive cone through two finite-index subgroups. The converse derives the parity obstruction from finite circle domains and their endpoint actions. The required base-cone theorem and the supporting algebraic and dynamical arguments are proved within Lean.

records.name: Erdos1180.Palomar.erdos_1180
records.entry_name: Erdős 1180: representing residues as sums of modular inverses with small denominators
records.doc: A complete Lean 4 proof of Erdős problem 1180 and its quantitative variants on representing every residue modulo a prime p as a sum of at most C(ε) modular inverses n⁻¹ (mod p) with 1 ≤ n ≤ p^ε and gcd(n, p) = 1. Formalizing Glibichuk's 8-fold bilinear covering theorem via additive energy and Cauchy–Davenport together with an inductive asymmetric two-block prime-reciprocal construction, this development proves the affirmative existence theorem for all ε > 0 and all primes p, the discrete large-prime bound C_asymp(ε) ≤ 8(⌊1/ε⌋ + 1)² = (8 + o(1))ε⁻² (and ≤ 32ε⁻² uniformly on (0, 1]), the asymmetric staircase bounds C_asymp(ε) ≤ 8k(k + 1) whenever (2k + 1)ε > 2 and C_asymp(ε) ≤ 8k whenever (2k - 1)ε > k (giving C_asymp(ε) ≤ 16 for ε > 2/3 and ≤ 24 for ε > 3/5), and Shparlinski's O(ε⁻³) bound. It also proves the large-prime pigeonhole lower bound 1/ε ≤ ⌈1/ε⌉ ≤ C_asymp(ε), the small-prime exponential lower bound 2^(1/ε) ≤ 4 C(ε), the strict separation C_asymp(1/n) < C(1/n) for all n ≥ 15, and the disproof of the unthresholded all-primes optimality statement.
